tasks.title: Thyroid Medication Management and Follow-up Planning
tasks.subject: Abnormal thyroid function results
tasks.request: TSH 9.4 mIU/L (H) and free T4 0.8 ng/dL (L), collected 2024-05-30, for a patient on levothyroxine. Please review.

required.why: Under-replacement (TSH 9.4, free T4 low) with confirmed adherence, correct administration and no interfering drugs: increase by 12.5-25 mcg (to 88 or 100 mcg) rather than to full weight-based dose at once.
Recheck TSH (with or without free T4) about 6-8 weeks after a dose change.

forbidden.why: T3-containing therapy is not indicated for simple levothyroxine under-replacement.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: Stroke Prevention and Initial Evaluation
tasks.subject: New atrial fibrillation: stroke prevention and workup
tasks.request: Newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation on ECG 5/24, now on metoprolol for rate control. Please evaluate stroke prevention and complete the initial atrial fibrillation workup.

required.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (age 75-79, female, hypertension, diabetes) with low bleeding risk: a DOAC is indicated. Apixaban dose reduction needs 2 of age >=80, weight <=60 kg, creatinine >=1.5; she meets only weight, so 5 mg twice daily. Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about 46-48 mL/min gives rivaroxaban 15 mg daily or edoxaban 30 mg daily; dabigatran 150 mg twice daily (US label).
Transthoracic echocardiogram for new atrial fibrillation (structure, valves, LV function).
Thyroid function testing in new atrial fibrillation; none in 3 years.

forbidden.why: No antiplatelet indication; adding one to anticoagulation raises bleeding risk.
Only one apixaban dose-reduction criterion (weight <=60 kg) is met; 2.5 mg would underdose.

tasks.title: Migraine Classification and Preventive Treatment Plan
tasks.subject: Headache: preventive treatment consult
tasks.request: Increasing migraine frequency despite triptan. Please advise on and start preventive treatment, and advise whether imaging is needed.
facts: Seven migraine days per month with disability
No red flags; normal neurological exam

required.why: Seven migraine days per month with disability warrants prevention. Asthma with documented timolol-induced bronchospasm excludes beta-blockers; recurrent calcium oxalate stones with hypocitraturia make topiramate (a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) a poor choice. Tricyclics, venlafaxine, candesartan, CGRP-targeting agents or valproate (male patient) are acceptable.

forbidden.why: Moderate persistent asthma with prior bronchospasm from a topical beta-blocker.
Recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis with hypocitraturia.
Opioids and butalbital are not recommended for migraine and promote medication-overuse headache.

tasks.title: Microcytic Anemia in Pregnancy: Hematology eConsult
tasks.subject: Microcytic anemia in pregnancy
tasks.request: Microcytic anemia at prenatal intake (12 weeks). Please advise on the evaluation and treatment, and place any orders you recommend.
facts: No response to 3 months of oral iron in 2021
Brother with an inherited blood condition

required.why: Long-standing microcytosis (MCV 67-68) with normal ferritin, high RBC count (Mentzer index about 12), no response to iron and a suggestive family history point to thalassemia trait: order hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC, with alpha-globin gene testing if electrophoresis is normal.

forbidden.why: Iron replete (ferritin 92 ng/mL); parenteral iron carries risk without benefit.
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL in an asymptomatic patient does not warrant transfusion.

tasks.title: Type 2 Diabetes Treatment Intensification
tasks.subject: Diabetes intensification
tasks.request: A1c 8.6% on metformin. Please recommend and start the next glucose-lowering medicine.

required.why: HFrEF (EF 30%) and CKD 3a with albuminuria: an SGLT2 inhibitor with proven heart-failure benefit is indicated regardless of A1c and is usable at eGFR 54.

forbidden.why: Thiazolidinediones cause fluid retention and are contraindicated in symptomatic heart failure.
Saxagliptin and alogliptin carry an increased heart-failure hospitalization signal.

tasks.title: Unilateral Tinnitus and Audiology Follow-up
tasks.subject: Audiology results available
tasks.request: Audiogram and speech testing completed 2024-05-21. Report is in the chart.
facts: Interaural threshold difference 25 dB at 2-4 kHz

required.why: Asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss (>=15 dB at two or more adjacent frequencies) with unilateral tinnitus and reduced word recognition requires MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium to exclude a retrocochlear lesion such as vestibular schwannoma; no MRI contraindication and normal renal function.
Otolaryngology evaluation for asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss.

forbidden.why: Gradual loss over months is not sudden sensorineural hearing loss; systemic steroids are not indicated.

tasks.title: Home Asbestos Exposure: Risk Assessment and Follow-up Planning
tasks.subject: Asbestos found after home renovation
tasks.request: Patient reports two days of do-it-yourself floor-tile and joint-compound removal; laboratory testing later found asbestos in both materials. She asks about her health risk, whether she needs testing, and how to make the home safe. Please review the chart and advise.
facts: Incidental 7 mm solid noncalcified right lower lobe nodule (2023-12-04)
No prior chest imaging for comparison

required.why: Incidental 7 mm solid noncalcified nodule on the 2023-12-04 CT with no prior chest imaging: Fleischner Society 2017 recommends CT chest at 6-12 months for a single 6-8 mm solid nodule in both low- and high-risk patients, so it is due now. With eGFR 25 and a nephrology instruction to avoid iodinated contrast, the study must be non-contrast (thin-section, low dose), which is also the Fleischner technique. Brief environmental asbestos exposure does not itself warrant imaging.

forbidden.why: eGFR 25 (CKD stage 4) with a nephrology instruction to avoid iodinated contrast; contrast adds nothing to nodule surveillance.
Fleischner and ACCP: PET is not recommended for solid nodules smaller than 8 mm (poor sensitivity, false positives).
Invasive sampling is not indicated for a 7 mm nodule at its first follow-up.

tasks.title: Incidental Cardiopulmonary Findings on Coronary Calcium CT
tasks.subject: Incidental findings on coronary calcium CT
tasks.request: Coronary calcium CT reported incidental findings in a patient with systemic sclerosis and exertional breathlessness. Please evaluate and order the indicated workup.
facts: Main pulmonary artery 34 mm, PA:aorta ratio 1.13

required.why: Enlarged main pulmonary artery (34 mm, PA:aorta 1.13) with right heart enlargement in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (a high-risk group for pulmonary arterial hypertension), exertional dyspnea, loud P2 and raised NT-proBNP, with annual screening lapsed since 2021: transthoracic echocardiography is the first-line test for suspected pulmonary hypertension (ESC/ERS 2022).

Complete pulmonary function tests with DLCO: a falling DLCO (and FVC%/DLCO% ratio) is central to systemic sclerosis-associated PAH screening (DETECT; ESC/ERS 2022) and lung volumes screen for interstitial lung disease; last done in 2021 (DLCO 66%). Spirometry alone omits DLCO and does not satisfy this item.

forbidden.why: Pulmonary hypertension is suspected but unconfirmed; PAH-specific therapy requires diagnosis and classification by right heart catheterization (ESC/ERS 2022).

tasks.title: Chronic Cough: Evaluation and Stepwise Treatment Plan
tasks.subject: Follow-up: persistent cough
tasks.request: Follow-up visit today to review the chest radiograph and agree on a treatment plan for a cough present since March despite treatment.
facts: Acute urinary retention (950 mL) after a diphenhydramine-phenylephrine product
Upper airway features: throat clearing, cobblestoning

required.why: Chronic cough (about 12 weeks) with a normal chest radiograph, no ACE inhibitor, no reflux symptoms and no asthma features, with throat clearing, postnasal drainage, cobblestoning and rhinitis on exam: upper airway cough syndrome is most likely (ACCP/CHEST cough guidelines). The guideline first-generation antihistamine-decongestant is unsafe here (age over 65; BPH with documented acute urinary retention after a diphenhydramine-phenylephrine product; uncontrolled hypertension 152/88), so an intranasal corticosteroid (or intranasal azelastine) is the appropriate initial therapy.

forbidden.why: Anticholinergic first-generation antihistamines precipitated acute urinary retention in this man with BPH and are potentially inappropriate after age 65 (AGS Beers Criteria).
Sympathomimetic decongestants worsen urinary retention in BPH (prior retention episode) and raise blood pressure that is already uncontrolled (152/88).
Opioid antitussives are not indicated before the likely cause is treated and add sedation, constipation and urinary retention risk in BPH.

tasks.title: Hyperthyroidism in Early Pregnancy: Treatment Plan
tasks.subject: Graves disease, newly pregnant, off methimazole
tasks.request: Positive pregnancy test today (LMP 4/15). Methimazole stopped. Please assess her Graves disease in pregnancy and manage; prenatal labs were drawn today and are in the chart.
facts: Methimazole stopped at positive test (first trimester)
E. coli bacteriuria on intake culture

required.why: Graves disease diagnosed 9 months ago with TRAb 8.2 and a large goiter, now overtly hyperthyroid off methimazole (free T4 2.9, 1.6x the upper limit; heart rate over 100) at 7 weeks: antithyroid treatment is needed. ATA 2017 pregnancy guideline: propylthiouracil is preferred until 16 weeks because methimazole embryopathy peaks at 6-10 weeks. Methimazole 10 mg is about propylthiouracil 200 mg/day in divided doses (accepted 50-150 mg per dose, two or three times daily), aiming for free T4 at or just above the upper reference limit.
ATA 2017: measure TSH receptor antibody in early pregnancy in women with Graves disease (repeat at 18-22 weeks if elevated) to assess the risk of fetal and neonatal hyperthyroidism.

Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy (E. coli over 100,000 CFU/mL on the intake culture, never acknowledged) must be treated to prevent pyelonephritis (IDSA 2019; USPSTF; ACOG). The isolate is resistant to ampicillin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and ciprofloxacin and intermediate to amoxicillin-clavulanate; cefazolin-susceptible (oral cephalosporins) and nitrofurantoin-susceptible. Cephalexin 250-500 mg, cefuroxime, cefpodoxime, nitrofurantoin 100 mg (ACOG: acceptable in the first trimester) or single-dose fosfomycin 3 g are accepted.

forbidden.why: Methimazole embryopathy risk at 6-10 weeks; ATA 2017 prefers propylthiouracil in the first trimester.
Radioiodine therapy and uptake scans are contraindicated in pregnancy.
Radioiodine is contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal thyroid ablation).
Ampicillin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and ciprofloxacin resistant on culture; trimethoprim (first trimester folate antagonist), fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines are also avoided in pregnancy.
Atenolol is associated with fetal growth restriction; propranolol or metoprolol are used if a beta-blocker is needed.

extras.why: Short-term beta-blockade for symptomatic tachycardia is reasonable (ATA 2017).
Repeat thyroid function in 2-4 weeks.
Test-of-cure urine culture after treatment.
Obstetric ultrasound or maternal-fetal medicine input.

tasks.title: Diabetic Foot Infection: Antibiotic Selection and Osteomyelitis Evaluation
tasks.subject: Infected diabetic foot ulcer, probe-to-bone positive
tasks.request: Left first metatarsal head ulcer with spreading cellulitis and a positive probe-to-bone test; debrided and deep tissue sent for culture. No antibiotics yet. Please select antibiotic therapy, evaluate for osteomyelitis and place the orders.
facts: Prior MRSA, D-test positive, doxycycline susceptible (December 2023)

required.why: Moderate diabetic foot infection (erythema more than 2 cm, no systemic toxicity; IWGDF/IDSA 2023) in a chronic previously debrided ulcer: cover streptococci, MSSA and gram-negatives. Cockcroft-Gault CrCl = (140 - 65..76) x 72 / (72 x 2.6) = about 25-29 mL/min, so amoxicillin-clavulanate is limited to 250-500 mg every 12 hours and the 875 mg and extended-release tablets must not be used (label). The 2019 amoxicillin reaction was gastrointestinal intolerance, not allergy. Ertapenem 500 mg daily (CrCl <=30) or ceftriaxone 1-2 g daily are accepted parenteral options.

MRSA from this foot in December 2023 (old microbiology report): IWGDF/IDSA 2023 advise empiric MRSA coverage with prior MRSA infection or colonization. Clindamycin is excluded (D-test positive), levofloxacin is resistant and QT-prolonging, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is avoided (potassium 5.4 on lisinopril with CKD 4). Doxycycline or minocycline 100 mg twice daily (no renal adjustment) or linezolid 600 mg twice daily are appropriate.
Probe-to-bone positive with ESR 74: evaluate for osteomyelitis with plain radiographs of the foot first, and MRI if uncertain (IWGDF/IDSA 2023).

forbidden.why: QTc 492 ms on amiodarone (additive QT prolongation); the prior MRSA was levofloxacin-resistant.
Trimethoprim blocks potassium excretion: potassium 5.4 on lisinopril with CKD 4 (CrCl about 27) risks severe hyperkalemia.
D-test positive: inducible clindamycin resistance in the prior MRSA isolate.
Label: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg and extended-release tablets are not for CrCl <30; for CrCl 10-30 use 250-500 mg every 12 hours.
Ertapenem label: 500 mg daily for CrCl <=30 mL/min.
No role in diabetic foot infection; QT prolongation with amiodarone (and MRSA erythromycin-resistant).

extras.why: Bone biopsy for culture or blood cultures are reasonable.
Peripheral arterial assessment is standard for diabetic foot ulcers.
Monitoring tests are low-risk.
Multidisciplinary foot care referral.
Adding anaerobic cover to ceftriaxone is reasonable.

tasks.title: New Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult: Evaluation and Risk-Factor Management
tasks.subject: Patch monitor: paroxysmal AF
tasks.request: The 14-day patch confirms paroxysmal AF (burden 6%). Referred for new AF evaluation and cardiovascular risk-factor management. No regular medicines per patient. Please review and place orders.
facts: Patient may not list these medicines
No medicines reported at PCP reconciliation

required.why: LDL cholesterol 198 mg/dL (>=190) at age 38-45: statin therapy is indicated without risk calculation (2018 AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline, class 1, high intensity preferred). He takes darunavir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/TAF from an outside HIV clinic (documented only in the scanned 2023 letter; not on the medication list). Darunavir/cobicistat labeling and DHHS guidelines: simvastatin and lovastatin contraindicated; atorvastatin and rosuvastatin no more than 20 mg/day; pitavastatin without restriction; pravastatin titrated. Rosuvastatin 20 mg gives high intensity within the limit.

Loud snoring, witnessed apneas, Epworth 13, BMI 34, neck 45 cm and hypertension: high pretest probability of obstructive sleep apnea, a modifiable AF driver; 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends screening for sleep-disordered breathing.
Transthoracic echocardiogram for new atrial fibrillation (structural heart disease, LV function, atrial size) before rhythm-control decisions.

forbidden.why: Contraindicated with darunavir/cobicistat (strong CYP3A inhibition; rhabdomyolysis).
Darunavir/cobicistat labeling: do not exceed 20 mg/day of atorvastatin or rosuvastatin.
Cobicistat is a combined strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitor: apixaban label requires a 50% dose reduction (5 mg to 2.5 mg) and rivaroxaban should be avoided.
Dronedarone is contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors.

extras.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 1 (hypertension): anticoagulation may be considered; only the cobicistat-adjusted 2.5 mg dose escapes the forbidden set.
A beta-blocker for symptomatic rate control and hypertension is reasonable.
Treating stage 2 hypertension is reasonable (amlodipine at a low dose with cobicistat).
Ezetimibe added to an interaction-limited statin is reasonable for LDL 198.
Further lipid characterization and low-risk cardiovascular testing.
Coordination with the HIV clinic, lifestyle and weight programs, or electrophysiology are reasonable.

tasks.title: Follow-Up After Hospitalization for Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding
tasks.subject: Post-discharge follow-up: lower GI bleeding
tasks.request: Discharged 2024-05-21 after presumed diverticular bleeding while on aspirin for a coronary stent. Please review the hospitalization and complete the follow-up plan and orders.
facts: 2021 Forrest IIa gastric ulcer hemorrhage (scanned outside report)
Prior ulcer was NSAID- and aspirin-associated, H. pylori negative
Discharge summary wrongly states no prior GI bleeding
Aspirin continued for a drug-eluting stent

required.why: Presumed diverticular hemorrhage without a prior colonoscopy: colonoscopy is needed to confirm the source and exclude neoplasia (ACG 2023 lower GI bleeding guideline), arranged through gastroenterology. The discharge plan also asks for it.

The scanned 2021 outside endoscopy report documents a Forrest IIa gastric ulcer hemorrhage on aspirin plus ibuprofen (Helicobacter pylori negative). The 2024 discharge summary wrongly states no prior GI bleeding or peptic ulcer disease. Aspirin must continue for a drug-eluting stent. A patient on antiplatelet therapy with a prior ulcer bleed should take a standard-dose PPI (ACCF/ACG/AHA 2010 expert consensus on antiplatelet gastroprotection; ACG 2022 guideline on GI bleeding with antithrombotics). PPI dose ranges are FDA once-daily maintenance doses.

forbidden.why: Systemic NSAIDs after a prior NSAID-associated ulcer hemorrhage and a recent GI bleed, on continuing aspirin, carry a high rebleeding risk (ACG 2022; ACR 2019 osteoarthritis guideline favours topical NSAIDs and acetaminophen).

extras.why: Topical NSAID or acetaminophen for knee osteoarthritis is guideline-concordant with minimal GI risk.
Repeat H. pylori testing is low value (2021 biopsies negative) but harmless.
Iron studies after acute blood loss are reasonable.
Non-pharmacological or procedural options for knee osteoarthritis are reasonable extras.

tasks.title: New-Onset Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Stroke Prevention and Evaluation
tasks.subject: Patch monitor: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
tasks.request: The 14-day patch monitor report is finalized and shows paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Please review and determine management.
facts: Weight 78 kg entered in error (nursing addendum)
PCP note cites the erroneous 78 kg
Hypertension and diabetes (CHA2DS2-VASc 3 with female sex)

required.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (female, hypertension, diabetes): oral anticoagulation is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, class 1). The PCP note uses a weight of 78 kg, which a nursing addendum shows was entered in the wrong chart; the corrected weight is 52 kg (53.1 kg in 2023). Cockcroft-Gault with creatinine 1.3 mg/dL at age 48: (140-48) x 52 x 0.85 / (72 x 1.3) = 43 mL/min (41-46 across the age window), against 65 mL/min with the erroneous weight. FDA labels for CrCl 15-50: rivaroxaban 15 mg once daily with the evening meal and edoxaban 30 mg once daily; dabigatran 150 mg twice daily for CrCl above 30. Apixaban stays 5 mg twice daily because she meets only one reduction criterion (weight 60 kg or less; age under 80, creatinine under 1.5). Warfarin is guideline-acceptable but not preferred.
Transthoracic echocardiography is recommended in new AF to assess chamber size, LV function and valvular disease (2023 ACC/AHA AF guideline); none on file.

forbidden.why: Rivaroxaban 20 mg follows from the erroneous 78 kg weight (CrCl about 65); with the corrected 52 kg, CrCl is about 43 and the labelled AF dose is 15 mg.
Edoxaban 60 mg follows from the erroneous weight; for CrCl 15-50 the labelled dose is 30 mg.
Only one apixaban dose-reduction criterion is met (weight 52 kg); 2.5 mg twice daily is an off-label underdose.
Dabigatran 75 mg is labelled only for CrCl 15-30 (or interacting drugs); CrCl here is about 43.
Aspirin is not recommended for stroke prevention in AF and adds bleeding risk on top of anticoagulation (2023 ACC/AHA AF guideline).

extras.why: Beta-blocker rate control is reasonable for symptomatic paroxysmal AF with rates up to 152 bpm.
Thyroid and cardiovascular risk labs are routine in new AF.
ECG and sleep apnea screening are reasonable in new AF.
Further kidney assessment is harmless.

tasks.title: Osteoporosis Treatment After Completion of Anabolic Therapy
tasks.subject: Teriparatide course completed: next therapy and abnormal labs
tasks.request: Teriparatide 24-month course completed in April 2024 and the follow-up DXA is finalized. Labs on 2024-05-20 showed calcium 5.9 mg/dL and potassium 7.4 mmol/L. Please advise on the next osteoporosis treatment, on management of these laboratory abnormalities and on any monitoring needed.
facts: Laboratory invalidated the 2024-05-20 results as EDTA contamination
No new fracture with BMD gain

required.why: BMD gains from teriparatide are lost unless an antiresorptive follows; the 24-month course is complete and she remains osteoporotic with a prior vertebral fracture (Endocrine Society 2019/2020 guideline; AACE 2020). Any bisphosphonate at an FDA treatment dose, or denosumab 60 mg every 6 months, is acceptable. Renal function is normal and no dental surgery is planned. The calcium of 5.9 mg/dL on 2024-05-20 is not a barrier: the laboratory invalidated it as K2-EDTA contamination (with K 7.4, ALP 21 and Mg 0.9 in the same sample), and the recollected calcium is 9.3 mg/dL.

25-hydroxyvitamin D is 16 ng/mL. Deficiency must be corrected before and during bisphosphonate or denosumab therapy to avoid hypocalcemia (zoledronic acid and denosumab labels; Endocrine Society). Dosing is in IU, so no mass-dose constraint applies.

forbidden.why: Treats the calcium of 5.9 mg/dL, which the laboratory invalidated (EDTA contamination); recollected calcium 9.3 mg/dL and asymptomatic.
Treats the potassium of 7.4 mmol/L from the invalidated specimen; recollected potassium 4.3 mmol/L.
Treats the magnesium of 0.9 mg/dL from the invalidated specimen; recollected magnesium 2.0 mg/dL.

extras.why: Continuing or adjusting calcium supplementation is reasonable.
Repeat calcium, vitamin D or electrolyte measurement before the antiresorptive is reasonable.
Bone turnover markers are optional monitoring.
Repeat DXA in 1-2 years or a dental review before antiresorptive therapy are reasonable.

tasks.title: Travel Thromboprophylaxis Substitution Request
tasks.subject: US substitute for Fraxiparine before flights
tasks.request: I am flying from Boston to Athens on June 20 (about 12 hours with a connection) and back on July 6. The Fraxiparine injections I used before are not sold in the US. Could you prescribe the US equivalent for the flights?
facts: Apixaban 5 mg twice daily since 2024-05-18 (outside discharge summary)
Adherent to the new twice-daily blood thinner (nurse note)
Prior travel prophylaxis plan with Fraxiparine

forbidden.why: She is on therapeutic apixaban 5 mg twice daily for a popliteal DVT diagnosed 2024-05-11 (planned through at least 2024-08-14, covering both flights). Adding prophylactic LMWH or fondaparinux would be dual anticoagulation with no added benefit and excess bleeding risk.
A second anticoagulant while she is on apixaban is duplicate anticoagulation.
Aspirin is not recommended for travel thromboprophylaxis (ASH 2018/ACCP) and adds bleeding risk on apixaban.
The 7-day apixaban 10 mg twice-daily initiation phase ended on 2024-05-17; repeating it is an overdose.

extras.why: A refill of her current apixaban 5 mg twice daily to cover the trip is reasonable (the 10 mg dose is forbidden).
Below-knee compression stockings are reasonable during long-haul flights.
Hematology follow-up or follow-up duplex is harmless.

tasks.title: Diabetes and Kidney Disease Regimen Review
tasks.subject: Diabetes with persistent albuminuria
tasks.request: Type 2 diabetes with CKD 3a, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 410 mg/g, HbA1c 7.9% and blood pressure 146/88 on metformin and amlodipine. History of hyperkalemia. Please review and adjust the regimen.
facts: Potassium 6.4 specimen grossly hemolyzed and invalid (2023 nurse note)
RAAS blockade withheld because of hyperkalemia

required.why: Diabetes, hypertension and albuminuria (UACR 290 to 410 mg/g) call for an ACE inhibitor or ARB titrated to the maximum tolerated dose (KDIGO 2022 diabetes-CKD guideline 1A; ADA Standards of Care section 11). The only barrier was a potassium of 6.4 mmol/L on 2023-03-14. A nurse telephone note records the laboratory addendum: the specimen was grossly hemolyzed and the result invalid. Repeat potassium was 4.6, then 4.5, now 4.7 mmol/L. The problem-list hyperkalemia entry and the low-relevance order alert are stale. Any FDA dose range is accepted; recheck potassium and creatinine in 1-2 weeks.

An SGLT2 inhibitor with proven kidney benefit is recommended for T2D with CKD and eGFR of 20 or more (KDIGO 2022 1A; ADA 2024), independent of HbA1c. Canagliflozin is limited to 100 mg at eGFR 30-60 per the FDA label.

forbidden.why: Potassium is normal (4.5-4.7 mmol/L). The only high value was a hemolyzed, invalid specimen, so a potassium binder treats an artifact.
Aliskiren combined with an ACE inhibitor or ARB is contraindicated in diabetes (FDA label; ALTITUDE), and it has no kidney-outcome evidence on its own.

extras.why: A GLP-1 receptor agonist is a reasonable addition for HbA1c 7.9% with CKD (ADA 2024; FLOW trial).
Potassium, creatinine and albuminuria monitoring after starting RAAS blockade are expected.
Nephrology referral and routine diabetes care referrals are reasonable.

tasks.title: Recurrent Septic Olecranon Bursitis: Antibiotic Selection and Next Steps
tasks.subject: Recurrent right olecranon bursitis
tasks.request: Recurrent right olecranon septic bursitis 11 days after completing doxycycline; the culture grew MSSA. No known drug allergies. Would a beta-lactam such as cephalexin be appropriate now? Please advise on antibiotics and next steps.
facts: Referral and intake record no known drug allergies
MSSA susceptible to TMP-SMX and clindamycin (D-test negative)

required.why: Recurrent MSSA septic bursitis after doxycycline needs a different active oral agent (IDSA 2014 skin and soft tissue guideline). The referral and the urgent care intake record no known drug allergies and suggest cephalexin, but a 2015 ED note documents anaphylaxis to amoxicillin (hypotension 84/50, epinephrine). Penicillins and the cephalosporins that share the aminopenicillin R1 side chain (cephalexin, cefadroxil, cefaclor, cefprozil, cephradine) are therefore excluded (AAAAI/ACAAI 2022 drug allergy practice parameter). The isolate is susceptible to TMP-SMX and to clindamycin (D-test negative); linezolid is an alternative. TMP-SMX is accepted at any dose because tablet-based entries carry no reliable mass dose; clindamycin 300-450 mg and linezolid 600 mg follow the FDA labels.

Recurrence after an adequate course with a susceptible organism points to inadequate drainage. Repeat aspiration or drainage, and bursectomy if it recurs again, is managed by orthopedics (standard of care for refractory septic bursitis; this mirrors the official task).

forbidden.why: Documented anaphylaxis to amoxicillin (2015 ED note).
These cephalosporins share the R1 side chain with amoxicillin and carry the highest cross-reactivity risk after amoxicillin anaphylaxis (AAAAI/ACAAI 2022).

extras.why: Imaging of the elbow to assess the collection or exclude osteomyelitis is reasonable.
Blood cultures, inflammatory markers and repeat fluid culture are reasonable.
An allergy referral to clarify the beta-lactam allergy is reasonable.
Renewing an epinephrine auto-injector is reasonable after documented anaphylaxis.

tasks.title: Pruritic Blistering Eruption: Diagnosis and Treatment Planning
tasks.subject: Biopsy-proven bullous pemphigoid: systemic therapy
tasks.request: Four months of itchy blisters on the elbows, knees and buttocks; the skin biopsy favors bullous pemphigoid. Started clobetasol with partial relief. Please see for systemic treatment.
facts: DIF: granular IgA in dermal papillae (addendum)
Iron deficiency refractory to oral iron

required.why: The DIF addendum (granular IgA in the dermal papillae, no linear IgG/C3) revises the diagnosis to dermatitis herpetiformis, the cutaneous form of celiac disease. Iron deficiency refractory to oral iron and chronic loose stools support enteropathy. Tissue transglutaminase IgA (with total IgA) is the recommended serology (BAD and ACG 2023 celiac guidance).

Dapsone is the first-line drug for rapid control of dermatitis herpetiformis alongside a gluten-free diet. G6PD activity must be measured before starting it because of the risk of severe hemolysis (FDA label; BAD guidance). Dapsone is therefore deferred until the result is known.

forbidden.why: Starting dapsone, or sulfapyridine or sulfasalazine, before G6PD status is known risks severe hemolysis.
Systemic corticosteroids treat the withdrawn bullous pemphigoid diagnosis; they are ineffective for dermatitis herpetiformis and add toxicity.
Steroid-sparing therapy for bullous pemphigoid is based on the withdrawn interpretation and is not indicated for dermatitis herpetiformis.

extras.why: Total IgA alongside tTG-IgA, or HLA-DQ2/DQ8 typing, is reasonable.
Gastroenterology referral and dietitian input for a gluten-free diet are standard.
Nutritional deficiency and autoimmune thyroid screening are reasonable in celiac disease.
Potent topical corticosteroid and antihistamine for itch are safe while the workup proceeds.
E8: a baseline methemoglobin level before dapsone is reasonable.

tasks.title: COVID-19 Treatment in a Solid Organ Transplant Recipient
tasks.subject: COVID-19 in kidney transplant recipient
tasks.request: Kidney transplant recipient with PCR-confirmed COVID-19, symptom onset 5/31, not hypoxic. Please recommend and order antiviral treatment.
facts: Prior tacrolimus toxicity (trough 24.1 ng/mL) with clarithromycin
Nephrology alert: avoid strong CYP3A inhibitors

required.why: Kidney transplant recipient on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 (onset 2024-05-31, day 4), not requiring oxygen: high risk for progression, so outpatient antiviral treatment is indicated (NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines; IDSA). Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir is avoided: ritonavir strongly inhibits CYP3A, he had documented tacrolimus toxicity (trough 24.1 ng/mL with AKI) from clarithromycin, and transplant nephrology placed an alert to avoid strong CYP3A inhibitors where an alternative exists. Remdesivir 200 mg IV on day 1 then 100 mg IV daily on days 2-3 (PINETREE; within 7 days of onset, infusion feasible) is preferred; molnupiravir 800 mg twice daily for 5 days is an acceptable alternative.

forbidden.why: Ritonavir (strong CYP3A inhibitor) with tacrolimus, prior tacrolimus toxicity from a CYP3A interaction and a transplant nephrology alert; non-interacting alternatives are available.

tasks.title: Genitourinary Tuberculosis: Treatment Initiation

Ethambutol 1550 mg or more is above 25 mg/kg at the current weight of 58 kg (a dose based on the old 76 kg weight); ocular toxicity risk.
Nephrotoxic injectable agents are not indicated for pan-susceptible tuberculosis and would worsen CKD.

tasks.subject: Infection prevention during GPA induction

Prednisone 20 mg daily for 4 weeks at the end of the taper

tasks.title: Anemia of Chronic Kidney Disease Not on Dialysis: Treatment Initiation
tasks.subject: CKD 4 anemia: iron studies back, please start treatment
tasks.request: Hemoglobin 9.2 with CKD stage 4, not on dialysis, with fatigue and exertional dyspnea. Iron studies from 5/28 have resulted. Please see her in the anemia clinic and start the appropriate treatment.
facts: Iron 42 mcg/dL (lab report; TSAT not reported)
CRP 38 mg/L with diverticulitis (urgent care note)
eGFR 22, CKD stage 4 not on dialysis

required.why: Anemia of CKD stage 4 (eGFR 22), not on dialysis, hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL; B12 and folate normal. The laboratory does not report TSAT: TSAT = iron / TIBC x 100 = 42 / 310 x 100 = 13.5%, below 20% (and far below the KDIGO 30% ceiling for an iron trial). Ferritin 420 ng/mL is raised by inflammation (CRP 38 mg/L with diverticulitis 2 weeks earlier, urgent care note) and is below 500, so it does not exclude iron-restricted erythropoiesis. The outside TSAT of 24% from 2023 is superseded. KDIGO 2012: when TSAT is 30% or less and ferritin 500 ng/mL or less, give iron first; in non-dialysis CKD, IV iron or a 1-3 month oral trial. Accepted: iron sucrose 200 mg IV (per dose, course of 5), ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV, ferumoxytol 510 mg IV, ferric derisomaltose 1000 mg IV, or ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental) daily or every other day.

forbidden.why: With a computed TSAT of 13.5%, iron stores are inadequate: KDIGO advises correcting iron deficiency before starting an ESA (ESA response is blunted and higher doses are needed). The outside TSAT of 24% from 2023 is superseded.

extras.why: Repeat iron indices and reticulocyte count after repletion.

tasks.subject: Question about my thyroid medicine
tasks.request: Hi, I have had a few tests and visits over the last couple of weeks. Do I need to change anything about my thyroid pill? I am still taking 100 mcg every morning before breakfast.

She is hypothyroid on replacement; antithyroid drugs are not indicated.

tasks.title: Dermatology E-Consult: Acute Painful Vesicular Facial Eruption
tasks.subject: Painful vesicular rash, left forehead: treatment advice
tasks.request: Painful grouped vesicles on the left forehead, scalp and upper eyelid since this morning in a man with chronic kidney disease. Seen in urgent care today; labs were drawn. Please advise on treatment, including kidney-appropriate dosing.
facts: Creatinine 1.3 from the 11:00 draw retracted as a mislabeled specimen; redraw 2.6 mg/dL
Vesicles on the tip of the nose with a red, photophobic left eye (Hutchinson sign; after-hours nurse triage note only)
Vesicles in the left V1 dermatome since the morning of 2024-06-02 (within 72 hours)

required.why: Acute herpes zoster of the left V1 dermatome, rash day 2 (within 72 hours) in a man aged about 80: oral antiviral treatment is indicated, and the nasal-tip involvement adds urgency. The 11:00 creatinine of 1.3 mg/dL was retracted (mislabeled specimen); the 15:30 redraw is 2.6 mg/dL, matching his CKD stage 4 baseline of 2.5-2.7. Cockcroft-Gault CrCl = (140 - 80) x 66 / (72 x 2.6) = 3960 / 187.2 = about 21 mL/min (20-22 across ages 78-82). Labeled zoster doses for this band: valacyclovir CrCl 10-29 mL/min, 1 g every 24 hours; acyclovir CrCl 10-25 mL/min, 800 mg every 8 hours; famciclovir CrCl 20-39 mL/min, 500 mg every 24 hours (250 mg every 24 hours below 20; both accepted because CrCl is close to 20). The retracted value would give CrCl = 3960 / (72 x 1.3) = about 42 mL/min, the valacyclovir 1 g every 12 hours band, which is forbidden here.

Herpes zoster in the V1 dermatome with vesicles on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson sign: nasociliary branch involvement) and a red, photophobic eye with blurred vision, recorded only in the after-hours nurse triage telephone note. Hutchinson sign roughly doubles to triples the risk of ocular involvement (keratitis, uveitis); a red painful eye with reduced vision in HZO needs same-day slit-lamp examination by ophthalmology (AAO; standard of care).

forbidden.why: With CrCl about 21 mL/min, valacyclovir 1 g every 8 hours (normal function) or every 12 hours (CrCl 30-49, the band suggested by the retracted creatinine of 1.3) accumulates acyclovir and risks neurotoxicity and acute kidney injury; the labeled dose is 1 g every 24 hours. No valacyclovir zoster dose exceeds 1 g.
Acyclovir 800 mg five times daily is the dose for CrCl above 25 mL/min; at CrCl about 21 the labeled dose is 800 mg every 8 hours. No single oral acyclovir dose exceeds 800 mg.

extras.why: Kidney-safe analgesia for acute zoster pain.
Lesion PCR to confirm varicella-zoster virus is a reasonable extra.
Directing him to the emergency department for eye examination if same-day ophthalmology is unavailable is reasonable.

tasks.subject: Results visit today: thyroid tests and blood count
tasks.request: Patient roomed for her results visit. The labs drawn on 5/28 for fatigue are back with abnormal thyroid tests and a low blood count. Please review, start treatment and arrange follow-up.
facts: Intrinsic factor antibody positive (laboratory addendum only)
No coronary artery disease: normal stress echocardiogram 2023

required.why: Overt primary hypothyroidism from Hashimoto thyroiditis (TSH 48 mIU/L, free T4 0.4 ng/dL, TPO antibody 640 IU/mL). Replace B12 lifelong: cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg IM (for example daily for 1 week, weekly for 4 weeks, then monthly) or high-dose oral cyanocobalamin 1000-2000 mcg daily, which is absorbed by passive diffusion even without intrinsic factor.

After starting levothyroxine, TSH (free T4 optional) is rechecked 6-8 weeks later, when a new steady state is reached (ATA 2014), and the dose is adjusted. Window accepted: 5-9 weeks after today (days 35-63); reference day 42.

Celiac serology: autoimmune clustering with Hashimoto thyroiditis and pernicious anemia.
Iron studies (atrophic gastritis also impairs iron absorption).

tasks.request: Seen in urgent care on 5/20 for a gout flare, now settled. Urgent care stopped one of his blood pressure tablets and asked us to sort out a replacement. He would like a plan to prevent further attacks. Labs from 5/28 are in. Roomed and ready.

Progressive CKD stage 4, no reversible cause (nephrology)

ACR 2020: start allopurinol at no more than 100 mg/day, and at 50 mg/day in CKD stage 4 or worse, titrating by 50 mg every 2-5 weeks to urate below 6 mg/dL.

NSAIDs with CKD and coronary disease on aspirin: kidney injury, cardiovascular and bleeding risk.
Thiazide and thiazide-like diuretics raise serum urate and flare risk; it was stopped at urgent care for gout (ACR 2020).

Cardiovascular risk follow-up after prior myocardial infarction.

tasks.title: Preconception Visit With Chronic Hypertension
tasks.subject: Getting ready for pregnancy
tasks.request: I stopped my birth control pills and we would like to start trying for a baby soon. I am booked to see you on June 3; please check that my medicines and everything else are ready for pregnancy.
facts: No MMR recorded since (immunization registry, nurse intake)
Prior pregnancy terminated for anencephaly (scanned 2020 MFM letter)
Lisinopril 20 mg daily for chronic hypertension
Plans to conceive within 3 months; contraception stopped

required.why: Lisinopril 20 mg daily is fetotoxic, and she plans to conceive within 3 months, so it is replaced before conception by a pregnancy-compatible agent (ACOG Practice Bulletin 203, 2019; ACC/AHA 2017): labetalol 100-200 mg twice daily or nifedipine extended-release 30-60 mg once daily. Blood pressure 138/88 on lisinopril needs continued treatment.

The scanned 2019 preconception panel shows rubella IgG 4 IU/mL (non-immune), and the immunization registry records no MMR since. CDC/ACIP and ACOG: non-immune women planning pregnancy receive one dose of MMR before conception and avoid pregnancy for 4 weeks afterwards; she has just stopped contraception and is not yet pregnant (LMP 2024-05-22).

The scanned 2020 maternal-fetal medicine letter documents a pregnancy terminated at 18 weeks for anencephaly (G2P1); the 2018 intake "G1P1, uncomplicated" predates it. After a prior neural tube defect-affected pregnancy the dose is 4 mg (4000 mcg) folic acid daily from at least 1 month before conception through 12 weeks (ACOG Practice Bulletin 187; CDC). Arithmetic: 4 mg = 10 x the standard 0.4 mg dose, i.e. four 1 mg tablets daily. Folic acid 0.4-1 mg, or a prenatal vitamin alone, does not satisfy it.

After switching antihypertensive agents, blood pressure is rechecked in 2-4 weeks to titrate to below 140/90 before conception (ACOG PB 203; ACC/AHA). Arithmetic: task date 2024-06-03 + 14 to 28 days = 2024-06-17 to 2024-07-01; the reference schedules day 21, 2024-06-24.

forbidden.why: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and renin inhibitors are fetotoxic (renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia; FDA boxed warning) and are replaced before conception in a woman planning pregnancy (ACOG Practice Bulletin 203).

For primary prevention (LDL 112 mg/dL on treatment) statins are stopped when trying to conceive and through pregnancy and breastfeeding (FDA 2021 labeling; ACOG); a new statin order continues a drug that should be held.
Atenolol is associated with fetal growth restriction and is not used for chronic hypertension in pregnancy (ACOG).

extras.why: A pregnancy test before the live vaccine and the medication change is reasonable.
Baseline proteinuria, thyroid and glycemic screening before pregnancy with chronic hypertension and BMI 31 are reasonable.
Updated preconception serologies and a baseline ECG for chronic hypertension are reasonable.
A prenatal multivitamin is a reasonable addition before conception.
Methyldopa is a pregnancy-compatible alternative antihypertensive (ACOG); acceptable as an extra order.

tasks.title: Cardiology Visit: Newly Documented Atrial Fibrillation
tasks.subject: New atrial fibrillation: cardiology evaluation
tasks.request: Atrial fibrillation on her ECGs of 4/22 and 5/13; she has hypertension and CKD stage 3b. She wanted to discuss stroke prevention with you before starting anything. Please evaluate and manage; she is booked in your clinic on 2024-06-03.
facts: Holter: pauses up to 4.3 seconds at AF termination (scanned outside report, January 2024)
Persistent atrial fibrillation on serial ECGs (ECG report)
Apixaban is the only covered DOAC (pharmacist review)

required.why: Persistent atrial fibrillation (serial ECGs 2024-04-22, 2024-05-13 and today) with CHA2DS2-VA at least 3 (age 75 or older: 2; hypertension: 1; CHA2DS2-VASc at least 4): oral anticoagulation is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, class 1; 2024 ESC). A DOAC is preferred to warfarin; the 2023 AGS Beers criteria advise against rivaroxaban and first-line warfarin in older adults and caution with dabigatran, and the pharmacist review documents that apixaban is her plan's only covered DOAC (rivaroxaban, edoxaban and dabigatran non-formulary and unaffordable). Apixaban label (AF): 2.5 mg twice daily if at least 2 of age 80 or older, weight 60 kg or less, serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or more; otherwise 5 mg twice daily. Age 80-84: criterion met. Weight 58.5 kg on the calibrated re-weigh (nursing addendum; the 63.0 kg triage value came from a lobby scale reading about 4.5 kg high): criterion met. Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL: not met. Two criteria, so 2.5 mg twice daily.

The scanned outside 48-hour Holter (January 2024) shows paroxysmal AF at 112-158 bpm alternating with sinus rates of 46-58 bpm and 11 pauses over 3 seconds at AF termination, the longest 4.3 seconds, coinciding with a diary entry of near-syncope: tachycardia-bradycardia syndrome (symptomatic sinus node dysfunction). The 2018 ACC/AHA/HRS bradycardia guideline supports permanent pacing when symptoms are attributable to sinus node dysfunction, and pacing is needed before any rate- or rhythm-control drug can be used safely; the 2023 AF guideline considers ablation as an alternative. Both decisions belong to electrophysiology. A direct pacemaker or ablation order also satisfies this checkpoint.

Transthoracic echocardiography is recommended in newly diagnosed AF to assess LV function, atrial size and valves (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline), and informs device selection; she has never had one (primary care note).
Thyroid dysfunction is a reversible cause of both AF (2023 AF guideline: thyroid function in new AF) and sinus node dysfunction (2018 bradycardia guideline); TSH was last measured in 2019.

EHRA 2021 practical guide on NOACs: renal function at least yearly, and when CrCl is 60 mL/min or less, every CrCl/10 months. Cockcroft-Gault (female) with the confirmed weight: (140 - 82) x 58.5 x 0.85 / (72 x 1.3) = 2884 / 93.6 = about 31 mL/min (30-32 across ages 80-84), so the interval is about 3 months (31 / 10 = 3.1). Window days 75-120 (2.5-4 months, 2024-08-17 to 2024-10-01) holds over the whole age range; the reference schedules day 91, 2024-09-02. An undated order, or one dated a year out, does not satisfy this.

forbidden.why: Apixaban 5 mg (or 10 mg) follows the 63.0 kg triage weight from a scale reading about 4.5 kg high; with the calibrated 58.5 kg and age 80 or older, two label criteria are met and the dose is 2.5 mg twice daily (higher bleeding risk at 5 mg).

Dabigatran is about 80% renally cleared; with CrCl about 30-32 mL/min at age 80 or older it accumulates (2023 AGS Beers: use with caution, more gastrointestinal bleeding than alternatives in older adults), and it is non-formulary for her.

Documented conversion pauses up to 4.3 seconds with near-syncope and awake sinus rates of 46-58 bpm, without a pacemaker: beta-blockers, diltiazem, verapamil, digoxin and ivabradine lengthen pauses and risk syncope or asystole; rate control is started only after pacing (2018 ACC/AHA/HRS bradycardia guideline).

Antiarrhythmic drugs suppress sinus node function and prolong post-conversion pauses; in tachycardia-bradycardia syndrome they are started only with pacing backup or under electrophysiology supervision.
No vascular indication: antiplatelet therapy is not recommended for stroke prevention in AF and adds bleeding risk to anticoagulation (2023 AF guideline).

Persistent AF for over 6 weeks without 3 weeks of therapeutic anticoagulation carries thromboembolic risk, and her documented conversion pauses up to 4.3 seconds make cardioversion without pacing backup unsafe; rhythm control is an electrophysiology decision after pacing.

extras.why: A repeat 12-lead ECG is a standard baseline before device evaluation.
Repeat ambulatory monitoring to quantify current rates and pauses is reasonable before electrophysiology review.
Low-risk baseline cardiovascular, thyroid and coagulation tests before anticoagulation and device evaluation.
Exercise testing for chronotropic competence is reasonable in suspected sinus node dysfunction.
Sleep apnea contributes to AF and nocturnal bradycardia; screening is reasonable.
Fall-risk assessment is reasonable for an older adult with near-syncope starting anticoagulation.

tasks.title: Endocrinology Consultation: New Atrial Fibrillation with Suppressed TSH
tasks.subject: New atrial fibrillation with suppressed TSH
tasks.request: New paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with a goiter; urgent care TSH 0.008 with free T4 5.6. The patch and echo are under way in cardiology. Please evaluate and treat her thyroid disease and manage her symptoms; she is booked with you on 2024-06-03.
facts: Severe bronchospasm after a first dose of propranolol (2021 pulmonology note)
Valid repeat free T4 4.1 ng/dL, 6 days off biotin
Laboratory comment: the biotin-affected 5.6 ng/dL is superseded
Biotin 10,000 mcg daily at the time of the urgent care sample

required.why: Graves disease: TSH receptor antibody 9.8 IU/L (positive, drawn 6 days off biotin), suppressed TSH and a diffuse goiter, with thyrotoxic paroxysmal AF. Antithyroid drug therapy is indicated and methimazole is preferred outside the first trimester (ATA 2016); pregnancy is excluded (negative urine tests on 2024-05-20 and today; copper IUD). ATA 2016 rough guide to the initial methimazole dose: free T4 1-1.5 x ULN, 5-10 mg/day; 1.5-2 x, 10-20 mg/day; 2-3 x, 30-40 mg/day. Valid free T4 4.1 ng/dL (2024-05-30, 6 days off biotin; reference 0.8-1.7): 4.1 / 1.7 = 2.41 x ULN, 20% above the 2.0 boundary and 20% below 3.0, so 30-40 mg/day. Accepted as 30-40 mg once daily, 15-20 mg twice daily, or 10-13.3 mg three times daily (the FDA label divides the daily dose into three). The urgent-care 5.6 ng/dL (3.3 x ULN) was drawn on biotin 10,000 mcg daily with a biotin-sensitive assay and is superseded.

Paroxysmal AF (patch burden 41%, 108-168 bpm) with heart rate 124 today from thyrotoxicosis: ATA 2016 recommends beta-adrenergic blockade in symptomatic thyrotoxicosis with resting heart rate over 90, and the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline uses a beta-blocker or a nondihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker for rate control. The 2021 pulmonology note documents moderate persistent asthma and an emergency visit in 2019 for severe bronchospasm after a first dose of propranolol, so non-selective beta-blockers are excluded. Accepted: a beta-1-selective agent used with caution (metoprolol, atenolol, bisoprolol) or diltiazem or verapamil (ATA: calcium-channel blockers when beta-blockers cannot be used), within labelled dose ranges.

ATA 2016 recommends a baseline complete blood count with white-cell differential before starting an antithyroid drug (agranulocytosis risk; Graves disease itself can lower the neutrophil count). The only blood count on file is from 2021.

ATA 2016 recommends a baseline liver profile (bilirubin and transaminases) before starting an antithyroid drug (drug-induced hepatotoxicity; thyrotoxicosis can raise liver enzymes). None is on file. A comprehensive metabolic panel satisfies this.

ATA 2016: free T4 (with total T3) 2-6 weeks after starting methimazole, then dose adjustment; TSH can stay suppressed for months, so TSH alone does not satisfy this. Window days 14-42 (2024-06-17 to 2024-07-15); the reference schedules day 28, 2024-07-01.

forbidden.why: Moderate persistent asthma with severe bronchospasm after a first dose of propranolol in 2019 (2021 pulmonology note): non-selective beta-blockade (propranolol, nadolol and similar) risks life-threatening bronchospasm.
Methimazole 10 mg/day or less is the band for free T4 1-1.5 x ULN; at 2.4 x ULN with AF it leaves her thyrotoxic for months (ATA 2016: 30-40 mg/day).
More than 40 mg/day follows the biotin-affected free T4 of 5.6 ng/dL (3.3 x ULN); at the valid 2.4 x ULN it overtreats, and methimazole agranulocytosis and hepatotoxicity are dose-related.
Amiodarone is 37% iodine by weight; its iodine load can worsen thyrotoxicosis and delay definitive therapy, and thyrotoxic AF usually reverts once she is euthyroid (ATA 2016; 2023 AF guideline).

extras.why: Transthoracic echocardiography is recommended in new AF and screens for thyrotoxic cardiomyopathy; cardiology has requested one, so another request is redundant but harmless.
A baseline T3 gauges T3-predominant disease; TSH or antibody repeats are harmless.
Thyroid ultrasound is optional with a diffuse goiter and positive TSH receptor antibody.
A serum pregnancy test before a teratogenic drug is reasonable even after negative urine tests.
A repeat ECG or cardiology follow-up to assess rate control is reasonable.

tasks.subject: Abdominal ultrasound result flagged
tasks.request: Right upper quadrant ultrasound finalized 2024-05-24 with gallbladder and liver findings that need follow-up. Report is in the chart.

required.why: An indeterminate 2.2 cm solid, vascular liver lesion needs multiphase contrast-enhanced characterization (ACR Appropriateness Criteria, liver lesion initial characterization). Prior anaphylaxis to iodinated contrast (iohexol, 2018) makes contrast CT inappropriate when an equivalent non-iodinated study exists, so MRI with gadolinium is the study of choice; contrast-enhanced ultrasound is an accepted alternative. No MRI contraindication; eGFR 81.

A sessile 13 mm gallbladder polyp that grew from 8 mm: polyps of 10 mm or more (and growth of 4 mm or more) warrant surgical consultation for cholecystectomy under both the 2022 SRU consensus and the 2022 ESGAR/EAES/IHPBA/ESGE/EFISDS guideline; surveillance alone is not appropriate.

forbidden.why: Documented anaphylaxis to iodinated contrast (iohexol, 2018): the ACR Manual on Contrast Media advises a non-iodinated alternative when it answers the clinical question, and MRI is equivalent or better for liver lesion characterization. Non-contrast CT (stated as without contrast) is not penalized but does not characterize the lesion.

ATA 2016: free T4 (with total T3) 2-6 weeks after starting methimazole, then dose adjustment; TSH can stay suppressed for months, so TSH alone does not satisfy this. Window days 14-42 (2024-06-17 to 2024-07-15); the reference schedules day 28, 2024-07-01.

forbidden.why: Moderate persistent asthma with severe bronchospasm after a first dose of propranolol in 2019 (2021 pulmonology note): non-selective beta-blockade (propranolol, nadolol and similar) risks life-threatening bronchospasm.

Methimazole 20 mg/day or more follows the biotin-affected free T4 of 5.6 ng/dL (3.3 x ULN); at the valid 1.3 x ULN it overtreats toward hypothyroidism, and agranulocytosis and hepatotoxicity are dose-related (ATA 2016: 5-10 mg/day).
Amiodarone is 37% iodine by weight; its iodine load can worsen thyrotoxicosis and delay definitive therapy, and thyrotoxic AF usually reverts once she is euthyroid (ATA 2016; 2023 AF guideline).

extras.why: Transthoracic echocardiography is recommended in new AF and screens for thyrotoxic cardiomyopathy; cardiology has requested one, so another request is redundant but harmless.
A baseline T3 gauges T3-predominant disease; TSH or antibody repeats are harmless.
Thyroid ultrasound is optional with a diffuse goiter and positive TSH receptor antibody.
A serum pregnancy test before a teratogenic drug is reasonable even after negative urine tests.
A repeat ECG or cardiology follow-up to assess rate control is reasonable.

tasks.subject: Results visit today: arthritis blood tests and X-rays
tasks.request: Patient roomed for her results visit. The rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP and inflammatory markers drawn on 5/20 and the X-ray reports are back. Please review, start treatment and set up any monitoring.
facts: Patient global 7/10 and evaluator global 6/10 (CDAI components)
Copper IUD inserted 2024-02-12 with a decision not to have children for several years (gynecology)
Copper IUD in place (nurse intake and medication list)
Normal kidney and liver function at baseline

required.why: New seropositive rheumatoid arthritis: ACR/EULAR 2010 score 10 (more than 10 joints including small joints 5; high-positive RF 186 IU/mL and anti-CCP 312 U/mL 3; CRP 31 mg/L and ESR 48 mm/h 1; symptoms 4 months 1). High disease activity: CDAI = 9 swollen + 12 tender + patient global 7 + evaluator global 6 = 34 (above 22). ACR 2021: methotrexate monotherapy is strongly recommended over hydroxychloroquine or sulfasalazine, and conditionally over leflunomide, for csDMARD-naive patients with moderate-high disease activity; start at 15 mg once weekly (accepted 10-20 mg once weekly, oral or subcutaneous) and escalate. Reproductive status decides it: a copper IUD since 2024-02-12, and on 2024-05-29 she confirmed no plans for pregnancy in the next several years (the 2022 wish to start a family within 1-2 years is outdated), so methotrexate is used with reliable contraception. Normal kidney and liver function (creatinine 0.68 mg/dL, ALT 17 U/L), clear chest radiograph, alcohol 1-2 drinks per month.

Folic acid with methotrexate reduces gastrointestinal, hepatic and mucosal toxicity (ACR 2008/2021; Cochrane 2013): 1 mg daily (accepted 1-5 mg daily, or 5 mg once weekly as in BSR 2017); leucovorin (folinic acid) is an accepted alternative.

Hepatitis B serologies (HBsAg and anti-HBc) are obtained before methotrexate (ACR 2008/2012 recommendations; BSR 2017): methotrexate is hepatotoxic and immunosuppressive and can reactivate HBV. None is on file.

Hepatitis C antibody before methotrexate (ACR 2008/2012: hepatitis B and C serologies at baseline for methotrexate and leflunomide); none on file. An undetected chronic hepatitis C raises the risk of methotrexate liver injury.

ACR 2008/2012: CBC, liver enzymes and creatinine every 2-4 weeks for the first 3 months after starting methotrexate (myelosuppression). Arithmetic: task date 2024-06-03 + 14 to 35 days = 2024-06-17 to 2024-07-08; the reference schedules day 28, 2024-07-01.

ACR 2008/2012: liver enzymes (a comprehensive metabolic panel also gives albumin and creatinine) every 2-4 weeks for the first 3 months of methotrexate (hepatotoxicity). Window days 14-35 (2024-06-17 to 2024-07-08); reference day 28, 2024-07-01.

forbidden.why: Methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis is taken once weekly. Daily (or every-other-day or divided daily) dosing is a recognised, sometimes fatal prescribing error (FDA label warning; ISMP high-alert drug): bone-marrow failure, mucositis, hepatotoxicity and death.

Retinal toxicity limit 5 mg/kg/day of actual body weight (AAO 2016; ACR/AAD/AAO/RDS 2020): 5 x 54 kg = 270 mg/day. A single dose of 300 mg or more (300 mg/day = 5.6 mg/kg; 400 mg/day = 7.4 mg/kg) or 200 mg twice daily (400 mg/day) exceeds it.

extras.why: Triple csDMARD therapy (methotrexate plus sulfasalazine and hydroxychloroquine) is an evidence-based alternative for high disease activity, although ACR 2021 conditionally prefers methotrexate monotherapy first; hydroxychloroquine above 5 mg/kg is forbidden separately.

HIV and tuberculosis screening, hepatitis B surface antibody (vaccine response) or a repeat chest radiograph are reasonable pre-immunosuppression extras (the May chest radiograph already meets the methotrexate baseline).

Short-term low-dose glucocorticoid bridging (prednisone 10 mg/day or less, or a single intramuscular depot) is reasonable while the csDMARD takes effect (ACR 2021 conditionally against long-term use only); compatible with conception at low dose.
A scheduled or as-needed NSAID for symptom relief is reasonable with normal kidney function.
Simple analgesia.

Vaccination before immunosuppression (ACR 2022 vaccine guideline: pneumococcal, influenza, COVID-19, recombinant zoster, HPV; hepatitis B vaccine if non-immune) is reasonable, as an order or a service.
A pregnancy test before starting a csDMARD is reasonable.
Repeat inflammatory markers, ANA and differential serologies, anti-Ro/La, or G6PD before sulfasalazine or hydroxychloroquine are reasonable extras.
Hand therapy or occupational therapy for active small-joint synovitis.
Baseline retinal examination within the first year of hydroxychloroquine (AAO 2016).

tasks.title: Chronic Hepatitis C With Cirrhosis: Treatment Visit
tasks.subject: Hepatitis C treatment visit today
tasks.request: Patient roomed for his hepatitis C treatment visit. His evaluation results from April and May are in the chart. Please review, start treatment and arrange follow-up.
facts: No ascites and no focal lesion on the 2024-05-20 ultrasound

required.why: Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, HCV RNA 2,150,000 IU/mL, treatment-naive; cirrhosis (liver stiffness 16.4 kPa, nodular liver, splenomegaly; no varices on the 2024-05-14 endoscopy); HIV negative. Current Child-Pugh (2024-05-28 labs, 2024-05-20 ultrasound, today's intake): bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL (below 2) = 1, albumin 3.9 g/dL (above 3.5) = 1, INR 1.1 (below 1.7) = 1, no ascites = 1, no encephalopathy = 1; total 5, class A (compensated). The Child-Pugh B (score 8) of the outside admission (albumin 2.6, bilirubin 2.3, INR 1.4 during pneumonia with sepsis) is superseded by recovery. AASLD-IDSA (simplified treatment of compensated cirrhosis; genotype 1a, treatment-naive): glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (Mavyret) 3 tablets once daily with food for 8 weeks, or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa) 1 tablet daily for 12 weeks; ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (Harvoni) for 12 weeks is also a recommended genotype 1a regimen. No ribavirin. No interacting medications (no acid suppressants, statins, amiodarone or enzyme inducers). Duration is checked in the note.

AASLD-IDSA HCV guidance and the FDA boxed warning for all direct-acting antivirals: test HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs before treatment, because HBV can reactivate (sometimes fulminantly) when HCV is cleared. His hepatitis B status has never been tested; the April work-up sent only HCV RNA, genotype and HIV.

Cure is confirmed by undetectable HCV RNA at least 12 weeks after the end of treatment (SVR12; AASLD-IDSA). Arithmetic: 8 weeks of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir ends on day 56, so SVR12 is due from day 56 + 84 = 140; 12 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir or ledipasvir/sofosbuvir ends on day 84, so from day 168. Window days 140-210 (2024-10-21 to 2024-12-30) covers every accepted regimen started within about 2 weeks; reference day 168 (2024-11-18).

Cirrhosis: hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance with ultrasound (with or without AFP) every 6 months (AASLD 2023), continued after cure. The last ultrasound was 2024-05-20 (no focal lesion, LI-RADS US-1), so the next is due about 2024-11-20. Window days 150-210 (2024-10-31 to 2024-12-30); reference day 170 (2024-11-20). MRI or CT in the window is accepted.

forbidden.why: Ribavirin is not indicated with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in treatment-naive genotype 1a compensated cirrhosis (AASLD-IDSA) and adds dose-related haemolytic anaemia and teratogenicity. It follows from the superseded Child-Pugh B of the sepsis admission.

extras.why: AFP with the surveillance ultrasound (AASLD 2023: ultrasound with or without AFP).
An additional HCV RNA (on treatment or at the end of treatment) is reasonable; only the scheduled SVR12 test is required.
Hepatic panel and INR during treatment of cirrhosis are reasonable.
Hepatitis A immunity testing and vaccination against hepatitis A, hepatitis B (if non-immune), pneumococcus and influenza are recommended in cirrhosis.
Resistance-associated substitution testing or repeat genotyping is harmless (needed only for elbasvir/grazoprevir).
A repeat HIV test is harmless (non-reactive in April).
Dietitian or pharmacist (drug-interaction) review is reasonable in cirrhosis.
A hepatology follow-up visit during treatment.

tasks.subject: Hepatitis C treatment visit today
tasks.request: Patient roomed for his hepatitis C treatment visit. His evaluation results from April and May are in the chart. Please review, start treatment and arrange follow-up.
facts: New moderate ascites on the 2024-05-20 ultrasound
Paracentesis 2024-05-21: portal-hypertensive ascites (SAAG 1.7), no SBP; diuretics started

required.why: Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, HCV RNA 2,150,000 IU/mL, treatment-naive; cirrhosis (liver stiffness 16.4 kPa, nodular liver, splenomegaly; no varices on the 2024-05-14 endoscopy); HIV negative. Weight-based ribavirin with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in decompensated cirrhosis (AASLD-IDSA; ASTRAL-4): 1000 mg/day below 75 kg, 1200 mg/day at 75 kg or more, in two divided doses with food. Weight 85 kg today (13% above the 75 kg cut-off; still above it after allowing for some ascites): 1200 mg/day = 600 mg twice daily (accepted as 600 mg twice daily, or 1200 mg/day written as divided doses). Ribavirin-eligible: hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, no cardiac disease; his wife is postmenopausal. A low starting dose of 600 mg/day (600 mg once daily or 300 mg twice daily), increased as tolerated, is also accepted: AASLD-IDSA lists it with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir in decompensated cirrhosis, and some hepatologists start low with either regimen because of haemolysis.

First decompensation (new ascites) in cirrhosis is an indication for liver transplant evaluation (AASLD/AST 2013: decompensation or MELD 15 or more), and AASLD-IDSA advises managing decompensated HCV cirrhosis with a liver transplant center. MELD: bilirubin 2.4, INR 1.5, creatinine 0.9 (set to 1.0) gives MELD(i) 14.3; MELD-Na with sodium 134 = 14.3 + 1.32 x 3 - 0.033 x 14.3 x 3 = 16.8, i.e. 17.

AASLD-IDSA HCV guidance and the FDA boxed warning for all direct-acting antivirals: test HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs before treatment, because HBV can reactivate (sometimes fulminantly) when HCV is cleared. His hepatitis B status has never been tested; the April work-up sent only HCV RNA, genotype and HIV.

Ribavirin causes dose-related haemolytic anaemia, mostly in the first 2-4 weeks (label: hemoglobin at weeks 2 and 4); decompensated cirrhosis needs close monitoring and dose reduction if hemoglobin falls below 10 g/dL. Window days 10-21 (2024-06-13 to 2024-06-24); reference day 14 (2024-06-17).

Cirrhosis: hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance with ultrasound (with or without AFP) every 6 months (AASLD 2023), continued after cure. The last ultrasound was 2024-05-20 (no focal lesion, LI-RADS US-1), so the next is due about 2024-11-20. Window days 150-210 (2024-10-31 to 2024-12-30); reference day 170 (2024-11-20). MRI or CT in the window is accepted.

SVR12: HCV RNA at least 12 weeks after the end of treatment. 12 weeks of treatment end on day 84, so SVR12 is due from day 84 + 84 = 168. Window days 168-230 (2024-11-18 to 2025-01-19); reference day 175 (2024-11-25).

forbidden.why: NS3/4A protease-inhibitor regimens (glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir, elbasvir/grazoprevir, paritaprevir- or simeprevir-based) are contraindicated in moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C; FDA labels): higher exposure and hepatic decompensation, failure or death. extras.why: AFP with the surveillance ultrasound (AASLD 2023: ultrasound with or without AFP).
An additional HCV RNA (on treatment or at the end of treatment) is reasonable; only the scheduled SVR12 test is required.
Hepatic panel and INR during treatment of cirrhosis are reasonable.
Hepatitis A immunity testing and vaccination against hepatitis A, hepatitis B (if non-immune), pneumococcus and influenza are recommended in cirrhosis.
Resistance-associated substitution testing or repeat genotyping is harmless (needed only for elbasvir/grazoprevir).
A repeat HIV test is harmless (non-reactive in April).
Dietitian or pharmacist (drug-interaction) review is reasonable in cirrhosis.
A hepatology follow-up visit during treatment.
Haemolysis markers on ribavirin.
Ascites management (therapeutic paracentesis as needed, urine sodium, electrolytes on diuretics).
Re-ordering the current diuretics is reasonable.
Repeat variceal screening after decompensation (Baveno VII: yearly in decompensated cirrhosis without varices).
A baseline ECG before ribavirin is reasonable.

tasks.title: Prenatal Visit: Anemia and Hypothyroidism at 16 Weeks
tasks.subject: 16-week visit today: blood count, iron studies and thyroid tests
tasks.request: Patient roomed for her 16-week prenatal visit. The laboratory tests from her transfer intake on 5/20 show anemia and an abnormal thyroid result. Please review, start treatment and arrange follow-up.
facts: Ferritin 9 ng/mL on 2024-05-20, with CRP 2 mg/L
RBC 4.0 x10^6/uL with MCV 69 fL: Mentzer index 17.3
CRP 2 mg/L with the current iron studies
Outside ferritin drawn during febrile influenza A, CRP 86 mg/L (scanned report)
No levothyroxine dose change since conception
Singleton intrauterine pregnancy, EDD 2024-11-18 (16 weeks today)

required.why: Microcytic anemia at 14 weeks (hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, MCV 69 fL) with ferritin 9 ng/mL while CRP was 2 mg/L, transferrin saturation 6% (iron 28 / TIBC 467), high RDW 17.6% and RBC 4.0 x10^6/uL: Mentzer index 69/4.0 = 17.3, above 13. This is iron-deficiency anemia, after a postpartum hemorrhage in 2021 and on only the prenatal vitamin. The outside ferritin of 68 ng/mL (2024-04-22) was drawn during febrile influenza A with CRP 86 mg/L; ferritin is an acute-phase reactant, so that value is superseded by the repeat. The prenatal vitamin (27 mg iron) is not treatment; ACOG Practice Bulletin 233 (2021) recommends therapeutic oral iron, e.g. ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) once daily or on alternate days. Standard tablet strengths of the common salts, ferric maltol 30 mg, or 60-120 mg elemental iron are accepted.
required.dose: 325 or 324 or 300 or 200 or 160 or 142 or 65 or 60 mg

required.why: Hashimoto hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 100 mcg daily with no dose change since conception (transfer intake). TSH 4.8 mIU/L at 14 weeks (free T4 0.9 ng/dL) is above the trimester-specific upper limit (ATA 2017: about 4.0 mIU/L when no local range is available) and far above the target for treated women, the lower half of the range (below 2.5). ATA 2017: increase the dose; requirements rise by about 25-30% in pregnancy. Arithmetic: 100 mcg x 1.25 = 125 mcg once daily (+25%). Accepted: 112-137 mcg once daily (+12% to +37%), or 100 mcg daily plus 2 extra doses a week (900/700 mcg = +29%). The pre-pregnancy TSH of 1.6 (2023) predates the pregnancy.

After a levothyroxine dose change in pregnancy, TSH (with free or total T4) is rechecked in about 4 weeks and every 4 weeks through mid-gestation (ATA 2017). Arithmetic: 2024-06-03 + 21 to 35 days = 2024-06-24 to 2024-07-08; the reference schedules day 28, 2024-07-01 (20 weeks). A TSH drawn today or months later does not satisfy this.

Response to oral iron is confirmed by a hemoglobin rise of about 1 g/dL within 2-4 weeks (ACOG Practice Bulletin 233; BSH 2019 guideline on iron deficiency in pregnancy: recheck at 2-4 weeks and consider intravenous iron if there is no response). Arithmetic: 2024-06-03 + 14 to 35 days = 2024-06-17 to 2024-07-08; the reference schedules day 28, 2024-07-01, with the TSH. Reticulocytes or ferritin may be added to the same draw.

forbidden.why: Asymptomatic, hemodynamically stable anemia with hemoglobin above 9 g/dL in the second trimester does not warrant red cell transfusion.
Liothyronine or desiccated thyroid is not used in pregnancy (ATA 2017: levothyroxine only; T3-containing preparations deliver less T4 to the fetal brain).

extras.why: Hemoglobinopathy screening is reasonable in pregnancy with microcytosis (ACOG Practice Bulletin 78), but not required: the iron indices and Mentzer index explain the microcytosis.
Follow-up iron studies, reticulocytes, folate or B12 to document the response or a combined deficiency.
Free or total T4 (or TPO antibodies) with the thyroid follow-up is standard.

Intravenous iron is an option in the second trimester for intolerance of or no response to oral iron (ACOG Practice Bulletin 233); reasonable as an extra, but oral iron is first line at hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL and does not satisfy the requirement by itself.
Continuing the prenatal vitamin or folic acid is appropriate.
A stool softener or osmotic laxative for iron-related constipation in pregnancy is reasonable.
Endocrinology, maternal-fetal medicine or hematology co-management is reasonable.
The routine 18-22 week anatomy ultrasound is a reasonable extra.

tasks.title: New Deep Vein Thrombosis: Long-Term Anticoagulation Visit
tasks.subject: New DVT: long-term anticoagulation decision today
tasks.request: Woman in her 40s with an acute left femoral-popliteal DVT on 5/31; combined pill stopped; given a 3-day parenteral bridge. She also has heavy periods and iron-deficiency anemia. Booked in your clinic on 6/3 to choose and start long-term anticoagulation and to address the bleeding and anemia.
facts: Confirmatory panel 2023-06-12 (16 weeks later, off anticoagulation): lupus anticoagulant not detected
Acute occlusive DVT of the left femoral and popliteal veins on duplex (ED)
Estrogen-containing combined pill since January 2024, stopped in the ED
The single positive lupus anticoagulant was drawn during a heparin infusion (not interpretable)

required.why: Acute proximal DVT (left femoral and popliteal veins) provoked by an estrogen-containing combined pill (stopped), without PE, in a 76 kg woman with normal renal and liver function and platelets: outpatient oral anticoagulation. The 2023 lupus anticoagulant was positive once only, drawn during a heparin infusion and acute pneumonia (not interpretable, per rheumatology); the confirmatory panel 16 weeks later, off anticoagulation, showed lupus anticoagulant not detected and negative anticardiolipin and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I antibodies, so antiphospholipid syndrome is not established. CHEST 2021 recommends a DOAC over a VKA for VTE without cancer or APS. Initial phase by label: apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily; or rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily with food for 21 days, then 20 mg once daily. Both start without a parenteral lead-in, at the time the next enoxaparin dose would have been due (this evening). Starting at the maintenance dose does not satisfy the initial phase.

Iron-deficiency anemia from heavy menstrual bleeding: hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, ferritin 5 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 5% on 2024-05-31 (ferritin 8 ng/mL in January); she never started iron, and anticoagulation will likely increase menstrual losses. Oral iron is first line: ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) once daily or on alternate days; equivalent salts, ferric maltol 30 mg or 60-120 mg elemental iron are accepted. Intravenous iron is also accepted because losses are ongoing and expected to rise on anticoagulation.
required.dose: 325 or 324 or 300 or 200 or 160 or 142 or 65 or 60 mg

required.why: Heavy menstrual bleeding (a pad every 1-2 hours on days 1-3, ferritin 5 ng/mL) is likely to worsen on anticoagulation (anticoagulant-associated abnormal uterine bleeding affects up to 70% of menstruating women). The estrogen-containing pill is stopped and must not restart, and tranexamic acid is avoided with an acute clot; ISTH guidance favours a levonorgestrel intrauterine system, which treats the bleeding and provides contraception without raising thrombotic risk. The planned pelvic ultrasound was never done. A gynecology referral is required.

Hemoglobin response to iron (an expected rise of about 1-2 g/dL by 2-4 weeks) and a check for bleeding on anticoagulation with heavy menses: CBC in 2-5 weeks. Arithmetic: 2024-06-03 + 14 to 35 days = 2024-06-17 to 2024-07-08; the reference schedules day 28, 2024-07-01. An undated CBC is a baseline extra and does not satisfy this.

forbidden.why: Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily and rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily are reduced extended-phase (or prophylactic) doses used after at least 6 months of treatment; they are subtherapeutic for an acute proximal DVT.
Tranexamic acid is contraindicated in active thromboembolic disease (Lysteda label) and is avoided with an acute DVT.

Estrogen-containing contraception or hormone therapy is contraindicated after an estrogen-associated DVT (CDC US MEC category 4 for acute DVT); the combined pill was stopped in the emergency department and must not be restarted.
NSAIDs and antiplatelet agents with therapeutic anticoagulation increase major and menstrual bleeding (her ibuprofen was stopped); there is no antiplatelet indication for a venous thrombosis.

extras.why: A separate order for the apixaban maintenance dose (5 mg twice daily from day 8) belongs to the same regimen.
A separate order for the rivaroxaban maintenance dose (20 mg once daily with food from day 22) belongs to the same regimen.

Genetic thrombophilia tests are unaffected by the acute clot or anticoagulants; ASH 2023 suggests thrombophilia testing after VTE associated with hormonal contraception when results could change the duration decision. Not required.

Solid-phase antiphospholipid antibodies are not affected by anticoagulation; repeating them after a first thrombosis in a woman with two pregnancy losses is reasonable though not required (2023 confirmatory panel negative). Lupus anticoagulant testing on a DOAC is unreliable and is not listed.
Baseline coagulation tests before a DOAC are reasonable (already done on 2024-05-31).
A pregnancy test before starting anticoagulation is reasonable (urine test negative in the ED).
A levonorgestrel intrauterine system treats heavy menstrual bleeding on anticoagulation and provides contraception without raising thrombotic risk.
IUD placement or the pelvic ultrasound planned in January (never done) are reasonable.
Follow-up iron studies, and thyroid or von Willebrand testing in heavy menstrual bleeding, are reasonable.
Compression stockings for leg symptoms are reasonable.
