tasks.title: New Deep Vein Thrombosis: Long-Term Anticoagulation Visit
tasks.subject: New DVT: long-term anticoagulation decision today
tasks.request: Woman in her 40s with an acute left femoral-popliteal DVT on 5/31; combined pill stopped; given a 3-day parenteral bridge. She also has heavy periods and iron-deficiency anemia. Booked in your clinic on 6/3 to choose and start long-term anticoagulation and to address the bleeding and anemia.
facts: Confirmatory panel 2023-06-12 (16 weeks later, off anticoagulation): lupus anticoagulant detected
Acute occlusive DVT of the left femoral and popliteal veins on duplex (ED)
Estrogen-containing combined pill since January 2024, stopped in the ED
The single positive lupus anticoagulant was drawn during a heparin infusion (not interpretable)

required.why: The scanned 2023 confirmatory panel (2023-06-12, 16 weeks after the first test, off anticoagulation) shows lupus anticoagulant detected, anticardiolipin IgG 80 GPL and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I IgG 60 U/mL: persistent triple-positive antiphospholipid antibodies. With two unexplained second-trimester losses and now a proximal DVT, this is thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome with a high-risk antibody profile. EULAR 2019 and ISTH 2020: a vitamin K antagonist with target INR 2.0-3.0, long term; DOACs are not recommended (TRAPS trial; FDA labeling of apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban and dabigatran). The 2023 rheumatology impression (single lupus anticoagulant on heparin, not interpretable) is superseded. Start warfarin 5 mg once daily this evening (2.5-10 mg accepted), overlapping with a parenteral anticoagulant.

Warfarin needs a parenteral anticoagulant overlap for at least 5 days and until the INR is 2.0 or more for 24 hours (CHEST). The dose uses today's measured weight, 76.0 kg on the clinic scale; the ED used a stated 95 kg (enoxaparin 100 mg every 12 hours = 1.32 mg/kg of the true weight). Arithmetic: enoxaparin 1 mg/kg x 76 kg = 76 mg every 12 hours, given as 80 mg (accepted 70-80 mg twice daily), or 1.5 mg/kg x 76 kg = 114 mg once daily (accepted 110-120 mg). Accepted equivalents: fondaparinux 7.5 mg daily (50-100 kg band), dalteparin 200 IU/kg = 15,200 IU daily (14,000-16,000) or 100 IU/kg twice daily (7,000-8,000), tinzaparin 175 IU/kg = 13,300 IU daily (12,000-14,500).

After warfarin is started, the INR is checked after 2-3 doses (CHEST initiation guidance) to titrate the dose and to know when the parenteral bridge can stop; baseline INR was 1.0 on 2024-05-31. Arithmetic: 2024-06-03 + 2 to 5 days = 2024-06-05 to 2024-06-08; the reference schedules day 3, 2024-06-06.

Iron-deficiency anemia from heavy menstrual bleeding: hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, ferritin 5 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 5% on 2024-05-31 (ferritin 8 ng/mL in January); she never started iron, and anticoagulation will likely increase menstrual losses. Oral iron is first line: ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) once daily or on alternate days; equivalent salts, ferric maltol 30 mg or 60-120 mg elemental iron are accepted. Intravenous iron is also accepted because losses are ongoing and expected to rise on anticoagulation.
required.dose: 325 or 324 or 300 or 200 or 160 or 142 or 65 or 60 mg

required.why: Heavy menstrual bleeding (a pad every 1-2 hours on days 1-3, ferritin 5 ng/mL) is likely to worsen on anticoagulation (anticoagulant-associated abnormal uterine bleeding affects up to 70% of menstruating women). The estrogen-containing pill is stopped and must not restart, and tranexamic acid is avoided with an acute clot; ISTH guidance favours a levonorgestrel intrauterine system, which treats the bleeding and provides contraception without raising thrombotic risk. The planned pelvic ultrasound was never done. A gynecology referral is required. Warfarin is teratogenic, so reliable contraception is also needed.

Hemoglobin response to iron (an expected rise of about 1-2 g/dL by 2-4 weeks) and a check for bleeding on anticoagulation with heavy menses: CBC in 2-5 weeks. Arithmetic: 2024-06-03 + 14 to 35 days = 2024-06-17 to 2024-07-08; the reference schedules day 28, 2024-07-01. An undated CBC is a baseline extra and does not satisfy this.

forbidden.why: Thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome with triple positivity: DOACs carry an excess of thrombotic events compared with warfarin (TRAPS) and are not recommended (EULAR 2019, ISTH 2020, FDA labeling).

Enoxaparin 100 mg every 12 hours (the ED dose from a stated 95 kg) is 1.32 mg/kg of her measured 76 kg, a 32% overdose in a woman with heavy menstrual bleeding and anemia; 125 mg or more in one dose exceeds 1.5 mg/kg.
Tranexamic acid is contraindicated in active thromboembolic disease (Lysteda label) and is avoided with an acute DVT.

Estrogen-containing contraception or hormone therapy is contraindicated after an estrogen-associated DVT (CDC US MEC category 4 for acute DVT); the combined pill was stopped in the emergency department and must not be restarted.

NSAIDs and antiplatelet agents with therapeutic anticoagulation increase major and menstrual bleeding (her ibuprofen was stopped); in venous APS without arterial events, aspirin is not added to warfarin (EULAR 2019).

extras.why: A baseline or additional INR (every 2-3 days until therapeutic) is part of warfarin initiation.
Referral to an anticoagulation clinic for warfarin management is reasonable.
Screening for systemic lupus and rheumatology co-management are reasonable in newly recognised APS.
A pregnancy test before starting anticoagulation is reasonable (urine test negative in the ED).

tasks.title: Steatotic Liver Disease with Elevated Ferritin and Hyperbilirubinemia
tasks.subject: Elevated ferritin and bilirubin in fatty liver disease
tasks.request: Ferritin 642 ng/mL (H) and total bilirubin 2.0 mg/dL (H), collected 2024-05-21, in a patient with fatty liver disease referred to hepatology. Please review and place orders.
facts: Atorvastatin held for elevated enzymes; ALT still elevated 6 months later

required.why: MASLD with type 2 diabetes and FIB-4 about 1.5-1.7 (age 50-56, AST 46, ALT 58, platelets 195), which is indeterminate (1.3-2.67): AASLD 2023 MASLD practice guidance and the AGA pathway call for VCTE (or ELF or MR elastography) next.

Type 2 diabetes, age 50-56, LDL 148 mg/dL with hypertension and low HDL: ADA Standards of Care 2024 recommend statin therapy (moderate intensity at minimum, high intensity with additional risk factors). AASLD 2023 and EASL-EASD-EASO 2024 state statins are safe in MASLD and that transaminases below 3 times normal are not a reason to withhold them; ALT stayed elevated 6 months after atorvastatin was held, so the statin was not the cause.

forbidden.why: Transferrin saturation 32% (normal): the hyperferritinemia reflects metabolic inflammation (dysmetabolic hyperferritinemia), not iron overload; phlebotomy is not indicated (ACG 2019 hereditary hemochromatosis guideline; AASLD 2023).
No iron overload (normal transferrin saturation); chelation is not indicated.

tasks.title: Persistent Diarrhea Evaluation
tasks.subject: Stool and serology results final
tasks.request: Stool and serology results are final for a patient being evaluated for persistent diarrhea after travel. Please review and place any orders.
facts: Never screened for colorectal cancer, age 50-56

required.why: Total IgA 6 mg/dL (selective IgA deficiency) makes the negative tTG-IgA uninterpretable; ACG 2023 celiac guideline: use IgG-based serology (DGP-IgG or tTG-IgG), or proceed to upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies, which is also indicated for iron deficiency with chronic diarrhea (AGA 2020 iron deficiency anemia guideline).

Positive FIT in a woman over 50 never screened requires diagnostic colonoscopy (USMSTF); chronic watery diarrhea over 4 weeks with nocturnal stools, weight loss, low ferritin and raised calprotectin also calls for colonoscopy with random biopsies for microscopic colitis or IBD (AGA 2019 chronic diarrhea guidance).

forbidden.why: Pathogen PCR (including Giardia and Cryptosporidium), C. difficile PCR and ova and parasites are all negative; IDSA 2017 advises against empiric antimicrobial therapy for persistent watery diarrhea without an identified pathogen, and it would delay the diagnosis.

tasks.title: Post-GI Bleed Follow-Up Assessment
tasks.subject: Discharge follow-up: upper GI bleed
tasks.request: Discharged 2024-05-21 after an upper GI bleed. Gastric biopsy pathology is now final. Please review and arrange follow-up treatment.

required.why: H. pylori-positive bleeding duodenal ulcer: eradication is required (ACG 2021 upper GI bleeding and ACG 2024 H. pylori guidelines). Anaphylaxis to amoxicillin excludes every amoxicillin-containing regimen (clarithromycin triple, vonoprazan dual or triple, rifabutin triple, levofloxacin triple) and clarithromycin exposure in 2022 predicts resistance, leaving 14-day bismuth quadruple therapy: tetracycline 500 mg four times daily (or the combined bismuth-metronidazole-tetracycline capsule).
Bismuth quadruple therapy component: metronidazole 500 mg three or four times daily for 14 days (ACG 2024; Maastricht VI).
Bismuth quadruple therapy component: bismuth subsalicylate or subcitrate four times daily for 14 days, with the twice-daily PPI already prescribed (pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily).

Test of eradication with urea breath test or stool antigen at least 4 weeks after therapy and after a 2-week PPI pause is recommended for every treated patient, especially after an ulcer bleed (ACG 2024). Serology cannot document cure.

forbidden.why: Documented anaphylaxis to amoxicillin (1998).
Prior macrolide exposure (clarithromycin 2022): ACG 2024 advises against clarithromycin-based therapy unless susceptibility is known.
NSAID-associated ulcer bleed in a patient who needs aspirin for a coronary stent: NSAIDs, including COX-2 inhibitors, should be avoided.

tasks.title: Iron Overload Management in Transfusion-Dependent MDS
tasks.subject: Iron overload in transfusion-dependent MDS
tasks.request: MRI iron quantification is finalized for this transfusion-dependent MDS patient. Please advise on iron chelation and place the order if indicated; patient has concerns about treatment side effects.

required.why: Lower-risk MDS, about 52 units transfused, ferritin 3510 ng/mL and LIC 11.4 mg/g with good expected survival: chelation is indicated (NCCN MDS guideline: consider chelation for lower-risk MDS with ferritin >2500 and ongoing transfusions; FDA labels). Creatinine 0.9, normal liver tests and platelets 104 (>50) allow deferasirox, which also fits his oral preference; deferoxamine is an accepted alternative. Deferiprone is excluded because ANC 0.9 (agranulocytosis risk; label: do not start if ANC <1.5).

forbidden.why: Baseline ANC 0.9 x10^3/uL in MDS: deferiprone causes agranulocytosis and must not be started when ANC is below 1.5.
Documented ESA failure and endogenous EPO 845 mIU/mL (>500): an ESA is not expected to help (NCCN) and adds thrombotic risk.

tasks.title: Thrombocytopenia Evaluation in a Patient on Immunotherapy
tasks.subject: Platelet count 44 on immunotherapy
tasks.request: Platelets 44 x10^3/uL (L) on 2024-05-28, falling over 6 weeks, in a patient receiving pembrolizumab. Pembrolizumab held. Please evaluate the cause and advise on workup and management.
facts: Normal spleen size and liver on CT

required.why: Peripheral smear review is mandatory in new thrombocytopenia to exclude pseudothrombocytopenia (clumping) and schistocytes of a thrombotic microangiopathy before labeling immune thrombocytopenia (ASH 2019 ITP guideline; ASCO 2021 immune-related adverse event guideline).
Coagulation studies including fibrinogen and D-dimer to exclude disseminated intravascular coagulation in a patient with metastatic cancer (ISTH DIC criteria).

Hemoglobin fell from 14.1 to 12.4 with the platelet drop: LDH and haptoglobin (with reticulocytes and smear) screen for microangiopathic hemolysis (TMA, including immune-related TTP) and Evans syndrome.

forbidden.why: Platelets 44 x10^3/uL with only minor petechiae and no procedure: transfusion is not indicated (AABB prophylactic threshold 10 x10^3/uL) and is harmful if a thrombotic microangiopathy is present.
Same as above, entered through the medication composer.

tasks.title: Peripheral Neuropathy Workup and Symptom Management
tasks.subject: Progressive foot numbness and burning
tasks.request: Nine months of progressive numbness and burning in both feet with night pain. Initial labs in the chart. Please advise on the diagnostic workup and symptom treatment and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Bifascicular block with first degree AV block
Progressive with motor signs and hand involvement

required.why: Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation is part of the core screen for distal symmetric polyneuropathy (AAN practice parameter 2009) and has never been done; a monoclonal gammopathy is a treatable cause in this age group.

B12 238 pg/mL is low-normal (200-400 borderline zone) in a patient on long-term omeprazole with a positive Romberg: methylmalonic acid (or homocysteine) is needed to confirm or exclude B12 deficiency (AAN 2009; standard hematology practice). Repeating B12 alone adds nothing.

Progression over 9 months with hand involvement, distal motor weakness and reflex loss: nerve conduction studies with EMG are needed to confirm the polyneuropathy and separate axonal from demyelinating (e.g. CIDP, paraprotein-associated) forms, which changes treatment.

Painful neuropathy disturbing sleep warrants a first-line agent (AAN 2021 painful neuropathy guideline; NeuPSIG): an SNRI or gabapentinoid. Tricyclics are excluded by bifascicular block with first degree AV block (risk of higher-grade block).

forbidden.why: Bifascicular block with first degree AV block (QRS 138 ms, PR 236 ms): tricyclic antidepressants slow intraventricular conduction and can precipitate complete heart block.
Strong opioids are not recommended for newly evaluated neuropathic pain (AAN 2021, CDC 2022) and raise fall risk in a patient with sensory ataxia.

tasks.title: Inflammatory Arthritis Serologic Workup Before the First Rheumatology Visit
tasks.subject: New inflammatory polyarthritis with positive ANA
tasks.request: Inflammatory polyarthritis with positive ANA, negative RF and CCP; patient is currently pregnant. Please review before her first rheumatology appointment and order the additional workup you recommend.

required.why: Suspected systemic lupus (ANA 1:640, polyarthritis, oral ulcers, photosensitive rash, leukopenia, lymphopenia) in a pregnant patient: anti-Ro/SSA (and anti-La/SSB) must be tested early in pregnancy because of the risk of congenital heart block and neonatal lupus (ACR 2020 reproductive health guideline).

Antiphospholipid antibodies (anticardiolipin, anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I, lupus anticoagulant) are indicated in suspected SLE, particularly in pregnancy with a prior loss, because positivity changes antenatal management (ACR 2020 reproductive health guideline; EULAR/ACR 2019 SLE criteria).
Anti-dsDNA is a specific SLE antibody and a marker of disease activity, including renal and obstetric risk (EULAR/ACR 2019 SLE classification).
C3 and C4 levels are part of SLE classification and activity assessment (EULAR/ACR 2019).

forbidden.why: Patient is about 12 weeks pregnant: methotrexate, leflunomide, mycophenolate and cyclophosphamide are teratogenic and contraindicated (ACR 2020 reproductive health guideline).

tasks.title: Recurrent Knee Flares in an NSAID-Intolerant Older Patient
tasks.subject: Rheumatology consult finalized: recurrent knee flares
tasks.request: Consultation for recurrent inflammatory knee flares is finalized in the chart. Please review the recommendations and start the treatment plan.
facts: CPP crystals on aspirate with chondrocalcinosis
No recent medication changes (no interacting drugs)

required.why: Recurrent acute CPP crystal arthritis (4 flares/year) warrants low-dose colchicine prophylaxis (EULAR 2011 CPPD recommendations). Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is about 21 mL/min (age 80, 54 kg, creatinine 1.8): the colchicine label caps the prophylactic starting dose at 0.3 mg daily for CrCl <30, so 0.3 mg daily (or 0.6 mg every other day, the same weekly exposure) is correct; 0.6 mg daily or twice daily is an overdose.

forbidden.why: CKD stage 4 and prior NSAID-associated bleeding gastric ulcer (ACR 2019 OA guideline cautions; KDIGO: avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD). Topical diclofenac labeling also advises against use in advanced renal disease.
Methotrexate is contraindicated with creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min.

tasks.title: Recurrent Olecranon Bursitis in an Immunocompromised Patient
tasks.subject: Recurrent right elbow infection after antibiotics
tasks.request: Kidney transplant recipient with recurrent right olecranon swelling and fever 8 days after completing antibiotics for MSSA bursitis. Please evaluate and advise next steps.
facts: Joint motion preserved (bursitis, not septic arthritis)

required.why: Recurrence after a complete course with a fluctuant swelling means an undrained or loculated collection: cross-sectional imaging (ultrasound first; MRI or CT acceptable) defines the collection and excludes deeper extension or osteomyelitis. Only a radiograph was done before.

Septic bursitis that recurs after antibiotics in an immunosuppressed host needs repeat aspiration or surgical drainage/bursectomy with culture; antibiotics alone fail without source control (standard septic bursitis management, e.g. IDSA skin and soft tissue guidance on drainage of purulent collections).
Fever 38.3 C with recurrent S. aureus infection in a transplant recipient: blood cultures before antibiotics to exclude bacteremia, which would change duration and require further evaluation.

forbidden.why: Corticosteroid injection is contraindicated in septic bursitis and in this immunosuppressed host.
Same as above, entered as a procedure order.
Rifamycins sharply lower tacrolimus levels (rejection risk) and clarithromycin or erythromycin raise them (nephrotoxicity); not needed for beta-lactam-susceptible MSSA.

tasks.title: Dermatology eConsult: Persistent Rash Not Responding to Treatment
tasks.subject: Persistent rash despite topical treatment
tasks.request: Expanding itchy rash on both inner thighs, worse after 6 weeks of triamcinolone 0.1% cream, which I have stopped. The scraping result is in the chart. Please advise on the diagnosis and place the treatment order you recommend.
facts: KOH preparation shows branching septate hyphae
Plaque enlarged on triamcinolone, which was stopped
Annular plaque with advancing scaly border and central clearing

required.why: Annular plaque with an advancing scaly border, central clearing and border pustules that enlarged and spread on a topical corticosteroid, interdigital toe-web scaling and a KOH preparation showing branching septate hyphae establish steroid-modified tinea corporis (tinea incognito) with tinea pedis. Treatment is an antifungal: a topical allylamine or azole for limited disease (AAD/standard dermatology references); oral terbinafine or itraconazole is also acceptable after steroid exposure. Corticosteroids must stop.

forbidden.why: Any topical or systemic corticosteroid, including combination antifungal-corticosteroid products (e.g. clotrimazole-betamethasone), worsens and masks dermatophyte infection; the rash already progressed on triamcinolone.
Oral ketoconazole carries an FDA boxed warning (hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, adrenal insufficiency) and must not be used for skin dermatophyte infections.

tasks.title: Skin Rash Evaluation and Treatment
tasks.subject: Painful rash on the left chest
tasks.request: Patient seen today by the resident for a painful rash on the left chest and back that appeared two days ago. Please confirm the diagnosis and place the treatment orders.
facts: Grouped vesicles in the left T5 dermatome

required.why: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base in a single unilateral T5 dermatome after a painful prodrome is acute herpes zoster; onset within 72 hours and age over 50 warrant oral antiviral therapy. Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is about 21-24 mL/min (age 68-76, 63 kg, creatinine 2.2, female), so labeled renal adjustment applies: valacyclovir 1 g every 24 hours (CrCl 10-29), acyclovir 800 mg every 8 hours (CrCl 10-25) or famciclovir 500 mg every 24 hours (CrCl 20-39). Full doses accumulate in CKD and cause neurotoxicity.

forbidden.why: NSAIDs are contraindicated in CKD stage 4 (risk of acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia); nephrology advised avoidance.

Unadjusted zoster dosing (valacyclovir 1 g three times daily, acyclovir 800 mg five times daily, famciclovir 500 mg three times daily) at CrCl about 22 mL/min risks acyclovir neurotoxicity and acute kidney injury.

tasks.title: Pruritic Papular Rash Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Itchy rash not improving
tasks.request: Five weeks of intensely itchy rash, not better with triamcinolone cream. Examined by the physician assistant today. Please complete the evaluation and place treatment orders.
facts: Burrows in finger web spaces and wrists

required.why: Nocturnal itch, burrows in the finger webs and wrists, papules at typical sites, a dermoscopic delta-wing sign and itchy household contacts establish classic scabies (IACS 2020 criteria); there are no crusted features, and normal bile acids make intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy unlikely. A topical scabicide is required: permethrin 5% cream is the drug of choice in pregnancy (CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021); precipitated sulfur ointment is an accepted pregnancy alternative. The topical corticosteroid did not treat the cause.

forbidden.why: Ivermectin safety in pregnancy is not established and it is not recommended for pregnant patients (CDC); topical permethrin is preferred.
Lindane carries an FDA boxed warning for neurotoxicity, is second-line only and is not recommended in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

tasks.title: Chronic Urticaria Management Plan
tasks.subject: Chronic hives not controlled
tasks.request: Near-daily hives for about 5 months that return after each prednisone course and are not controlled on the current antihistamine. Please assess and start a long-term treatment plan.
facts: Standard-dose cetirizine 10 mg daily, adherent, partial relief
Hydroxyzine caused acute urinary retention (950 mL)

required.why: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (over 6 weeks, wheals under 24 hours without bruising, normal CRP/ESR, no systemic features) with UAS7 28 despite adherent standard-dose cetirizine: the next guideline step is a second-generation H1 antihistamine increased to 2-4 times the standard dose (EAACI/GA2LEN/EuroGuiDerm/APAAACI 2021; AAAAI/ACAAI practice parameter). Accepted: total daily dose 2-4x standard, e.g. fexofenadine 180 mg two to four times daily or cetirizine 10 mg two to four times daily. Re-ordering the standard once-daily dose does not satisfy this step. Repeated systemic corticosteroid courses are not a maintenance strategy.

forbidden.why: Hydroxyzine precipitated acute urinary retention (950 mL) with benign prostatic hyperplasia and caused next-morning sedation; first-generation and anticholinergic antihistamines (including doxepin) are unsafe for this patient and for a commercial bus driver, and guidelines do not recommend them for chronic urticaria.

tasks.title: Travel-Related Parasitic Infection Evaluation
tasks.subject: Eosinophilia after work abroad
tasks.request: Persistent eosinophilia and a recurrent itchy rash after 3 years of work in Vietnam; stool O&P negative x3. Please evaluate and advise on further testing and treatment.
facts: Barefoot soil exposure in northern Vietnam 2020-2023
Migratory rash moving over hours (larva currens)

required.why: Persistent eosinophilia, high IgE, recurrent migratory serpiginous rash on the buttocks and thighs that moves over hours (larva currens), GI and respiratory symptoms after years of barefoot soil exposure in Southeast Asia indicate chronic strongyloidiasis. Stool O&P has low sensitivity for Strongyloides, so three negative specimens do not exclude it; Strongyloides serology (or another Strongyloides-specific test) is indicated (CDC; IDSA/ASTMH guidance).

High pretest probability and a pending decision about systemic corticosteroids justify treatment now: ivermectin 200 mcg/kg (72 kg = 14.4 mg, given as 15 mg per the 66-79 kg weight band) daily for 1-2 days (CDC). No Loa loa exposure (never in sub-Saharan Africa), so ivermectin is safe.

forbidden.why: Systemic corticosteroids in untreated strongyloidiasis can precipitate hyperinfection syndrome and disseminated disease, which is often fatal.

tasks.title: Opioid Use Disorder in a Patient on Long-Term Opioid Therapy: Treatment Initiation
tasks.subject: Long-term opioid therapy: request to start addiction treatment
tasks.request: Patient on long-term oxycodone for back pain meets criteria for opioid use disorder and asks for help stopping oxycodone. Please evaluate and start medication treatment.
facts: Daily full agonist: oxycodone 15 mg four times daily
Urine drug screen negative for fentanyl
Cannot attend a clinic daily (office-based treatment)

required.why: Moderate opioid use disorder (5 DSM-5 criteria) in a patient on daily oxycodone who cannot attend a clinic daily and wants analgesia: office-based sublingual buprenorphine (preferably buprenorphine-naloxone) is first-line (ASAM 2020 National Practice Guideline; SAMHSA TIP 63). Methadone for OUD is dispensed only through an opioid treatment program and prolongs QTc (QTc 492 ms); naltrexone requires 7-10 opioid-free days and blocks analgesia. Accepted doses are SL induction or day-1/maintenance amounts in mg (including low-dose induction steps and Zubsolv strengths); transdermal or buccal pain formulations dosed in mcg do not satisfy this requirement.
required.dose: 0.5 or 1 or 2 or 4 or 6 or 8 or 12 or 16 or 1.4 or 2.9 or 5.7 or 8.6 or 11.4 mg

forbidden.why: Daily full-agonist use: naltrexone would precipitate withdrawal (requires 7-10 opioid-free days) and blocks analgesia for his chronic pain.
QTc 492 ms with cardiology advice to avoid QT-prolonging drugs; methadone for opioid use disorder cannot be prescribed from an office practice (opioid treatment program only).

tasks.title: Anxiety and Depression Medication Plan After SSRI Intolerance
tasks.subject: Adverse reaction to anxiety medication
tasks.request: Patient stopped citalopram because of side effects and still has anxiety and low mood. Please review and advise on an alternative medication plan.
facts: Oncologist: avoid moderate or strong CYP2D6 inhibitors
Citalopram 20 mg stopped for GI upset and activation

required.why: GAD with moderate depression after intolerance (GI upset, activation) to citalopram 20 mg, in a woman on adjuvant tamoxifen whose oncologist asks to avoid moderate or strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (NCCN survivorship guidance; FDA CYP2D6 inhibitor classification). Venlafaxine is preferred (minimal CYP2D6 inhibition, treats anxiety, depression and tamoxifen hot flashes); desvenlafaxine, mirtazapine or low-dose escitalopram are acceptable. Conservative start after an activation reaction: venlafaxine 37.5-75 mg, desvenlafaxine 25-50 mg, mirtazapine 7.5-15 mg; escitalopram only 5 mg because 10 mg is equivalent to the citalopram 20 mg that was not tolerated.

forbidden.why: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors reduce conversion of tamoxifen to endoxifen; the oncologist documented that they must be avoided.
Duloxetine is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor; the oncologist asked to avoid moderate or strong CYP2D6 inhibitors with tamoxifen.

tasks.title: Erectile Dysfunction and Premature Ejaculation: Results Review and Treatment
tasks.subject: Hormone results for sexual dysfunction follow-up
tasks.request: Morning testosterone (two samples), LH, prolactin, TSH and PSA resulted for a patient seen for erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation. Please review and complete the treatment plan.
facts: On doxazosin 4 mg with prior orthostatic symptoms
Acquired premature ejaculation after ED onset

required.why: Organic ED with normal morning testosterone on two occasions, LH, prolactin and TSH: a PDE5 inhibitor is first-line (AUA Erectile Dysfunction guideline 2018). He takes doxazosin, a non-selective alpha-blocker, and had orthostatic symptoms on titration; all PDE5 inhibitor labels advise starting at the lowest dose in men on stable alpha-blocker therapy (sildenafil 25 mg, or one 20 mg generic tablet; tadalafil 2.5-5 mg; vardenafil 5 mg or lower; avanafil 50 mg). Acquired premature ejaculation secondary to ED is managed by treating the ED first plus behavioral counseling (AUA/ISSM).

forbidden.why: Morning total testosterone 468 and 512 ng/dL with normal LH: eugonadal; testosterone (or clomiphene) is not indicated for ED in eugonadal men (AUA testosterone deficiency guideline).

tasks.title: Oligomenorrhea and Hyperandrogenism: Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Irregular menses and hirsutism: gynecology evaluation
tasks.request: Menses every 45-90 days with hirsutism; initial labs and pelvic ultrasound are in the chart. Please complete the evaluation and start management.

required.why: Hyperandrogenism (testosterone 71 ng/dL, mFG 14) with oligomenorrhea: non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia must be excluded with an early-morning follicular 17-hydroxyprogesterone before PCOS is confirmed (Endocrine Society hirsutism guideline 2018; International PCOS guideline 2023). TSH, prolactin and FSH are already normal.

All women with PCOS need glycemic assessment at diagnosis; with BMI 30.9 a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test is preferred, A1c or fasting glucose acceptable (International PCOS guideline 2023; ACOG Practice Bulletin 194). Lipids are already done.

Four to five cycles per year (endometrial thickness 9 mm, last menses over 3 months ago) needs endometrial protection. Migraine with aura makes estrogen-containing contraception US MEC category 4, so a progestin is indicated: cyclic oral progestin (medroxyprogesterone 10 mg or norethindrone acetate 5 mg for 10-14 days monthly, or micronized progesterone), a levonorgestrel IUD or a progestin-only pill (US MEC 2024; ACOG Practice Bulletin 194).

forbidden.why: Migraine with aura: estrogen-containing contraception is US MEC category 4 (unacceptable stroke risk).

tasks.title: Osteoporosis With Hypercalcemia: Metabolic Evaluation and Treatment Planning
tasks.subject: Osteoporosis with vertebral fracture and high calcium
tasks.request: New osteoporosis with a T12 compression fracture and persistent high calcium. Please advise on the evaluation and osteoporosis treatment, and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: PTH-dependent hypercalcemia (calcium 10.9-11.0 with normal albumin, PTH 94, low-normal phosphorus, vitamin D replete, persistent off thiazide): primary hyperparathyroidism. A 24-hour urine calcium with creatinine is needed to exclude familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia and to assess hypercalciuria (Fifth International Workshop on asymptomatic PHPT, 2022).

Osteoporosis (T-score -3.4 at the one-third radius, -2.9 at the spine) and a vertebral fracture are each indications for parathyroidectomy in primary hyperparathyroidism (Fifth International Workshop, 2022; AAES guideline 2016).

forbidden.why: Teriparatide and abaloparatide are contraindicated in hypercalcemia and hyperparathyroidism (labeling).
Thiazides and active vitamin D raise serum calcium in a patient with hypercalcemia of 11.0 mg/dL.

tasks.title: Declining Kidney Function in a Patient on HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis
tasks.subject: Rising creatinine on HIV PrEP
tasks.request: Creatinine 1.66 mg/dL (eGFR 51) and rising on daily oral PrEP, which was held on 5/29. Please evaluate his kidney function, complete the workup, and advise on and order HIV prevention that is safe for his kidneys.
facts: Cystatin C 1.42 mg/L confirms reduced GFR

required.why: Progressive decline to eGFR 51 (creatinine 1.66, cystatin C-based eGFR 52 confirms) with normoglycemic glycosuria, hypophosphatemia, low bicarbonate and protein/creatinine ratio far exceeding albuminuria: tenofovir disoproxil (TDF)-associated proximal tubulopathy. HIV prevention is still indicated (ongoing condomless receptive anal sex, recent rectal STI). CDC 2021 PrEP guideline: TDF/FTC is not recommended for CrCl <60 mL/min; F/TAF (approved for men who have sex with men, CrCl >=30) or long-acting injectable cabotegravir (no renal adjustment) are the options. HIV test negative 6 days before; HBsAg negative.

New CKD G3a (eGFR <60 for over 3 months) with no prior kidney imaging: KDIGO 2024 CKD evaluation includes kidney ultrasound (size, echogenicity, obstruction, structural disease) even when a drug cause is likely.

forbidden.why: TDF-containing PrEP (at any dosing interval) is not recommended with CrCl <60 mL/min and has caused proximal tubulopathy in this patient.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult
tasks.subject: Ambulatory ECG patch report finalized
tasks.request: The 14-day ambulatory ECG patch report is finalized for a patient referred for palpitations and smartwatch irregular-rhythm alerts. Please review and manage.
facts: Short PR 98 ms with delta wave
Ventricular rate up to 262 bpm in AF

required.why: Manifest pre-excitation (PR 98 ms, delta wave) with pre-excited atrial fibrillation, ventricular rates to 262 bpm and shortest pre-excited R-R 230 ms (<=250 ms, high-risk accessory pathway): 2015 ACC/AHA/HRS SVT and 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guidelines recommend electrophysiology study and catheter ablation of the accessory pathway (Class 1).

Transthoracic echocardiogram for new atrial fibrillation (2023 AF guideline) and to exclude structural disease associated with pre-excitation (Ebstein anomaly, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy); never done.

forbidden.why: AV nodal blocking drugs (beta-blockers, diltiazem, verapamil, digoxin, adenosine) can accelerate conduction over the accessory pathway in pre-excited AF and precipitate ventricular fibrillation (2015 SVT guideline Class 3: Harm).
CHA2DS2-VASc 0 in a young man: oral anticoagulation and antiplatelet therapy are not indicated for stroke prevention.

tasks.title: Unilateral Pulsatile Tinnitus: Diagnostic Evaluation
tasks.subject: Left pulsatile tinnitus
tasks.request: Two months of constant left-sided pulsatile tinnitus. Please evaluate and order the indicated workup.

required.why: Pulse-synchronous unilateral tinnitus with normal otoscopy needs vascular imaging of the head and neck (ACR Appropriateness Criteria: CTA or MRA/MRV usually appropriate) to exclude dural arteriovenous fistula, venous sinus stenosis or diverticulum, and carotid disease; suppression by ipsilateral jugular compression suggests a venous source. Prior anaphylaxis to iodinated contrast makes MR angiography/venography (time-of-flight or gadolinium, no cross-reactivity) the appropriate modality; no MRI contraindication and normal renal function.
Comprehensive audiometry is part of every tinnitus evaluation (AAO-HNSF tinnitus guideline) and directs further imaging; none has been done.

forbidden.why: Documented anaphylaxis (hypotension 78/40, epinephrine required) to iodinated contrast; an equally appropriate non-iodinated modality exists (ACR Manual on Contrast Media).

tasks.title: Acute Urinary Retention: Catheter Management and Workup
tasks.subject: Urinary retention with indwelling catheter
tasks.request: Acute urinary retention on 5/24; indwelling catheter in place; on tamsulosin. Please evaluate, place orders for catheter management and the indicated workup, and advise on his bladder symptoms and the PSA result.
facts: Oxybutynin started 18 days before the retention
Prostate volume about 58 mL, no hydronephrosis

required.why: Precipitated acute urinary retention (oxybutynin and diphenhydramine on a background of benign prostatic enlargement, 58 mL) with resolved obstructive AKI, no hydronephrosis, no infection or hematuria, and 7-10 days of an alpha-blocker: trial without catheter with post-void residual measurement is the next step (EAU non-neurogenic male LUTS guideline; alpha-blocker for at least 2-3 days before TWOC increases success).

forbidden.why: Antimuscarinics precipitated this retention and are contraindicated in urinary retention; they should not be restarted while bladder outlet obstruction is untreated.

PSA 9.6 was drawn during acute retention after catheterization (prior 2.1, smooth benign-feeling gland) and is unreliable; repeat PSA at least 6 weeks after catheter removal before any biopsy decision (AUA/SUO early detection guideline).

tasks.title: Substitution of Travel Thromboprophylaxis Unavailable in the United States
tasks.subject: Substitute for travel thromboprophylaxis
tasks.request: He needs a US-available substitute for the anticoagulant injection he used before long-haul flights (danaparoid, prescribed in the United Kingdom). Next flight 6/20. Please review and order an appropriate substitute.
facts: Danaparoid not available in the US

required.why: Serologically and functionally confirmed heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with thrombosis after enoxaparin (2020): all heparins including LMWH must be avoided (ASH 2018 HIT guideline: in patients with a history of HIT, use a non-heparin anticoagulant such as fondaparinux for VTE prophylaxis). Prior VTE plus frequent long-haul flights is substantially increased travel risk (ASH 2018 VTE prophylaxis guideline; he used situational prophylaxis successfully). Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC daily is the prophylactic dose for weight >=50 kg (84 kg) with CrCl >=30 (creatinine 0.92). Prophylactic-dose DOACs (rivaroxaban 10 mg daily, apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily) are also accepted as non-heparin options (widened conservatively by the tier editor; confirm in review).

forbidden.why: History of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with thrombosis triggered by enoxaparin: unfractionated heparin and all LMWHs are contraindicated.
Weight-based fondaparinux 5-10 mg is the treatment dose; prophylaxis is 2.5 mg.

tasks.title: Thyroid Medication Management and Follow-up Planning
tasks.subject: Abnormal thyroid function results
tasks.request: TSH 9.4 mIU/L (H) and free T4 0.8 ng/dL (L), collected 2024-05-30, for a patient on levothyroxine. Please review.
facts: TSH 9.4 mIU/L (H) with free T4 0.8 on 2024-05-30
TSH 2.3 on the same 75 mcg dose in December 2023

required.why: TSH rose from 2.3 to 9.4 on an unchanged, adherently taken dose after calcium carbonate was started and swallowed together with levothyroxine: impaired absorption is the likely cause. Separate the two by at least 4 hours and recheck TSH (with or without free T4) in 6-8 weeks before considering a dose change.

forbidden.why: The rise is explained by calcium co-administration; increasing the dose before correcting the timing risks over-replacement once absorption normalizes.
forbidden.dose: 88 or 100 or 112 or 125 or 137 or 150 mcg

forbidden.why: T3-containing therapy is not indicated for impaired levothyroxine absorption.

extras.why: Re-issuing the unchanged 75 mcg dose with updated administration instructions (alone, fasting, 4 hours before calcium).
Re-prescribing the calcium/vitamin D supplement with instructions to take it at least 4 hours after levothyroxine (e.g., with the evening meal).
Free T4 as a separate follow-up order alongside TSH.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: Stroke Prevention and Initial Evaluation
tasks.subject: New atrial fibrillation: stroke prevention and workup
tasks.request: Newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation on ECG 5/24, now on metoprolol for rate control. Please evaluate stroke prevention and complete the initial atrial fibrillation workup.
facts: Birth date gives age 81-84 (80 or older)

required.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (age >=75, female, hypertension, diabetes) with low bleeding risk: a DOAC is indicated. Apixaban dose reduction needs 2 of age >=80, weight <=60 kg, creatinine >=1.5 mg/dL; she is 81-84 years old and weighs 58 kg (creatinine 0.9), so 2 criteria are met: 2.5 mg twice daily. Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about 42-45 mL/min gives rivaroxaban 15 mg daily or edoxaban 30 mg daily; dabigatran 150 mg twice daily (US label, CrCl >30) or 110 mg twice daily (ESC, age >=80).
Transthoracic echocardiogram for new atrial fibrillation (structure, valves, LV function).
Thyroid function testing in new atrial fibrillation; none in 3 years.

forbidden.why: No antiplatelet indication; adding one to anticoagulation raises bleeding risk.
Two apixaban dose-reduction criteria are met (age >=80 and weight <=60 kg); 5 mg twice daily would overdose.
CrCl about 42-45 mL/min requires rivaroxaban 15 mg or edoxaban 30 mg; the full doses would overdose.

extras.why: Repeat 12-lead ECG to confirm rate control (one is already on the chart).
Ambulatory monitoring to assess rate control or burden.
Cardiovascular risk-factor labs in new atrial fibrillation.

tasks.title: Migraine Classification and Preventive Treatment Plan
tasks.subject: Headache: preventive treatment consult
tasks.request: Increasing migraine frequency despite triptan. Please advise on and start preventive treatment, and advise whether imaging is needed.
facts: No red flags; normal neurological exam

forbidden.why: Moderate persistent asthma with prior bronchospasm from a topical beta-blocker.
Recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis with hypocitraturia.
Opioids and butalbital are not recommended for migraine and promote medication-overuse headache.
2-3 migraine days per month without disability and with an effective, non-overused acute treatment: preventive therapy is not indicated (AHS consensus thresholds); starting one is over-treatment.

extras.why: Refill of the effective triptan (or an alternative triptan) for acute treatment, limited to under 10 days per month.
NSAID for acute treatment; ibuprofen previously tolerated despite asthma.
Antiemetic adjunct for migraine-associated nausea.

tasks.title: Microcytic Anemia in Pregnancy: Hematology eConsult
tasks.subject: Microcytic anemia in pregnancy
tasks.request: Microcytic anemia at prenatal intake (12 weeks). Please advise on the evaluation and treatment, and place any orders you recommend.

required.why: New microcytosis (MCV 74, previously 88) with ferritin 9 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 6%, high RDW 17.2% and low RBC 4.1 (Mentzer index about 18) in a first-trimester pregnancy with prior heavy menses: iron-deficiency anemia. The prenatal vitamin (27 mg iron) is insufficient; ACOG recommends therapeutic oral iron (about 60-120 mg elemental iron daily, or alternate-day dosing) first line. Accepted at standard tablet strengths of the common iron salts or as 60-120 mg elemental iron.
required.dose: 325 or 324 or 300 or 200 or 160 or 142 or 65 or 60 mg

forbidden.why: Mild anemia (Hb 10.2) in the first trimester with no trial of therapeutic oral iron: oral iron is first line; parenteral iron is reserved for intolerance or non-response and is generally avoided in the first trimester.
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL in an asymptomatic patient does not warrant transfusion.

extras.why: Hemoglobinopathy screening is reasonable given the brother's inherited blood condition and the untested partner, but not required: iron deficiency explains the new microcytosis.
Follow-up iron studies or reticulocyte count to document the response to iron.
Folate and B12 levels for possible combined deficiency (high RDW, vegetarian diet).

tasks.title: Type 2 Diabetes Treatment Intensification
tasks.subject: Diabetes intensification
tasks.request: A1c 8.6%; metformin was stopped by nephrology. Please recommend and start the next glucose-lowering medicine.
facts: No pancreatitis, medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2

required.why: Type 2 diabetes above target with ischemic cardiomyopathy (HFrEF, EF 30%) and CKD stage 4 (eGFR 18, stable 19-18): SGLT2 inhibitor initiation is not recommended below eGFR 20 (KDIGO 2022, ADA 2024; empagliflozin label), and metformin is contraindicated below eGFR 30. A GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven cardiovascular benefit (subcutaneous semaglutide, dulaglutide or liraglutide) needs no renal dose adjustment and is the recommended agent.

forbidden.why: Thiazolidinediones cause fluid retention and are contraindicated in symptomatic heart failure.
Saxagliptin and alogliptin carry an increased heart-failure hospitalization signal.
SGLT2 inhibitor initiation is not recommended at eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73m2 (eGFR 18).
Metformin is contraindicated at eGFR below 30 and was stopped by nephrology.
Exenatide is not recommended with CrCl below 30 mL/min (renally cleared).
Glyburide has active renally cleared metabolites and causes prolonged hypoglycemia in CKD stage 4.

extras.why: Follow-up A1c in 3 months.
Urine albumin/creatinine ratio monitoring in diabetic kidney disease.
Retinal examination when starting semaglutide (retinopathy-worsening signal with rapid A1c lowering).
Glucose self-monitoring supplies.

tasks.title: Tinnitus and Audiology Follow-up
tasks.subject: Audiology results available
tasks.request: Audiogram and speech testing completed 2024-05-21. Report is in the chart.
facts: Symmetric thresholds (interaural difference 5 dB or less at 2-4 kHz)

required.why: Persistent, bothersome bilateral tinnitus with documented bilateral symmetric high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and communication difficulty: AAO-HNS tinnitus guideline recommends a hearing aid evaluation (audiology referral).

forbidden.why: Bilateral non-pulsatile tinnitus with symmetric hearing loss, symmetric word recognition and a normal neurological examination: imaging is not indicated (AAO-HNS tinnitus guideline).
Gradual, symmetric loss over months is not sudden sensorineural hearing loss; systemic steroids are not indicated.

extras.why: Otolaryngology evaluation is reasonable for bothersome tinnitus with hearing loss, though not required.
Cognitive behavioral therapy or tinnitus counseling for persistent bothersome tinnitus (AAO-HNS option).

tasks.title: Methotrexate Refill Request in Rheumatoid Arthritis
tasks.subject: Refill request: methotrexate 2.5 mg tablets
tasks.request: Refill requested for methotrexate 2.5 mg tablets, 6 tablets (15 mg) by mouth once weekly, #24. Last filled 2024-05-04. Please authorize.

forbidden.why: New pancytopenia (WBC 2.4, ANC 1.1, platelets 88, Hb 10.8) with mucositis and ALT 3x ULN after a trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole course: methotrexate must be held, not refilled, at any dose or route.
Starting another myelosuppressive or hepatotoxic DMARD during active cytopenia and transaminitis is unsafe.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole precipitated the antifolate toxicity; re-exposure is contraindicated with methotrexate.

extras.why: Leucovorin rescue is reasonable for methotrexate-associated cytopenia with mucositis.
Continuing or renewing folic acid supplementation.
Smear or reticulocyte count in the evaluation of new cytopenias.
Viral hepatitis serology in the evaluation of a new ALT elevation.

tasks.title: Knee Osteoarthritis Pain: Patient Medication Request
tasks.subject: Knee pain - can I get naproxen?
tasks.request: My right knee has been worse this past month and the Tylenol is not cutting it. A friend takes naproxen (Aleve) for her arthritis and says it works great. Could you please send a prescription for naproxen 500 mg to my pharmacy?
facts: Prior duodenal ulcer hemorrhage requiring transfusion
Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 knee osteoarthritis, partial response to acetaminophen

forbidden.why: Systemic NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors and salicylates) are unsafe: CKD stage 4 (eGFR 28), therapeutic warfarin, and a prior ibuprofen-associated duodenal ulcer hemorrhage requiring transfusion.
Ketorolac by any route carries the highest renal and gastrointestinal bleeding risk and is contraindicated with eGFR 28, anticoagulation and prior GI bleeding.

extras.why: Acetaminophen up to 3 g/day remains the safest systemic analgesic here (monitor INR with regular use).
Topical NSAID for knee osteoarthritis (ACR strong recommendation); minimal systemic absorption, acceptable with caution here.
Topical capsaicin for knee osteoarthritis.
Exercise-based physical therapy is first-line for knee osteoarthritis and has not been tried.
Intra-articular corticosteroid injection or orthopedic/sports medicine evaluation.
INR check when acetaminophen use is regular in a patient on warfarin.

tasks.title: Acute Respiratory Symptoms: Patient Request for Treatment
tasks.subject: Still sick - need antibiotics
tasks.request: I have had a sore throat, cough and stuffy nose since Thursday and now the mucus is turning yellow-green. Last time a Z-Pak cleared up the same thing in a couple of days. I have a big presentation on Friday. Can you please send antibiotics to my pharmacy?
facts: No chronic lung disease or immunosuppression

forbidden.why: Four days of cough, rhinorrhea and sore throat, afebrile, normal lung exam, no exudate or tender nodes and a negative rapid strep test: an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection, for which antibiotics give no benefit and cause harm. Colored mucus does not indicate bacterial infection.

extras.why: Analgesic/antipyretic for sore throat and malaise.
Symptomatic cough treatment.
Decongestant, antihistamine-decongestant or nasal saline/ipratropium for rhinorrhea and congestion.
Topical throat analgesic.
Respiratory viral testing.

tasks.title: Early Refill Request for a Controlled Substance
tasks.subject: Early refill request: alprazolam 0.5 mg
tasks.request: Patient requests an early refill of alprazolam 0.5 mg tablets, 1 tablet three times daily as needed, #90. Last filled 2024-05-15 (30-day supply). Patient reports the bottle was lost. Please authorize or deny.

forbidden.why: Oversedation with respiratory depression reversed by naloxone on 2024-05-24 while on oxycodone plus extra alprazolam, urine confirmation of non-prescribed clonazepam, a reported lost bottle and an agreement prohibiting early refills: no early refill and no additional benzodiazepine.
Z-drug hypnotics add the same respiratory-depression risk with opioids after an overdose event.
Other sedative CNS depressants are unsafe with long-term opioids after an oversedation event.

extras.why: Naloxone co-prescription after an overdose (already dispensed by the ED; re-prescribing is reasonable).
An SSRI/SNRI at a standard starting dose (or buspirone) as non-benzodiazepine treatment of panic disorder.
Behavioral health, addiction medicine or pain medicine referral.
Repeat urine drug testing under the controlled-substance agreement.

tasks.title: Positive Rapid Strep Test: Treatment Decision
tasks.subject: Positive rapid strep test
tasks.request: Group A Streptococcus rapid antigen test POSITIVE on a throat swab collected 2024-06-03 for a patient seen in the walk-in clinic this morning. No antibiotic has been prescribed yet. Please review and treat.
facts: Rapid antigen test positive for group A Streptococcus
Centor score 4, no peritonsillar abscess signs
Anaphylaxis to amoxicillin in 2016 with hypotension

required.why: Group A streptococcal pharyngitis (Centor 4, positive rapid antigen test) warrants antibiotic therapy. With documented penicillin anaphylaxis, IDSA 2012 recommends a non-beta-lactam agent: azithromycin (500 mg day 1 then 250 mg days 2-5, or 12 mg/kg max 500 mg daily for 5 days), clindamycin 300 mg three times daily for 10 days, or clarithromycin 250 mg twice daily for 10 days. First-generation cephalosporins are reserved for non-anaphylactic penicillin allergy.

forbidden.why: Documented anaphylaxis to amoxicillin (2016, hypotension, epinephrine): penicillins and aminopenicillins are contraindicated.
IDSA 2012 limits first-generation cephalosporins to patients without anaphylactic penicillin allergy; these agents also share or resemble the amoxicillin/ampicillin R1 side chain.

extras.why: Symptomatic analgesic or antipyretic is reasonable adjunctive care for pharyngitis.
Renewing the epinephrine auto-injector is reasonable in a patient with documented anaphylaxis.
Back-up culture is unnecessary after a positive rapid test in an adult but harmless.
Mononucleosis testing is low-yield here but a tolerated extra.

tasks.title: Outpatient Community-Acquired Pneumonia Treatment
tasks.subject: Chest radiograph: right lower lobe pneumonia
tasks.request: PA/lateral chest radiograph 2024-06-03: right lower lobe consolidation consistent with pneumonia. The patient was seen in clinic this morning and is waiting at home; no antibiotic has been prescribed yet. Please review and treat.
facts: Right lower lobe consolidation on radiograph
No comorbidities, no antibiotics in 3 months

required.why: Outpatient CAP (CURB-65 0) in an adult without IDSA/ATS 2019 comorbidities and without recent antibiotics: amoxicillin 1 g three times daily, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, or a macrolide where pneumococcal macrolide resistance is below 25% (regional 18%). Azithromycin has no relevant CYP3A4 interaction with simvastatin; clarithromycin and erythromycin are contraindicated with simvastatin. Amoxicillin-clavulanate is broader than needed but accepted.

forbidden.why: Clarithromycin and erythromycin are strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors; with simvastatin 40 mg they are contraindicated (rhabdomyolysis risk) and safe alternatives exist.

extras.why: Sputum culture is not routinely needed for outpatient CAP but is a tolerated extra.
Viral testing is reasonable during respiratory illness.
A follow-up radiograph is optional but harmless.
Low-risk additional laboratory test.
Antipyretic or analgesic for symptoms.

tasks.title: Knee Osteoarthritis Pain Management in an Older Adult
tasks.subject: Orthopedic evaluation finalized: bilateral knee osteoarthritis
tasks.request: Orthopedic evaluation of bilateral knee osteoarthritis is finalized. Not a surgical candidate at present. Please review and update the pharmacologic pain plan.
facts: Prior NSAID ulcer bleed, avoid oral NSAIDs
Duloxetine stopped for dizziness and fall

required.why: Symptomatic knee OA after acetaminophen failure, duloxetine intolerance (dizziness, fall) and only brief benefit from an intra-articular steroid; she declines opioids and oral NSAIDs are ruled out by a prior NSAID ulcer bleed. ACR 2019 strongly recommends topical NSAIDs for knee OA, and AGS guidance prefers them over oral NSAIDs in older adults because systemic exposure is low. The Beers drug-age alert targets systemic NSAID use and is acknowledged and overridden for topical diclofenac.

forbidden.why: Prior NSAID-associated duodenal ulcer bleed requiring transfusion (2021); gastroenterology advised avoiding oral NSAIDs indefinitely. COX-2 selective agents are included given age 72+ and bleed history.
Duloxetine was stopped in October 2023 after dizziness and a fall.

extras.why: Topical capsaicin is conditionally recommended for knee OA (ACR 2019).
Repeat intra-articular corticosteroid injection (no sooner than 3 months after the last) is strongly recommended for knee OA.
Exercise therapy is a core strongly recommended intervention.
A cane or knee brace is recommended for knee OA.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: Cardiology Follow-up
tasks.subject: Echocardiogram result for new atrial fibrillation
tasks.request: Transthoracic echocardiogram 2024-05-31 for new atrial fibrillation (ED visit 2024-05-27) is final. The patient is in clinic today for cardiology follow-up; no rate-control or antithrombotic therapy has been started. Please review and manage.
facts: ED suggested oral diltiazem pending echo (trap)

required.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age 65-74, hypertension, heart failure) warrants oral anticoagulation; a DOAC is preferred. Full doses apply (age under 80, weight 88 kg, creatinine 1.0, estimated CrCl about 85 mL/min). The 2013 GI bleed was hemorrhoidal, treated with banding, with no recurrence and a normal 2023 colonoscopy, so the bleeding-history alert is acknowledged and overridden.

Persistent rapid ventricular rate (118/min) with LVEF 30%: a beta-blocker with HFrEF evidence (metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol, carvedilol) is first-line rate control and GDMT; digoxin is an accepted alternative. Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are contraindicated with LVEF below 40%.

forbidden.why: LVEF 30%: diltiazem and verapamil are contraindicated in HFrEF (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, class 3: harm).
Class IC antiarrhythmics are contraindicated with structural heart disease and reduced LVEF.
No apixaban dose-reduction criteria are met (age under 80, weight 88 kg, creatinine 1.0).
No vascular indication for antiplatelet therapy; adding it to anticoagulation increases bleeding risk.

extras.why: Initiating guideline-directed medical therapy for newly found LVEF 30% is reasonable.
A loop diuretic is reasonable if congestion is judged present.
Amiodarone is a safe rhythm-control option in HFrEF when tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy is suspected.
Early rhythm control is reasonable for suspected tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Ischemic evaluation of new cardiomyopathy is standard.
Low-risk baseline testing for new AF and cardiomyopathy.

tasks.title: Thyroid Medication Management and Follow-up Planning
tasks.subject: Abnormal thyroid function results
tasks.request: TSH 0.03 mIU/L (L) and free T4 2.3 ng/dL (H), collected 2024-05-29, for a patient on levothyroxine after thyroidectomy. Please review.
facts: Benign pathology, no TSH suppression target

required.why: Overt exogenous over-replacement (TSH 0.03, free T4 2.3, symptoms) after 14 kg intentional weight loss, in a 64-78-year-old woman with osteopenia, after thyroidectomy for benign goiter (no indication for TSH suppression): reduce levothyroxine by 12.5-25 mcg, to 112 or 100 mcg daily (about 1.5-1.7 mcg/kg at 67 kg).
Recheck TSH and free T4 about 6-8 weeks after the dose change.

forbidden.why: Thyrotoxicosis is exogenous in an athyreotic patient; antithyroid drugs are not indicated.
Continuing or increasing the dose perpetuates overt over-replacement (atrial fibrillation and bone loss risk).
forbidden.dose: 125 or 137 or 150 or 175 or 200 or 225 or 250 or 300 mcg

forbidden.why: T3-containing therapy has no role in correcting over-replacement.

extras.why: A short course of beta-blocker for adrenergic symptoms is reasonable while the dose is corrected.
Bone density reassessment is reasonable given osteopenia and prolonged over-replacement.
Rhythm assessment for palpitations is low-risk.

tasks.title: Headache Classification and Diagnostic Workup
tasks.subject: Urgent referral: progressive headache with abnormal examination
tasks.request: Six weeks of new, progressive daily headache with focal findings on examination. Please evaluate urgently and arrange the diagnostic workup.

required.why: New progressive headache after age 50 with positional/Valsalva features, focal signs and papilledema requires urgent neuroimaging to exclude a mass lesion or other cause of raised intracranial pressure. MRI is preferred in general, but this patient has a non-MR-conditional pacemaker system with an abandoned lead and is pacemaker dependent, so CT of the head (with and/or without contrast; renal function normal) is the appropriate study.

forbidden.why: Non-MR-conditional pacemaker system with an abandoned, capped right ventricular lead in a pacemaker-dependent patient.
Papilledema with focal neurological signs: lumbar puncture before imaging risks herniation and must be deferred until a mass lesion is excluded.

extras.why: Formal ophthalmologic confirmation of papilledema is reasonable.
Coagulation testing is a low-risk baseline before possible procedures.
Early neurosurgical involvement is tolerated if a mass is suspected.

tasks.title: Atrial Fibrillation with Ambulatory Monitor Findings in an Older Adult
tasks.subject: Ambulatory ECG patch report finalized
tasks.request: The 14-day ambulatory ECG patch report is final for a patient with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on metoprolol and apixaban, referred by primary care for palpitations and lightheadedness. Primary care asks whether metoprolol should be increased. Please review and manage.
facts: Pauses occur at termination of AF (tachy-brady pattern)
AF burden 22% with rates up to 158 bpm
Already on metoprolol succinate 50 mg (PCP asks to increase it: trap)

required.why: Symptomatic post-conversion pauses up to 5.2 s with sinus bradycardia (38 bpm) alternating with paroxysmal AF at up to 158 bpm on metoprolol: tachycardia-bradycardia syndrome. The 2018 ACC/AHA/HRS bradycardia guideline supports permanent pacing for symptomatic sinus node dysfunction, including tachy-brady syndrome, so that rate control can be continued; the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline considers catheter ablation reasonable to avoid pacing. Both decisions belong to electrophysiology.
Transthoracic echocardiogram to assess LV function, atrial size and valves before device or ablation decisions; the last study was in 2017.
Thyroid dysfunction is a reversible cause of both AF and sinus node dysfunction (2018 bradycardia guideline); TSH was last checked in 2019.

forbidden.why: Symptomatic pauses up to 5.2 s and awake sinus rates of 38 bpm without a pacemaker: increasing metoprolol, switching or adding a beta-blocker, or adding diltiazem, verapamil or digoxin risks syncope and asystole. Rate control can be intensified only after pacing (2018 bradycardia guideline).
Antiarrhythmic drugs suppress sinus node function and can prolong post-conversion pauses; in tachy-brady syndrome they are started only with pacing backup or under electrophysiology supervision.
Already anticoagulated with apixaban and no vascular indication: adding an antiplatelet agent increases bleeding risk.

extras.why: A resting 12-lead ECG is standard baseline before device evaluation.
Low-risk baseline cardiovascular laboratory tests.
Exercise testing for chronotropic competence is reasonable in suspected sinus node dysfunction.
Screening for sleep apnea, a contributor to both AF and nocturnal bradycardia, is reasonable.

tasks.title: COVID-19 Treatment in an Immunocompromised Outpatient
tasks.subject: COVID-19 in a B-cell-depleted patient
tasks.request: Patient on rituximab maintenance for vasculitis with PCR-confirmed COVID-19, symptom onset 6/1, not hypoxic and being managed at home. Please recommend and order treatment today.
facts: Day 3 of symptoms (within the treatment window)
Amlodipine on the medication list (low-relevance interaction alert)

required.why: B-cell depletion (rituximab, CD19 0, IgG 452) plus prednisone puts her at high risk of progression; she is on day 3 of mild COVID-19 without hypoxia. The NIH COVID-19 treatment guidelines prefer ritonavir-boosted nirmatrelvir within 5 days of onset; with eGFR 30 to <60 (41) the FDA label dose is nirmatrelvir 150 mg with ritonavir 100 mg twice daily for 5 days (150 mg, or 250 mg if the pack's combined content is entered). There are no contraindicated CYP3A interactions (amlodipine only needs monitoring). Remdesivir 200 mg IV on day 1, then 100 mg on days 2-3 (within 7 days, no renal adjustment) is the other preferred option.

forbidden.why: eGFR 41 (30 to <60): the full nirmatrelvir dose of 300 mg twice daily doubles exposure; the FDA label requires 150 mg with ritonavir 100 mg twice daily.
The NIH guidelines recommend against systemic corticosteroids for outpatients who do not need supplemental oxygen; maintenance prednisone continues.
Not effective for COVID-19 (NIH guidelines recommend against); colchicine is also contraindicated with ritonavir in kidney impairment.

extras.why: Symptomatic treatment is reasonable.
Home pulse oximetry monitoring in a high-risk patient.
Rechecking immunoglobulins is reasonable but not urgent.
Follow-up viral testing for prolonged shedding in an immunocompromised host is tolerated.

tasks.title: Inflammatory Arthritis Serologic and Pre-Treatment Workup
tasks.subject: New rheumatology referral: inflammatory arthritis
tasks.request: Inflammatory back pain, heel pain and knee and ankle synovitis; synovial fluid inflammatory without crystals; RF and CCP negative. Partial response to naproxen. Please review before the first rheumatology visit and order the additional workup you recommend, including anything needed before immunosuppressive therapy.
facts: Prior TST caused vesiculation, bullae and ulceration (contraindication to repeat TST)
Hepatitis B status unknown, born in the Philippines

required.why: Inflammatory back pain, Achilles enthesitis, asymmetric lower-limb oligoarthritis and prior acute anterior uveitis with negative RF, anti-CCP and ANA suggest spondyloarthritis; HLA-B27 is part of the ASAS classification criteria and the standard serologic marker.
Hepatitis B screening (HBsAg) is required before TNF inhibitors or other immunosuppression (ACR, AASLD); he was born in an intermediate-to-high prevalence country and his status is unknown.
Total hepatitis B core antibody detects resolved infection with reactivation risk under immunosuppression (CDC 2023 and AASLD screening guidance).

Latent tuberculosis screening is required before biologic therapy, and the 2019 result is too old. An IGRA is the required method here: ATS/IDSA/CDC 2017 prefer IGRA in BCG-vaccinated people, and his 2019 skin test caused vesiculation, bullae and ulceration.

forbidden.why: The prior tuberculin skin test caused vesiculation, bullae and ulceration, and is recorded as an allergy; CDC lists a prior severe (blistering) reaction as a contraindication to repeat TST. BCG vaccination also makes the TST unreliable.
Biologic or targeted synthetic DMARD therapy must not start before tuberculosis and hepatitis B screening results are available.

extras.why: Hepatitis C antibody is routine before immunosuppressive therapy.
HIV screening before immunosuppression is reasonable.
Hepatitis B surface antibody helps decide on vaccination.
Sacroiliac imaging (radiograph or MRI) is standard for suspected axial spondyloarthritis.
A baseline chest radiograph is reasonable before biologic therapy in a BCG-vaccinated person.
Fecal calprotectin screening for occult IBD, or ophthalmology follow-up after uveitis, are tolerated extras.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult
tasks.subject: New atrial fibrillation: ED follow-up
tasks.request: Young woman seen for new atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response that converted spontaneously; discharged without prescriptions. ED laboratory results are in the chart. She is in cardiology clinic today with recurrent palpitations. Please evaluate and manage.
facts: Diffuse goiter with bruit (likely Graves disease)
No hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, stroke or vascular disease (CHA2DS2-VASc 1 from sex only)

required.why: AF precipitated by overt thyrotoxicosis (TSH 0.008, free T4 3.6, T3 285) with an ongoing rapid rate (112-140). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline and the 2016 ATA hyperthyroidism guideline recommend a beta-blocker for rate control and adrenergic symptoms; she has no asthma. Accepted per-dose sets follow FDA labeling: propranolol 10-40 mg three or four times daily or long-acting 60-160 mg daily; metoprolol tartrate 12.5-100 mg twice daily or succinate 25-200 mg daily; atenolol 25-100 mg daily; nadolol 20-160 mg daily; bisoprolol 1.25-10 mg daily.
required.dose: 10 or 20 or 30 or 40 or 60 or 80 or 120 or 160 mg

required.why: The 2016 ATA guideline requires the cause of thyrotoxicosis to be established (TRAb or TSI, radioactive iodine uptake, or thyroid ultrasound with Doppler) before definitive therapy. Endocrinology referral or an etiology test satisfies this; Graves disease is likely given the diffuse goiter with bruit.
Transthoracic echocardiography is recommended for all patients with new AF (2023 AF guideline), and she has never had one; it also screens for thyrotoxic cardiomyopathy.

forbidden.why: Amiodarone is 37% iodine by weight. Its iodine load can worsen thyrotoxicosis and it can cause thyroiditis. Rhythm control is unlikely to succeed until she is euthyroid, and AF usually reverts once the thyroid is treated (2016 ATA; 2023 AF guideline).

Her CHA2DS2-VASc score of 1 comes from female sex alone (CHA2DS2-VA 0), so oral anticoagulation is not indicated. The 2023 guideline applies the same risk score to thyrotoxic AF, and antiplatelet therapy is not recommended for stroke prevention.

extras.why: Starting methimazole is reasonable when Graves disease is likely (diffuse goiter with bruit; ATA 2016), although many cardiologists defer it to endocrinology.
Repeat thyroid function or TPO antibodies are reasonable extras.
Repeat ECG or ambulatory monitoring to assess rate control.

tasks.title: Persistent Diarrhea: Stool Results and Treatment
tasks.subject: Stool C. difficile and pathogen panel results
tasks.request: Stool testing for a patient with 5 weeks of diarrhea after antibiotics: C. difficile GDH antigen and toxin positive; GI pathogen panel negative. Blood tests from 5/31 have also resulted. Please review and treat.
facts: No distension or peritoneal signs (not fulminant)

required.why: Initial episode of toxigenic C. difficile infection (GDH and toxin positive) after amoxicillin-clavulanate in a patient on a PPI. It is severe by IDSA/SHEA 2017 criteria (WBC 16.2 x10^3/uL, at least 15) but not fulminant (no hypotension, ileus or distension; creatinine 0.9). IDSA/SHEA 2021: fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily for 10 days (preferred) or oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily for 10 days.

forbidden.why: Severe CDI (WBC 16.2): IDSA/SHEA guidelines recommend vancomycin or fidaxomicin. Metronidazole is inferior and is reserved for non-severe disease when neither first-line agent is available, despite the clinic note's plan.
Antiperistaltic agents in active severe CDI can precipitate ileus and toxic megacolon; they are avoided.
Intravenous vancomycin does not reach the colonic lumen and is ineffective for CDI.
The pathogen panel is negative; any other antibacterial worsens CDI outcomes and raises recurrence risk.

extras.why: Potassium 3.4 mmol/L with ongoing diarrhea: oral replacement is reasonable.
Oral rehydration support.
Severity markers are reasonable extras.
Specialist input is tolerated, although not needed for a first episode responding to treatment.

tasks.title: Recurrent Olecranon Bursitis in an Immunocompromised Patient
tasks.subject: Recurrent olecranon bursitis: culture result
tasks.request: Third episode of right olecranon septic bursitis in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and prednisone. The bursal fluid culture is now final, and empiric cephalexin was stopped after the result. Please evaluate and advise on antibiotic therapy and next steps.
facts: Takes calcium carbonate (tetracycline spacing, low-relevance alert)

required.why: MRSA septic bursitis susceptible to doxycycline, TMP-SMX, linezolid and vancomycin. TMP-SMX is excluded by the methotrexate interaction, clindamycin by inducible resistance (D-test positive), and beta-lactams are inactive. IDSA 2011 MRSA guideline oral options: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, minocycline 200 mg then 100 mg twice daily, linezolid 600 mg twice daily (tedizolid 200 mg daily). IV vancomycin 15-20 mg/kg (70 kg: 1000-1500 mg) is accepted if parenteral therapy is chosen. With calcium carbonate, doxycycline or minocycline must be spaced at least 2 hours apart (the alert is acknowledged).

Third episode of septic bursitis in 9 months in an immunosuppressed host, with a persistent 6 cm fluctuant collection: repeat drainage and evaluation for surgical bursectomy are indicated for recurrent or refractory septic olecranon bursitis.

forbidden.why: Despite in vitro susceptibility, TMP-SMX with methotrexate 15 mg weekly adds antifolate effect and reduces renal methotrexate clearance. The combination can cause severe, sometimes fatal pancytopenia (major interaction).
Inducible clindamycin resistance (D-test positive) predicts clinical failure (CLSI reports the isolate as resistant).
MRSA (oxacillin and cefazolin resistant): these beta-lactams are inactive.
Corticosteroid injection is contraindicated in septic bursitis.
Same as above, entered as a procedure order.

extras.why: Elbow ultrasound, radiograph or MRI to define the collection and exclude osteomyelitis or a foreign body.
Repeat blood cultures are tolerated; the first set is negative at 72 hours.
Inflammatory markers to follow the response.
Coordination with rheumatology about holding methotrexate during active infection.

tasks.title: Travel-Related Parasitic Infection: Malaria Treatment
tasks.subject: Malaria on blood smear in a returned traveler
tasks.request: Returned traveler from Honduras with cyclic fevers; blood smear shows Plasmodium vivax, parasitemia 0.3%, no severe features. In overnight observation. Please recommend and order treatment, including relapse prevention.

required.why: Uncomplicated P. vivax malaria (parasitemia 0.3%, HRP2 negative, no severe features) acquired in Honduras, where P. vivax is chloroquine-sensitive. CDC 2024 US treatment guidance: chloroquine phosphate 600 mg base (1 g salt) then 300 mg base (500 mg salt) at 6, 24 and 48 hours; or hydroxychloroquine 620 mg base (800 mg salt) then 310 mg base (400 mg salt) at 6, 24 and 48 hours. Artemether-lumefantrine and atovaquone-proguanil are also acceptable. These fixed-combination tablets are checked by name and frequency only, because their dose is entered in tablets.

forbidden.why: Severe G6PD deficiency (1.1 U/g Hb, below 10% activity; fava-bean hemolysis in 2016). Primaquine and tafenoquine cause life-threatening hemolysis and are contraindicated (FDA labels, CDC). Relapse prevention uses weekly chloroquine prophylaxis instead.
Oxidant drugs that cause hemolysis in severe G6PD deficiency; none is indicated.

extras.why: Repeat blood smears to document parasite clearance (CDC).
Hemolysis monitoring in a G6PD-deficient patient with malaria.
Baseline QTc before chloroquine is reasonable.
Repeating G6PD activity is unnecessary (it is known to be severely low) but harmless.
Antipyretic.

tasks.title: Asbestos Exposure Concern with a New Pleural Effusion
tasks.subject: Right pleural effusion on chest radiograph
tasks.request: Urgent care visit 2024-05-28 for progressive shortness of breath; the chest radiograph shows a right pleural effusion. The patient asks whether this could be related to asbestos: her late husband worked in a shipyard. Please review and arrange the next steps.
facts: Moderate right pleural effusion with nodular pleural thickening
Para-occupational asbestos exposure (laundered husband's shipyard work clothes 1968-1990)
Urgent care suggested a diuretic trial (trap)

required.why: A new unilateral effusion with nodular pleural thickening, 5 kg weight loss and thrombocytosis 34-56 years after para-occupational asbestos exposure must be sampled to exclude malignant pleural mesothelioma: BTS 2023 pleural guideline recommends image-guided diagnostic pleural aspiration (protein, LDH, pH, glucose, cell count, microbiology and cytology) for a unilateral effusion without a clear transudative cause. Normal NT-proBNP, no edema or JVD, LVEF 60%, normal albumin and creatinine make heart failure, hypoalbuminemia and renal causes unlikely.

Cross-sectional imaging is needed to characterize the nodular pleural thickening, plaques and underlying lung: BTS 2023 recommends contrast-enhanced CT of the thorax (pleural phase) for an undiagnosed effusion, ideally before complete drainage. eGFR 78 permits contrast, so the metformin alert is acknowledged and overridden (ACR Manual on Contrast Media: metformin need not be held with eGFR of 30 or more and no acute kidney injury).

forbidden.why: Unilateral effusion with normal NT-proBNP (96 pg/mL), no edema or JVD and LVEF 60%: not heart failure. An empiric diuretic trial, as suggested in urgent care, delays the diagnosis of a possible malignant effusion and is not indicated (BTS 2023).

extras.why: Referral to a pleural, pulmonology or thoracic surgery service for aspiration, thoracoscopy or biopsy is appropriate.
Pleural biopsy is the next step if cytology is non-diagnostic; arranging it early is reasonable when mesothelioma is suspected.
Thoracic ultrasound to characterize the effusion and guide aspiration.
Paired serum LDH and protein are needed for Light's criteria.
PET-CT is used in staging if malignancy is confirmed; tolerated.
Baseline lung function is reasonable after asbestos exposure.

tasks.title: Dermatology E-Consult: Persistent Lower-Leg Rash
tasks.subject: Bilateral leg rash not responding to treatment
tasks.request: E-consult from primary care: 4-month bilateral lower-leg rash treated as cellulitis without response to two antibiotic courses or an over-the-counter cream, and now worse. Please review the chart and advise on the diagnosis and treatment.
facts: Patch test positive for neomycin and bacitracin
Patch test negative for corticosteroid markers
No response to two antibiotic courses

required.why: Bilateral, symmetric, itchy, scaly, lichenified plaques with hemosiderin staining, edema and varicose veins over documented superficial venous reflux, with no fever, normal WBC and CRP and no response to two antibiotic courses: stasis dermatitis misdiagnosed as cellulitis (true bilateral cellulitis is rare; IDSA 2014). The weeping, spreading flare after neomycin/bacitracin ointment in a patient with patch-test-proven allergy to both is superimposed allergic contact dermatitis. Treatment is a medium- or high-potency topical corticosteroid for 1-2 weeks (AAD and standard dermatology references); low-potency hydrocortisone 1% already failed. Patch testing was negative for tixocortol pivalate and budesonide, so there is no corticosteroid allergy. The cellulitis alert is acknowledged and overridden because the cellulitis diagnosis is not supported.

forbidden.why: Patch-test-proven allergic contact dermatitis to neomycin and bacitracin (2022), and the current flare began after triple antibiotic ointment: any neomycin- or bacitracin-containing product, including steroid combinations, is contraindicated.

No infection: bilateral and symmetric, non-tender, afebrile, WBC 7.2, CRP 3.1 and no response to cephalexin or doxycycline. Further antibiotics are not indicated and add adverse-event and resistance risk.

extras.why: Compression treats the underlying venous hypertension; ABI 1.04-1.06 confirms it is safe.
A bland emollient or zinc barrier on fissures avoids further sensitizers.
Repeat or expanded patch testing is reasonable if dermatitis persists.
Vein specialist referral for symptomatic superficial reflux.
Topical mupirocin to crusted fissures is low risk and not cross-reactive with neomycin or bacitracin, though not required.
A non-sedating antihistamine for pruritus is harmless.

tasks.title: Persistently Elevated Liver Enzymes: Etiology and Fibrosis Assessment
tasks.subject: Persistently elevated liver enzymes
tasks.request: Automated alert: ALT and AST above the reference range on two results at least 6 months apart (most recent 2024-05-20). The patient was referred by primary care for hepatology input on the workup.
facts: ALT 64 U/L (2024-05-20), elevated more than 6 months
Viral and autoimmune workup already negative
Iron, IgG, ceruloplasmin and tTG already normal
