required.why: Persistent transaminase elevation with viral, autoimmune, iron, Wilson, celiac and metabolic causes already excluded (negative serologies, normal ferritin and transferrin saturation, IgG, ceruloplasmin and tTG-IgA; BMI 23.7, no steatosis, minimal alcohol), together with early lower-lobe panlobular emphysema and a brother with emphysema at 49: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency must be tested (ACG 2017 abnormal liver chemistries guideline; ATS/ERS and Alpha-1 Foundation testing guidance: serum AAT level with phenotype or genotype).

FIB-4 is indeterminate (about 2.0 at age 46 with AST 58, ALT 64 and platelets 168; 1.8-2.2 across ages 42-50), and AAT-deficiency liver disease needs staging: vibration-controlled transient elastography, ultrasound shear-wave elastography or the ELF test is the recommended second step (AASLD 2024 practice guideline on noninvasive liver disease assessment). MR elastography is excluded by the retained ferromagnetic fragments.

forbidden.why: Retained metallic fragments presumed ferromagnetic, one 3 mm from the cervical spinal cord; the MRI safety team documented that MRI is contraindicated. MR elastography, MRI and MRCP risk fragment migration, heating and cord injury.

extras.why: Coordination with pulmonology is reasonable given early emphysema.
Genetic counseling and family testing if deficiency is confirmed.
Synthetic function check.
Hepatitis A immunity testing or vaccination in chronic liver disease.
Low-cost tests for alcohol, muscle or thyroid causes of transaminase elevation.
Repeat ultrasound is low risk, although one was done in April.

tasks.title: Amenorrhea Workup and Possible PCOS
tasks.subject: Irregular periods: possible PCOS
tasks.request: Referral for evaluation of amenorrhea and possible polycystic ovary syndrome; the pelvic ultrasound shows polycystic-appearing ovaries. Please evaluate and advise on management.
facts: PCP suggested metformin for presumed PCOS (trap)

required.why: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea with about 8 months of amenorrhea, low estradiol and a prior metatarsal stress fracture: the Endocrine Society 2017 FHA guideline recommends baseline bone mineral density by DXA after 6 or more months of amenorrhea, or earlier with severe nutritional deficiency or skeletal fragility.

FHA from low energy availability (80 km per week of running, 6 kg weight loss to BMI 18.1, meal skipping) is treated by restoring energy balance: the Endocrine Society guideline recommends correcting the energy deficit with nutritional support and suggests psychological support (e.g. CBT) and screening for disordered eating, ideally in a multidisciplinary team (registered dietitian, mental health, sports medicine).

forbidden.why: The findings do not support PCOS: normal androgens and 17-OHP, no clinical hyperandrogenism, low LH and estradiol with a thin endometrium, and an energy deficit; polycystic ovarian morphology is common in FHA, which must be excluded before diagnosing PCOS (2023 International PCOS guideline). Metformin has no indication, and its anorexia, GI effects and weight loss worsen the energy deficit.

extras.why: 25-hydroxyvitamin D is reasonable after a stress fracture.
Calcium and vitamin D sufficiency supports bone health (Endocrine Society FHA guideline).
Short-term transdermal estradiol with cyclic progestin is the guideline option if energy restoration fails or bone loss is significant; starting at the first visit is early but acceptable.
Cyclic progestin paired with transdermal estradiol.
Resting heart rate 48 in possible energy deficiency: an ECG is reasonable.
Repeat gonadotropins, prolactin, thyroid tests or AMH are low-risk confirmatory tests.

tasks.title: Post-Hospitalization Follow-Up After Gastrointestinal Bleeding
tasks.subject: Hospital discharge: gastrointestinal bleeding
tasks.request: Patient discharged 2024-05-23 after admission for gastrointestinal bleeding with a new diagnosis of cirrhosis. He is in clinic today for post-discharge follow-up. Please review the hospitalization and coordinate ongoing care.
facts: Home metoprolol and lisinopril stopped; no prophylactic drug started
Patient asks to restart metoprolol and lisinopril (trap)

required.why: Secondary prophylaxis after acute esophageal variceal hemorrhage is a nonselective beta-blocker combined with serial band ligation (AASLD 2024 portal hypertension guidance; Baveno VII). Starting doses: propranolol 20-40 mg twice daily (10 mg acceptable after recent hypotension), nadolol 20-40 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg daily or 3.125 mg twice daily; titrate to heart rate 55-60 with systolic BP above 90 (with ascites, at most propranolol 80 mg/day, nadolol 40 mg/day, carvedilol 12.5 mg/day). The in-hospital hypotension on octreotide has resolved (124/76, HR 92 today), so the hypotension alert is acknowledged and overridden.

Endoscopic band ligation is repeated every 1-4 weeks until the varices are eradicated (AASLD 2024; Baveno VII); no repeat endoscopy was arranged at discharge, so a gastroenterology or hepatology referral or a repeat EGD with band ligation within 1-2 weeks is required.

forbidden.why: Beta-1-selective blockers, including his previous metoprolol, do not reduce portal pressure (no beta-2 splanchnic vasoconstriction) and give false reassurance; only nonselective agents (propranolol, nadolol, carvedilol) are recommended for variceal prophylaxis.
Cirrhosis with ascites on diuretics: ACE inhibitors and ARBs cause hypotension and acute kidney injury and should be avoided (AASLD 2021 ascites guidance); blood pressure is controlled without them.

Decompensated alcohol-associated cirrhosis (variceal bleeding, ascites): disulfiram is hepatotoxic and contraindicated, and naltrexone should be avoided in decompensated liver disease (AASLD 2019 alcohol-associated liver disease guidance; ACG 2024 guideline); acamprosate or baclofen are the preferred options.

extras.why: Acamprosate or baclofen are recommended options for alcohol use disorder in cirrhosis.
Referral for alcohol use disorder treatment is standard.
Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance every 6 months in cirrhosis.
Viral hepatitis serologies and vaccination are standard in newly diagnosed cirrhosis.
INR and PEth for synthetic function and abstinence monitoring.
A short PPI course after further banding is acceptable.

tasks.title: Depression and Anxiety Medication Management After an Antidepressant Adverse Reaction
tasks.subject: Adverse reaction to antidepressant: requesting alternative
tasks.request: Daughter called: the antidepressant was stopped last week because of hyponatremia. Confusion has resolved, but mood and sleep are worse. She requests an updated medication plan.
facts: Poor appetite with 4 kg weight loss

required.why: Sertraline-associated SIADH (sodium 124, serum osmolality 259, urine osmolality 418) with sodium still 131: SSRIs and SNRIs carry the highest hyponatremia risk and recurrence on rechallenge is likely. Mirtazapine or bupropion has a lower risk (Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines; De Picker et al. 2014). Mirtazapine also targets her insomnia, poor appetite and weight loss. Conservative geriatric start: mirtazapine 7.5-15 mg at bedtime, titrated every 1-2 weeks; bupropion SR 100 mg, XL 150 mg or IR 75 mg daily is an accepted alternative. The Beers caution alert for mirtazapine is acknowledged and overridden with sodium monitoring.

Starting any antidepressant after drug-induced SIADH, with sodium still 131, requires a sodium check within 1-2 weeks (AGS Beers 2023: monitor sodium when starting or changing antidepressants in older adults).

forbidden.why: SIADH on sertraline with sodium still 131 mmol/L: SSRIs, SNRIs and related serotonergic agents (vortioxetine, vilazodone) share the highest hyponatremia risk, and rechallenge in a 79-year-old who became confused at sodium 124 is unsafe.
Older adult with recent hyponatremic confusion: benzodiazepines and Z-drug hypnotics should be avoided (AGS Beers 2023: cognitive impairment, delirium, falls, fractures).
Tricyclic antidepressants are strongly anticholinergic, sedating and orthostatic in older adults (AGS Beers 2023: avoid) and also cause SIADH.

extras.why: Psychotherapy or psychiatry follow-up is recommended alongside pharmacotherapy.
Repeat SIADH indices are reasonable.
Excluding hypothyroidism or adrenal insufficiency is reasonable in hyponatremia (both already normal).
Low-dose melatonin for sleep is a low-risk option in older adults.
Low-cost tests in late-life depression with weight loss.

tasks.title: Urinary Retention Management and Workup Planning
tasks.subject: Urinary retention with indwelling catheter
tasks.request: Referral for urinary retention: catheter placed in the emergency department on 2024-05-20 (900 mL). Primary care asks for urology evaluation and management, including whether prostate surgery is appropriate.
facts: Autonomic neuropathy (orthostatic drop without heart rate rise)

required.why: Chronic painless retention (PVR 640 mL, then 900 mL) with a small 24 mL prostate, long-standing diabetes with polyneuropathy, gastroparesis and orthostatic hypotension without heart rate rise (autonomic neuropathy): diabetic cystopathy with detrusor underactivity is as likely as bladder outlet obstruction. Multichannel urodynamics with a pressure-flow study is needed to distinguish them before any outlet procedure (AUA 2021 BPH guideline: pressure-flow studies when diagnostic uncertainty exists before intervention; EAU guidelines: pressure-flow studies in men with PVR above 300 mL or suspected neurogenic dysfunction who are considering surgery).

forbidden.why: Scheduling an outlet procedure now is premature and likely harmful: the prostate is small (24 mL) and diabetic cystopathy is suspected; outlet surgery fails in detrusor underactivity and leaves the patient catheter-dependent with surgical morbidity. Surgery is considered only if urodynamics confirms obstruction.

extras.why: Clean intermittent self-catheterization is the preferred drainage for chronic retention with suspected detrusor underactivity.
A voiding trial on tamsulosin is reasonable before or with urodynamics.
Cystoscopy to assess the outlet (stricture, bladder neck) is reasonable before any surgical decision.
Residual and flow measurement.
Urine culture before urodynamics in a catheterized patient.
Optimizing glycemic control.

tasks.title: Buprenorphine Initiation for Opioid Use Disorder on Long-Term Opioid Therapy
tasks.subject: Request to start buprenorphine treatment
tasks.request: Patient on long-term hydromorphone for spinal stenosis now meets criteria for opioid use disorder and is motivated to transition to buprenorphine. Induction visit with you today. Please review the chart and prescribe an appropriate buprenorphine regimen.

required.why: Opioid use disorder, moderate, with motivation for buprenorphine. Decompensated cirrhosis, Child-Pugh class C (bilirubin 3.4, albumin 2.6, INR 2.0, ascites needing paracentesis): the FDA labeling of buprenorphine/naloxone combination products does not recommend them in severe hepatic impairment (reduced naloxone clearance can precipitate withdrawal and reduce efficacy), so the sublingual buprenorphine mono-product is used, with the starting and titration doses halved (label: consider halving in severe hepatic impairment): 1-2 mg per dose instead of 2-4 mg.

forbidden.why: Child-Pugh class C: buprenorphine/naloxone combination products are not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (FDA labeling), because naloxone exposure rises and may precipitate withdrawal and reduce efficacy.
Naltrexone precipitates withdrawal in a physiologically opioid-dependent patient, does not treat his pain, and its labeling warns against use in acute hepatitis or liver failure.

extras.why: Take-home naloxone for overdose rescue is recommended for every patient with opioid use disorder.
Symptomatic treatment of nausea during induction is reasonable.
Urine drug testing at induction and follow-up is standard.
Infectious disease screening is recommended at entry to opioid use disorder treatment.
Liver monitoring or addiction medicine or hepatology involvement is reasonable.

tasks.title: Diabetes Management Reassessment After Marked A1C Improvement
tasks.subject: HbA1c markedly improved
tasks.request: Hemoglobin A1c 6.0% (collected 2024-05-29), down from 10.9% at the August 2023 admission for hyperosmolar hyperglycemia, in a patient on metformin and glipizide. Please review the regimen for possible de-escalation.
facts: Transfused 3 units of red cells in April 2024

required.why: The A1C of 6.0% is discordant with meter glucose (fasting 172-228, pre-dinner 181-262 mg/dL, none below 70), a fasting plasma glucose of 214 and persistent polyuria. It is falsely low: 3 units of red cells were transfused on 2024-04-12/13 after acute blood loss, and reticulocytes are 3.8%, so the circulating red cells are young. ADA Standards of Care (section 6) advise against relying on A1C with recent blood loss, transfusion or increased red cell turnover and suggest fructosamine/glycated albumin or CGM with glucose data instead.

forbidden.why: Glipizide dose reduction (from 10 mg twice daily) is based on a falsely low A1C; meter readings show persistent hyperglycemia without hypoglycemia.
Metformin dose reduction (from 1000 mg twice daily) is based on a falsely low A1C; renal function is normal and there is no intolerance.

extras.why: A repeat A1C becomes informative again about 3 months after the transfusion (mid-July 2024 or later).
Intensification is reasonable given meter glucose of 170-260 mg/dL without hypoglycemia (ADA: GLP-1 RA, SGLT2 inhibitor, basal insulin or DPP-4 inhibitor).
Glucose-monitoring supplies support the meter-based assessment.
Follow-up of post-hemorrhagic anemia and plasma glucose are low-risk extras.
Routine diabetes surveillance labs are harmless extras.

tasks.title: Elevated Liver Enzymes in Pregnancy: Hepatology Evaluation
tasks.subject: Persistently elevated ALT in pregnancy
tasks.request: ALT 81 U/L (H) on 2024-05-20, previously 74 U/L in March, in a pregnant patient (26 weeks) with chronic hepatitis B referred to hepatology by obstetrics. Hepatitis B viral load resulted 2024-05-21. Please review and manage.

required.why: HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B with HBV DNA 84,000,000 IU/mL at 26-27 weeks: AASLD 2018 guidance and SMFM Consult 38 recommend antiviral therapy for HBV DNA above 200,000 IU/mL to reduce perinatal transmission, started at 28-32 weeks, with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg daily preferred. ALT 81 U/L (more than twice the upper limit for women) also makes her immune-active. Tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily is accepted as an alternative with accumulating pregnancy data. Renal function is normal (creatinine 0.55). The tenofovir pregnancy alert is low-relevance and is acknowledged and overridden.

forbidden.why: The 2022 entecavir plan predates the pregnancy: human pregnancy safety data are limited and animal studies showed embryo-fetal toxicity; AASLD, SMFM and ACOG recommend tenofovir in pregnancy.
Interferon alfa and peginterferon are contraindicated in pregnancy.
No indication for CT or gadolinium-enhanced MRI in pregnancy; ultrasound suffices for liver imaging.

extras.why: Repeat HBV markers before delivery or on therapy are reasonable.
Liver ultrasound is safe in pregnancy; elastography is a harmless extra.
Coinfection testing is standard in chronic hepatitis B.
Low-risk baseline or renal-safety tests before tenofovir.
Coordination with obstetrics or maternal-fetal medicine is reasonable.

tasks.title: Hip Osteoarthritis Pain Management in an NSAID-Intolerant Patient
tasks.subject: Hip pain - can I get the gel shot?
tasks.request: Dr. Reyes said I could have an injection in my right hip and that you would set it up. My sister had Synvisc gel shots in her knee and they worked really well. Could you please order the gel shot for my hip? The Tylenol is not enough anymore.
facts: Orthopedics: candidate for intra-articular injection, type to be chosen by primary care

required.why: Symptomatic right hip osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3) despite acetaminophen, completed physical therapy, cane use and topical diclofenac (ineffective for a deep joint); surgery deferred; orthopedics found her a candidate for injection. Oral NSAIDs are unsafe (meloxicam-associated AKI, CKD 3b, eGFR 36) and tramadol caused a fall. The 2019 ACR/AF guideline strongly recommends intra-articular glucocorticoid injection for hip osteoarthritis, preferably image-guided, and strongly recommends against intra-articular hyaluronic acid for the hip, which she requested.

forbidden.why: ACR/AF 2019 strongly recommends against intra-articular hyaluronic acid for hip osteoarthritis.
ACR/AF 2019 strongly recommends against intra-articular hyaluronic acid for hip osteoarthritis.
ACR/AF 2019 strongly recommends against platelet-rich plasma and stem-cell injections for osteoarthritis.
Meloxicam-associated acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.4) and CKD stage 3b (eGFR 36): systemic NSAIDs, including COX-2 inhibitors, are unsafe.
Tramadol caused dizziness and a fall in 2023.

extras.why: Some workflows also enter the injectate (corticosteroid with local anesthetic) as a medication order.
Referral to the service that performs the image-guided injection, or orthopedic follow-up, is reasonable.
Exercise therapy is strongly recommended in hip osteoarthritis.
A cane is strongly recommended for hip osteoarthritis.
Acetaminophen up to 3 g/day, or duloxetine (conditional ACR recommendation; eGFR 36 is above the 30 mL/min limit).

tasks.title: Anemia Management in Pregnancy with Beta Thalassemia Trait
tasks.subject: Anemia in pregnancy with thalassemia trait
tasks.request: New CBC for a patient at 10 weeks with known beta thalassemia trait: hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, MCV 63 fL, ferritin 78 ng/mL. Should she start extra iron, oral or intravenous? Please advise on anemia management and anything else needed for this pregnancy.

required.why: She has beta thalassemia trait (HbA2 5.6%) and her partner has hemoglobin E trait (HbE 27%): each pregnancy has a 1 in 4 risk of HbE/beta thalassemia, which is often transfusion-dependent. ACOG Practice Bulletin 78 and Committee Opinion 691 recommend genetic counseling and an offer of prenatal diagnosis when both partners are carriers; at 11 weeks she is in the window for chorionic villus sampling (10-13 weeks), so the referral is time-sensitive.

forbidden.why: Ferritin 78 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 31%: no iron deficiency; the microcytic anemia is explained by beta thalassemia trait.
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL with stable thalassemia-trait anemia in an asymptomatic patient: no indication for transfusion.

extras.why: Folic acid (often 1-4 mg daily in hemoglobinopathy carriers) or continuing the prenatal vitamin is reasonable.
Nutritional and hemolysis labs are low-risk extras.
Molecular characterization of her beta-globin mutation (and alpha-globin testing) helps targeted prenatal diagnosis.
Routine first-trimester ultrasound is a harmless extra.

tasks.title: Thrombocytopenia Evaluation for a Patient on Immunotherapy
tasks.subject: Falling platelets on nivolumab
tasks.request: Platelet count 37 on 2024-05-31, down from 196 in April, in a patient on adjuvant nivolumab for melanoma. We are concerned about immune-related thrombocytopenia. Should we hold nivolumab and start prednisone? Please evaluate and advise.

required.why: The analyzer counts (37-64) come with a platelet clump flag, and the pathologist smear shows numerous platelet clumps with an adequate estimated count, normal other lineages, no schistocytes, no bleeding and no petechiae: this is EDTA-dependent pseudothrombocytopenia until proven otherwise. The standard confirmation is a platelet count collected in a sodium citrate (or heparin) tube, before any treatment for immune thrombocytopenia (ASCO 2021 irAE guideline: exclude other causes before attributing to the checkpoint inhibitor).

forbidden.why: No true thrombocytopenia is established (clumping with adequate smear estimate, no bleeding): glucocorticoids are not indicated and would expose the patient to steroid toxicity during adjuvant immunotherapy.
Immune thrombocytopenia therapy is not indicated before a true low platelet count is confirmed.
No bleeding and no true thrombocytopenia: platelet transfusion is not indicated.
An invasive marrow examination is not indicated when the smear shows clumping with an adequate platelet estimate and the other lineages are normal.

extras.why: A repeat smear review with the non-EDTA sample is reasonable.
Coagulation tests are low-risk extras while true thrombocytopenia is being excluded.
Hemolysis or platelet-production markers are low-risk extras.
Routine immune-related adverse event monitoring on nivolumab.

tasks.title: VTE Prophylaxis Medication Substitution
tasks.subject: Substitute needed for overseas VTE prophylaxis injection
tasks.request: I fly to France on June 14. My doctor in France prescribes Fraxiparine injections for my flights because I had a blood clot after a long flight in 2019. I have run out and my pharmacy says it is not sold here. Can you prescribe the US equivalent?

required.why: Prior travel-provoked proximal DVT and a 9-hour flight: ASH 2018 suggests prophylactic-dose LMWH (or compression stockings) for long-distance travelers at substantially increased risk, and she used LMWH uneventfully before. Weight 47 kg, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL and age 76-82 give a Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance of about 25-27 mL/min, although the eGFR is 42. The FDA enoxaparin label reduces prophylaxis to 30 mg once daily for CrCl below 30 mL/min. Dalteparin once daily is accepted (less accumulation in severe renal impairment; dose in IU cannot be checked). The SSRI interaction alert is low-relevance for single travel-day doses and is acknowledged and overridden.

forbidden.why: Creatinine clearance about 25-27 mL/min: 40 mg daily, 30 mg twice daily and treatment doses exceed the labeled prophylactic dose (30 mg once daily) and raise bleeding risk.
forbidden.dose: 40 or 45 or 47 or 50 or 60 or 70 or 80 or 100 mg

forbidden.why: Fondaparinux is contraindicated for prophylaxis with creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min and with body weight below 50 kg (FDA labeling).

extras.why: Below-knee graduated compression stockings are recommended alongside or instead of LMWH for high-risk travelers.
Anti-Xa monitoring is reasonable with LMWH in severe renal impairment.
Measured or confirmed renal function is a harmless extra.
Sharps container for self-injection.

tasks.title: Chronic Cough: Results Review and Stepwise Management
tasks.subject: Follow-up: chronic cough and breathing test results
tasks.request: Follow-up visit today to review pulmonary function and methacholine challenge results for a dry cough that has not responded to several treatment trials. Please review and update the treatment plan.
facts: Positive methacholine challenge (PC20 1.8 mg/mL) with normal spirometry
Prior suicide attempt (montelukast boxed warning trap)
Cough persists after stopping the ACE inhibitor

required.why: Chronic cough (7 months) with a normal chest radiograph, cough no better 5 months after stopping lisinopril, and no response to 8-week trials of an intranasal corticosteroid (upper airway cough syndrome) and high-dose omeprazole (reflux). Normal spirometry with a positive methacholine challenge (PC20 1.8 mg/mL), FeNO 52 ppb and blood eosinophils 0.52 establish cough-variant asthma. An inhaled corticosteroid is first-line therapy (CHEST 2020 chronic cough guideline; GINA 2024), alone or as ICS-formoterol; an ICS-LABA combination is accepted.

forbidden.why: Recurrent major depression with a 2019 suicide attempt and passive death wishes in 2022: montelukast carries an FDA boxed warning (2020) for serious neuropsychiatric events including suicidality and should be reserved for patients without alternatives; zafirlukast and zileuton carry neuropsychiatric warnings and are inferior to inhaled corticosteroids. An inhaled corticosteroid is available and preferred.
Long-acting beta-agonist monotherapy in asthma is contraindicated (FDA labeling; increased risk of asthma-related death) and LABA must be given only with an inhaled corticosteroid.
Opioid antitussives do not treat the cause, and the patient has a prior suicide attempt by overdose; FDA restricts opioid cough products to symptomatic use when benefits outweigh risks.

extras.why: An as-needed short-acting bronchodilator reliever alongside the inhaled corticosteroid is reasonable.
Pulmonology or allergy evaluation is reasonable for a confirmed airway disorder, though not required before a first ICS trial.
Total IgE or aeroallergen testing is a reasonable part of an asthma evaluation.
Repeat spirometry or FeNO to monitor response is reasonable.

tasks.title: Erectile Dysfunction and Premature Ejaculation: Results Review and Treatment Planning
tasks.subject: Hormone results for sexual health follow-up
tasks.request: Morning testosterone, LH, prolactin and TSH have resulted for a patient seen for erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation. Please review and complete the treatment plan.

required.why: Vasculogenic erectile dysfunction in an eugonadal man (morning testosterone 486 ng/dL, normal LH, prolactin and TSH). PDE5 inhibitors are first-line in general (AUA Erectile Dysfunction guideline 2018) but every PDE5 inhibitor label contraindicates any regular or intermittent nitrate use; he needs daily isosorbide mononitrate and as-needed sublingual nitroglycerin for angina that is not revascularizable and ranolazine failed, so the nitrate cannot simply be withdrawn. Nitrate-compatible options are a vacuum erection device, intraurethral or intracavernosal alprostadil (first dose under supervision) or a prosthesis: urology referral (or a vacuum erection device order) is the appropriate step.

forbidden.why: Daily isosorbide mononitrate and as-needed sublingual nitroglycerin: PDE5 inhibitors are contraindicated with nitrates in any form (FDA labeling; AUA 2018) because of severe hypotension, myocardial ischemia and death.
Morning testosterone 486 ng/dL with normal LH: eugonadal; testosterone therapy is not indicated (AUA testosterone deficiency guideline 2018).
Soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators are contraindicated with nitrates and have no role in erectile dysfunction.

extras.why: Alprostadil is a nitrate-compatible second-line ED therapy; the first dose should be given under supervision (usually arranged by urology).
Topical penile anesthetic is a first-line option for lifelong premature ejaculation (AUA/SMSNA 2020 ejaculation disorders guideline).
Daily or on-demand SSRI is a first-line option for lifelong premature ejaculation; agents without CYP2D6 inhibition of metoprolol preferred.
Behavioral and psychosexual therapy for premature ejaculation.
Cardiology input on whether the antianginal regimen could be changed is reasonable.
Cardiometabolic risk testing in vasculogenic ED (already done; harmless repeat).

tasks.title: Abnormal Liver Imaging, Gallbladder Polyps and Elevated Aminotransferases
tasks.subject: Abdominal ultrasound finalized
tasks.request: Abdominal ultrasound performed 2024-05-29 to characterize a liver finding on a recent emergency department CT is final and flagged for your review. Please interpret and arrange appropriate follow-up.
facts: CT lesion is a simple cyst

required.why: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (steatosis on ultrasound, type 2 diabetes, obesity, ALT persistently elevated, minimal alcohol, negative hepatitis B and C). FIB-4 = age x AST 52 / (platelets 168 x sqrt(ALT 62)) is about 1.6-1.9 for age 40-49: indeterminate (1.3-2.67). AASLD 2023 MASLD practice guidance and the AGA clinical care pathway call for a second-line test (vibration-controlled transient elastography, MR or shear-wave elastography, or ELF), or hepatology referral when unavailable; type 2 diabetes further raises the priority.

forbidden.why: Two 4 mm pedunculated ('ball-on-the-wall') gallbladder polyps in an asymptomatic man under 50 without primary sclerosing cholangitis or other risk factors are extremely low risk: neither cholecystectomy nor surgical evaluation is indicated (SRU 2022 consensus; ESGAR/EAES/EFISDS/ESGE 2022 guideline).

extras.why: Hepatitis A immunity testing before vaccination is reasonable in chronic liver disease.
Hepatitis A vaccination is recommended for people with chronic liver disease.
Metabolic and iron studies are reasonable in the MASLD evaluation.
Structured weight-loss support is first-line MASLD therapy.
A GLP-1 receptor agonist or pioglitazone is reasonable for type 2 diabetes with MASLD (AASLD 2023, ADA Standards of Care).

tasks.title: Osteoporosis: Treatment Planning After Anabolic Therapy
tasks.subject: Next osteoporosis therapy after abaloparatide
tasks.request: My patient completed a 24-month course of abaloparatide last month. The follow-up DXA is final. Please advise on and order the next osteoporosis treatment, and any monitoring she needs.

required.why: Very high fracture risk (vertebral and wrist fractures, femoral neck T-score -2.7) at the end of a 24-month abaloparatide course: gains are lost unless an antiresorptive follows immediately (Endocrine Society 2020 guideline; AACE 2020; Tymlos labeling limits cumulative use to 2 years). Bisphosphonates are excluded by bisphosphonate-associated scleritis after zoledronic acid; romosozumab by NSTEMI within the past year (boxed warning); raloxifene by established coronary disease. Denosumab 60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months is the appropriate agent; calcium 9.3, vitamin D 38 and eGFR 76 allow starting now. The duplication alert is overridden because abaloparatide is completed.

forbidden.why: Bisphosphonate-associated scleritis after zoledronic acid in 2019, recorded as an adverse drug reaction: bisphosphonate-induced ocular inflammation recurs on rechallenge (oral or intravenous), and scleritis threatens vision.
NSTEMI on 2023-11-08 (within the past year): romosozumab carries an FDA boxed warning and must not be initiated within a year of myocardial infarction or stroke.

Raloxifene carries a boxed warning for increased risk of death from stroke in women with documented coronary disease (and VTE); estrogen therapy is not appropriate after a recent myocardial infarction.
Abaloparatide labeling does not recommend cumulative use beyond 2 years; she has completed 24 months.
Denosumab 120 mg every 4 weeks (Xgeva) is the oncology regimen; the osteoporosis dose is 60 mg every 6 months.

extras.why: Checking calcium and vitamin D before and 1-2 weeks after the first denosumab dose is reasonable (labeling: correct hypocalcemia before starting).
Repeat DXA in 1-2 years to monitor response.
Dental evaluation before antiresorptive therapy (osteonecrosis of the jaw prevention).
Continuing or adjusting calcium and vitamin D supplementation is standard with denosumab.
Fall prevention and exercise therapy for a patient with prior fragility fractures.
Bone turnover markers to confirm suppression on denosumab.

tasks.title: Pruritic Papular Rash Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Itchy rash: please complete the plan
tasks.request: Three weeks of intensely itchy rash, worse at night, not better with the cream from urgent care. Examined by the physician assistant today; findings are in the chart. Please complete the evaluation and place treatment orders.
facts: Mite and eggs on scraping; dermoscopic delta-wing sign

required.why: Classic scabies (nocturnal itch, burrows in finger webs and wrists, scrotal nodules, dermoscopic delta-wing sign, mite and eggs on scraping, itchy bed partner; no crusting) not improved by a topical corticosteroid. Permethrin 5% is first-line but is excluded by patch-test-confirmed allergic contact dermatitis to permethrin. Oral ivermectin 200 mcg/kg is the guideline alternative (CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021; IACS): 92 kg x 0.2 mg/kg = 18.4 mg, given as 18 mg (six 3 mg tablets), repeated in 7-14 days. Spinosad 0.9% suspension (FDA-approved for scabies) or 5-10% precipitated sulfur ointment are accepted topical alternatives.

forbidden.why: Patch-test-confirmed allergic contact dermatitis to permethrin with a severe blistering reaction in 2022: permethrin is contraindicated (labeling: hypersensitivity to permethrin or pyrethroids).
Lindane carries an FDA boxed warning for neurotoxicity and seizures, is second-line only and is to be avoided in patients with seizure disorders (focal epilepsy, seizure in 2022).

extras.why: An antihistamine for nocturnal itch is reasonable symptomatic care.
A low- or mid-potency topical corticosteroid for post-scabetic itch alongside the scabicide is reasonable.
Scabies acquired from a sexual partner warrants screening for other sexually transmitted infections (CDC 2021).
Dermatology referral is reasonable if the rash does not clear.

tasks.title: Thyroid Medication Management and Follow-up Planning
tasks.subject: Thyroid hormone results
tasks.request: Thyroid hormone results collected 2024-05-30 for a patient on levothyroxine; all values are within the laboratory reference range. Ordered by the obstetrics clinic. Please review.
facts: Confirmed intrauterine pregnancy at about 6 weeks
TSH 3.9 on 2024-05-30 (within the lab range, above the pregnancy target)
Prenatal iron taken at bedtime, separated from levothyroxine

required.why: Treated Hashimoto hypothyroidism with a newly confirmed pregnancy (6-7 weeks). Levothyroxine requirements rise by 20-30% from early gestation; TSH has risen from 1.6 before conception to 3.9, inside the non-pregnant reference range but above the first-trimester target (below 2.5 mIU/L or the lower half of a trimester-specific range), and free T4 has fallen to 1.0. ATA 2017 pregnancy guideline: increase levothyroxine by about 25-30% on confirmation of pregnancy, e.g. 100 to 125 mcg daily, or two extra daily doses per week (9 doses weekly). Absorption is not the cause: she takes levothyroxine fasting at 6 am and the iron-containing prenatal vitamin at bedtime, so the interaction alert is acknowledged and overridden.
In pregnancy, TSH (with free or total T4) is checked about every 4 weeks until mid-gestation and after every dose change (ATA 2017).

forbidden.why: ATA 2017 recommends against liothyronine or desiccated thyroid in pregnancy; levothyroxine is the treatment of choice (fetal brain depends on maternal T4).
She is hypothyroid on replacement; antithyroid drugs are not indicated.
A dose reduction would worsen maternal hypothyroxinemia in early pregnancy.

extras.why: Free or total T4 alongside TSH is standard pregnancy monitoring.
Coordinating with obstetrics is reasonable.
Continuing the prenatal vitamin is appropriate.

tasks.title: Chronic Urticaria Management Plan
tasks.subject: Chronic hives not controlled on antihistamine
tasks.request: Referring a patient with hives on most days for about 6 months that come back each time a prednisone course ends. Her antihistamine has not controlled them even at a higher dose. Please evaluate and start the next step of treatment.
facts: Cetirizine updosed to 20 mg twice daily (4-fold) with adherence
Steroid-dependent: hives return within 5 days of prednisone
No urticarial vasculitis features (wheals under 24 hours, normal CRP)

required.why: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (daily wheals for 6 months, UAS7 30) uncontrolled after more than 4 weeks of a second-generation H1 antihistamine updosed to four times the standard dose with confirmed adherence, and steroid-dependent. The 2022 EAACI/GA2LEN/EuroGuiDerm/APAAACI guideline and the AAAAI/ACAAI practice parameter make add-on omalizumab the next step. FDA-labelled CSU dosing is 150 or 300 mg subcutaneously every 4 weeks, independent of weight or IgE (the guideline starts at 300 mg). Total IgE 210 IU/mL predicts a good response. Omalizumab has no renal toxicity, so it suits her IgA nephropathy. The boxed-warning anaphylaxis alert is acknowledged and overridden: the first doses are given in clinic with observation.

forbidden.why: Cyclosporine is the guideline step after omalizumab failure only, and it is contraindicated here: IgA nephropathy with eGFR 52, proteinuria 640 mg/g and uncontrolled hypertension (148/94). Cyclosporine is nephrotoxic and raises blood pressure (label: contraindicated with abnormal renal function or uncontrolled hypertension in non-transplant indications).

Steroid-dependent CSU after two bursts with relapse within 5 days: guidelines advise against repeated or long-term systemic corticosteroids, which also worsen her hypertension and kidney disease. The plan is steroid-sparing therapy.

extras.why: Continuing (or re-prescribing) the updosed second-generation H1 antihistamine alongside omalizumab is guideline practice.
An epinephrine auto-injector is reasonable for recurrent angioedema and when starting omalizumab (boxed anaphylaxis warning).
H2 antihistamine add-on is weakly supported but low risk; tolerated as an extra.
Guideline baseline or response-predictor tests for chronic spontaneous urticaria.
Scheduling in-clinic administration and observation for the first omalizumab doses.

tasks.title: Headache Classification and Management Plan
tasks.subject: Change in headache pattern
tasks.request: Patient with a past diagnosis of migraine now has three weeks of severe one-sided headaches that wake him at night. Please classify the headache disorder and advise on treatment.
facts: Ipsilateral autonomic features (eyelid droop, tearing, rhinorrhea)
Sumatriptan stopped after the coronary event
Conduction and ventricular function allow verapamil: PR 168 ms, LVEF 55%

required.why: Episodic cluster headache (ICHD-3 3.1.1): strictly unilateral orbital-temporal attacks of 45-90 minutes, 1-3 per day with nocturnal attacks, ipsilateral lacrimation, rhinorrhea and ptosis, restlessness, and bouts in 2019 and 2021 with remission between. A bout lasting weeks with daily attacks warrants prevention; verapamil is first-line (AHS 2016 cluster guideline; EHF and EAN consensus). Nothing contraindicates it: LVEF 55%, PR 168 ms, heart rate 74, and no beta-blocker since October 2023. FDA tablet strengths cover the accepted per-dose set: immediate release 40, 80 or 120 mg, extended release 120, 180 or 240 mg. The verapamil-atorvastatin interaction alert is low relevance (no labelled atorvastatin limit with verapamil) and is acknowledged and overridden.

forbidden.why: Triptans by any route (including subcutaneous or nasal sumatriptan and nasal zolmitriptan, otherwise first-line acute cluster treatment) are contraindicated with coronary artery disease and prior myocardial infarction (FDA labels); sumatriptan was stopped after his 2022 NSTEMI.
Ergot alkaloids are vasoconstrictors contraindicated in coronary artery disease.

extras.why: High-flow 100% oxygen (12-15 L/min by non-rebreather mask) is first-line acute cluster treatment (AHS Level A) and safe with coronary disease.
A short corticosteroid taper is accepted transitional therapy while verapamil is titrated.
A baseline ECG before verapamil and before each dose increase is recommended.
Greater occipital nerve block with corticosteroid is an evidence-based transitional treatment (AHS Level A).
Not needed (stereotyped recurrence, normal exam, normal 2021 brain and pituitary MRI) but tolerated.
Melatonin (AHS Level C) or galcanezumab (FDA-approved for episodic cluster headache) as an add-on preventive is tolerated; galcanezumab does not replace first-line verapamil here.

tasks.title: Iron Overload Management in Transfusion-Dependent MDS
tasks.subject: MRI liver iron quantification finalized
tasks.request: MRI liver and cardiac iron quantification is final for a patient followed in the MDS clinic. The referring hematologist asks for a chelation recommendation; the patient stopped her previous chelator because of side effects and is worried about restarting treatment.
facts: Prior dispersible deferasirox 1250 mg, about 20 mg/kg, stopped for GI intolerance
Liver iron 14.2 mg Fe/g dry weight
Patient declines subcutaneous infusion therapy, prefers a tablet

required.why: Chelation remains indicated: lower-risk MDS with ongoing transfusion dependence (34 units in 12 months), ferritin 2860 ng/mL and LIC 14.2 mg Fe/g dry weight (NCCN MDS: chelation for ferritin above 2500 in lower-risk disease). Dispersible deferasirox (Exjade) 20 mg/kg was stopped for GI intolerance. Film-coated deferasirox (Jadenu, or the granule formulation with the same dosing) has better GI tolerability (ECLIPSE). The FDA label requires a dose about 30% lower when converting from the dispersible tablets: 14 mg/kg, which at 64 kg is 896 mg, rounded to whole 90/180/360 mg tablets as 900 mg once daily. Accepted per-dose set: 896-900 mg, plus one smallest-tablet step either side (810 or 990 mg). Renal (creatinine 0.80-0.82 on two baselines) and hepatic function permit deferasirox. Deferoxamine is not an alternative because she declines subcutaneous infusions.

forbidden.why: About 20 mg/kg: as film-coated tablets this is roughly 43% above the bioequivalent dose (a renal and hepatic toxicity risk); as dispersible tablets it repeats the regimen that caused GI intolerance.
Deferiprone carries a boxed warning for agranulocytosis. The label says not to start it with ANC below 1.5; her ANC is 1.3 with chronic MDS-related neutropenia.
Serum erythropoietin 720 mIU/mL (above 500) with transfusion dependence predicts a very low ESA response rate (NCCN MDS); not indicated.

extras.why: Luspatercept is appropriate to reduce transfusion burden in SF3B1-mutated MDS with ring sideroblasts and erythropoietin above 500 (FDA 2020, MEDALIST; NCCN).
Continuing folic acid.
Monthly ferritin monitoring on chelation.
The deferasirox label recommends auditory and ophthalmic examination before starting and yearly.
Monthly urine protein monitoring on deferasirox.
Continuing scheduled red cell transfusions.

tasks.title: Skin Rash Evaluation and Treatment
tasks.subject: Itchy rash around both eyes
tasks.request: Patient added to today's schedule for an itchy, swollen rash around both eyes for 3 weeks. Please evaluate and treat.
facts: IOP rose to 34 mmHg on prednisolone acetate drops
Primary open-angle glaucoma with field loss
Acrylic gel manicures started 5 weeks ago

required.why: Bilateral eyelid allergic contact dermatitis, most likely from acrylates in gel manicures (eyelids are a classic transfer site for nail allergens). Periocular corticosteroids of any potency can raise intraocular pressure. She has glaucoma with visual field loss and a documented steroid response (34 mmHg on prednisolone acetate), so a topical calcineurin inhibitor is the safe anti-inflammatory for the eyelids: tacrolimus 0.03% or 0.1% ointment, or pimecrolimus 1% cream, twice daily. This follows the AAD 2023 guideline for sensitive sites and contact dermatitis reviews of eyelid dermatitis. The boxed-warning alert is low relevance for short intermittent eyelid use and is acknowledged and overridden.

forbidden.why: Topical or ophthalmic corticosteroids on or near the eyelids can raise intraocular pressure. She has glaucoma with an arcuate field defect and a documented steroid response (IOP 34 mmHg on prednisolone acetate).

Systemic (or any other) prednisone, prednisolone or dexamethasone: systemic corticosteroids are not indicated for localized eyelid dermatitis and also raise intraocular pressure in a known steroid responder with glaucoma.

extras.why: Patch testing (including acrylates and tosylamide resin) to confirm the allergen is recommended for eyelid dermatitis.
Ophthalmology input or an IOP check is reasonable in a glaucoma patient with periocular inflammation.
A bland emollient barrier is standard adjunctive care.
A non-sedating oral antihistamine for itch is of limited benefit but harmless.

tasks.title: Pulsatile Tinnitus Evaluation and Diagnostic Workup
tasks.subject: Urgent: new right-sided pulsatile tinnitus
tasks.request: Please see urgently: six weeks of right-sided pulsatile tinnitus in time with her heartbeat, with daily headaches. Optometry found swollen optic discs last week. Please evaluate and order the indicated workup.
facts: Papilledema Frisén grade 2 with transient visual obscurations
Venous features: tinnitus stops with ipsilateral neck compression
Ferromagnetic intraocular foreign body: MRI contraindicated
Renal function and pregnancy test allow iodinated contrast

required.why: Venous-type pulsatile tinnitus (louder lying down, abolished by ipsilateral jugular compression) with daily headaches, transient visual obscurations and Frisén grade 2 papilledema in an obese woman on an estrogen-containing contraceptive. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis must be excluded, along with a mass, and the transverse and sigmoid sinuses assessed (stenosis in idiopathic intracranial hypertension). MRI with MR venography is the usual first test but is contraindicated by the ferromagnetic intraocular foreign body. CT head with CT venography is the guideline alternative (AHA 2024 CVT scientific statement; IIH consensus guideline, Mollan 2018; ACR Appropriateness Criteria: tinnitus). An arterial-phase CTA alone does not adequately exclude venous thrombosis.

Comprehensive audiometry is part of every pulsatile tinnitus evaluation (AAO-HNSF tinnitus guideline; ACR): it documents the baseline and detects conductive or asymmetric loss that would change the imaging plan.

Papilledema with transient visual obscurations threatens vision; urgent neuro-ophthalmology (or ophthalmology or neurology) evaluation with formal perimetry is needed whatever the imaging shows (IIH consensus guideline). Optometry only notified the PCP.

forbidden.why: Retained ferromagnetic (steel) intraocular foreign body: MRI, MRA and MRV are contraindicated (ACR Manual on MR Safety); the 2019 ophthalmology note documents the contraindication.

extras.why: Non-contrast CT head or arterial CTA of the head and neck complements venous imaging in pulsatile tinnitus.
High-resolution CT of the temporal bone can show sigmoid sinus wall dehiscence or diverticulum.
Lumbar puncture with opening pressure is the next step once imaging excludes a mass and venous sinus thrombosis.
Pre-contrast pregnancy test or coagulation tests are reasonable extras.
Weight management is central if idiopathic intracranial hypertension is confirmed.

tasks.title: Tick-Borne Infection Workup and Co-Infection Assessment
tasks.subject: Tick-borne PCR panel and smear results
tasks.request: Tick-borne PCR panel, blood smear and blood culture results are available for a patient with recent erythema migrans who now has fever and low blood counts. Please review and act on the results.
facts: Amoxicillin stopped after a morbilliform eruption

required.why: Human granulocytic anaplasmosis (Anaplasma phagocytophilum PCR detected, neutrophil morulae) with fever, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and transaminase elevation, after erythema migrans treated with only 7 days of amoxicillin. Beta-lactams have no activity against Anaplasma. Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily (oral or IV) is first-line for anaplasmosis (CDC/IDSA tick-borne rickettsial disease guidance, Biggs 2016) and treats early Lyme disease at the same dose. A 10-14-day course covers both (IDSA/AAN/ACR 2020 Lyme guideline). Babesia is excluded (PCR not detected, smear negative). Warfarin is not a reason to avoid doxycycline: the moderate interaction alert is acknowledged and managed with an INR check in 3-5 days.

forbidden.why: Rifampin is an anaplasmosis alternative only when doxycycline cannot be used. It does not treat Lyme disease, and as a potent CYP inducer it can make warfarin ineffective, risking mechanical aortic valve thrombosis.
Amoxicillin caused a morbilliform drug eruption on 2024-05-27; re-challenge is not appropriate, and penicillins do not treat anaplasmosis.
Babesiosis is excluded (Babesia microti PCR not detected, no intraerythrocytic parasites on smear); babesiosis therapy is not indicated.

extras.why: INR check in 3-5 days after starting doxycycline, and notifying the anticoagulation clinic, is good practice on warfarin.
Following up or repeating blood cultures is reasonable with fever and a mechanical valve.
Echocardiography is tolerated if endocarditis concern persists, although an alternative diagnosis is confirmed.
Repeat smear or PCR is reasonable if fever persists beyond 48 hours on doxycycline.
Acetaminophen for fever and myalgia (NSAIDs avoided with warfarin and thrombocytopenia).

tasks.title: Rising Creatinine in a Patient on HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis
tasks.subject: Rising creatinine on PrEP
tasks.request: Creatinine 1.40 mg/dL (eGFR 44) and rising on daily oral PrEP, which was held on 5/24. She still needs HIV prevention. Kidney ultrasound is now done. Please evaluate her kidney disease and advise on and order HIV prevention that is safe for her kidneys.
facts: Cisgender woman exposed through receptive vaginal sex
Last HIV test 2024-03-18 (more than 2 months ago)
Hepatitis B immune (safe to stop tenofovir)
No tubulopathy: urine glucose negative, phosphate normal
Diabetic kidney disease features: retinopathy, albuminuria

required.why: HIV prevention remains indicated (receptive vaginal sex with a partner with detectable viral load). Estimated CrCl about 50 mL/min: F/TDF is not recommended for PrEP below 60 mL/min (CDC 2021 PrEP guideline, F/TDF label). F/TAF is not indicated for people at risk from receptive vaginal sex (FDA label; DISCOVER enrolled no cisgender women). Long-acting cabotegravir (FDA label: 600 mg IM, repeated 1 month later, then every 2 months; no renal dose adjustment) is therefore the only appropriate PrEP agent on the task date. The calcium-carbonate interaction alert applies to oral cabotegravir only and is overridden for the intramuscular product.

CDC 2021: HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody and HIV-1 RNA testing are required before the first cabotegravir injection; her last HIV test was 2024-03-18 and she has had ongoing exposure off PrEP since 2024-05-24.

forbidden.why: Emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide is not FDA-indicated for PrEP in people at risk of HIV from receptive vaginal sex (efficacy not established; CDC 2021).
Oral tenofovir/emtricitabine PrEP is inappropriate here: F/TDF is not recommended with CrCl below 60 mL/min (CrCl about 50 and falling), and F/TAF is not indicated for receptive vaginal exposure.

extras.why: An optional oral cabotegravir 30 mg lead-in before the first injection is label-concordant.
KDIGO 2022: an SGLT2 inhibitor (and finerenone) for type 2 diabetes with CKD and albuminuria is reasonable kidney protection.
Cystatin C to confirm the GFR estimate (KDIGO 2024).
Repeat quantification of albuminuria.
STI screening is part of PrEP care.
Hepatitis serology is reasonable PrEP-visit testing.

tasks.title: Incidental Lung Findings on a Coronary Calcium CT
tasks.subject: Incidental lung findings on calcium score CT
tasks.request: Coronary calcium CT on 5/14 reported incidental findings in both lung bases. She has had worsening breathlessness for several months and asks about steroids. Please evaluate and order the workup you recommend.
facts: Subpleural reticulation with traction bronchiectasis (fibrotic ILA)
Upper lungs not imaged by the calcium score CT

required.why: Fleischner Society 2020 ILA position paper and ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT 2022: a fibrotic interstitial lung abnormality (subpleural reticulation with traction bronchiectasis) with symptoms, crackles and exertional desaturation is clinically significant and needs a dedicated non-contrast HRCT (supine, prone, expiratory). The calcium-score CT omitted the upper lungs and is not an HRCT, so the recent-CT alert is overridden.
Complete PFTs with lung volumes and DLCO quantify restriction and gas-transfer impairment in suspected fibrotic ILD (Fleischner 2020; ATS/ERS); she has never had lung function testing.

forbidden.why: Empiric systemic corticosteroids before a diagnosis are not indicated for a fibrotic ILA; in IPF they are harmful (ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT strong recommendation against; PANTHER-IPF), and she has osteoporosis.
Antifibrotic therapy requires an established diagnosis (HRCT pattern and multidisciplinary discussion); it is not started from an incidental finding on a calcium-score CT.

extras.why: Connective tissue disease serologies are part of the ILD evaluation (ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT 2022).
Exertional desaturation to 91% warrants a 6-minute walk test or ambulatory oxygen assessment.
Pulmonary follow-up or ILD multidisciplinary review after the HRCT and PFTs.
Echocardiography to screen for pulmonary hypertension in fibrotic lung disease is reasonable.
Serum precipitins can be part of the hypersensitivity pneumonitis evaluation.
Vaccination is recommended in chronic lung disease.

tasks.title: Abnormal Iron Studies and Liver Tests: Hepatology Evaluation
tasks.subject: Ferritin 1,320 and abnormal liver tests
tasks.request: Ferritin 1,320 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 81% and ALT 74 U/L (5/20) in a patient with abnormal iron studies in 2019 who was lost to follow-up; liver ultrasound 5/28 shows fatty liver. Please review and place orders.

required.why: HFE C282Y homozygous hemochromatosis with iron overload (ferritin 1,320 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 81%) and liver injury: therapeutic phlebotomy (about 500 mL weekly as tolerated, target ferritin 50-100 ng/mL) is first-line (AASLD 2011, ACG 2019, EASL 2022). Hemoglobin 15.4 g/dL permits phlebotomy.

Ferritin above 1,000 ng/mL with raised aminotransferases, platelets 138 and mild splenomegaly (FIB-4 about 2.8) in hemochromatosis with coexisting MASLD carries a high risk of advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis: fibrosis must be staged by liver biopsy (ACG 2019, AASLD 2011) or liver stiffness measurement (EASL 2022).

forbidden.why: Chelation is reserved for hemochromatosis patients who cannot undergo phlebotomy (anemia, severe cardiac disease, poor venous access); with hemoglobin 15.4 g/dL phlebotomy is the standard (AASLD, ACG, EASL).
Iron supplementation is contraindicated in iron overload.

extras.why: Liver imaging (HCC surveillance if cirrhosis is confirmed) or MRI liver iron quantification is reasonable.
Hepatitis serologies and hepatitis A/B vaccination in chronic liver disease.
Variceal screening if cirrhosis is suspected (platelets 138, splenomegaly).
Iron indices to monitor phlebotomy.
Cardiac assessment for iron-related cardiomyopathy or arrhythmia is reasonable with ferritin above 1,000.
Screening for hemochromatosis complications (hypogonadism, osteoporosis, arthropathy).

tasks.title: Painful Neuropathy E-Consult: Workup and Symptom Management
tasks.subject: Burning feet: workup and treatment
tasks.request: Five months of symmetric burning foot pain and numbness waking him at night; acetaminophen has not helped. Recent labs are in the chart. Please advise on the diagnostic workup and symptom treatment and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily for 13 years
Length-dependent sensory signs with absent ankle reflexes
Pain waking him most nights; acetaminophen failed

required.why: Vitamin B12 168 pg/mL after 13 years of metformin in a patient with neuropathy: replace B12. Oral cyanocobalamin 1000-2000 mcg daily or intramuscular 1000 mcg are standard (ADA Standards of Care: periodic B12 checks and replacement on long-term metformin).

AAN practice parameter: serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation is a high-yield screen in distal symmetric polyneuropathy, with glucose and B12; monoclonal gammopathy is common at 70+ and diabetes does not exclude a second cause.

AAN 2021 painful diabetic neuropathy guideline: gabapentinoids, SNRIs, TCAs and topical capsaicin are effective. Estimated CrCl about 27 mL/min sets the doses: pregabalin label for CrCl 15-30 is 25-150 mg/day in one or two doses (25-75 mg per dose); gabapentin label for CrCl 15-29 is 200-700 mg/day (accepted as 100-300 mg up to twice daily or 400-700 mg once daily); venlafaxine total daily dose reduced by at least 50% (37.5-75 mg once daily); topical capsaicin has no renal limit. Duloxetine is avoided below CrCl 30.

forbidden.why: Duloxetine label: avoid with estimated CrCl below 30 mL/min (CrCl about 27, eGFR 25).
Pregabalin per-dose amounts of 100 mg or more exceed the label maximum for CrCl 15-30 (150 mg/day in one or two doses); extended-release pregabalin is not recommended below CrCl 30.
forbidden.dose: 100 or 150 or 200 or 225 or 300 or 330 mg

forbidden.why: Gabapentin doses of 800 mg or more per dose exceed the label maximum for CrCl 15-29 (700 mg/day); Gralise and gabapentin enacarbil are not recommended below CrCl 30.

extras.why: Nerve conduction studies are reasonable but not required for a typical length-dependent diabetic neuropathy.
Confirming B12 deficiency or testing for pernicious anemia is reasonable.
In-person neurology or podiatry for diabetic foot care.
Topical lidocaine is a low-risk adjunct.
Other metabolic screening labs are low-risk extras.

tasks.title: Positive Interferon-Gamma Release Assay in a Kidney Transplant Candidate
tasks.subject: Positive TB blood test in transplant candidate
tasks.request: Positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold Plus on pre-transplant screening; chest radiograph now done. She asks whether her childhood BCG vaccine explains the result. Please evaluate, advise on clearance for listing and place the treatment orders you recommend.
facts: On apixaban that must continue (rifamycin interaction)
BCG as an infant (question to answer)

required.why: Positive IGRA, no symptoms, stable weight, normal chest radiograph and no pyuria: active (including genitourinary) TB is excluded and LTBI should be treated before transplantation (KDIGO 2020 transplant candidate guideline; CDC/NTCA 2020). The preferred rifamycin regimens (3HP, 4R, 3HR) are inappropriate because rifampin and rifapentine are strong CYP3A4/P-gp inducers and the apixaban label advises avoiding them; they would also interact with post-transplant tacrolimus. Isoniazid for 6-9 months is the alternative: 5 mg/kg up to 300 mg daily, or 15 mg/kg up to 900 mg twice weekly by DOT; no renal dose adjustment, so the CKD alert is overridden.
Chronic kidney disease (uremia) is a risk factor for isoniazid neuropathy: pyridoxine 25-50 mg daily is recommended (CDC LTBI guidance; ATS/CDC/IDSA).

forbidden.why: Rifampin and rifapentine (3HP, 4R, 3HR) markedly lower apixaban levels (apixaban label: avoid combined strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inducers) in a patient whose cardiologist wants anticoagulation continued; rifabutin also induces CYP3A4 and is not a guideline LTBI regimen.
Active tuberculosis is excluded (asymptomatic, stable weight, normal chest radiograph, no pyuria); multidrug active-TB therapy is not indicated.

extras.why: Baseline and symptom-driven liver tests during isoniazid therapy.
HIV and hepatitis screening are recommended with LTBI treatment (results from 2024-04-22 already available).
Communication or follow-up with the transplant team.

tasks.title: Unilateral Tinnitus: Imaging Assessment
tasks.subject: Left tinnitus and hearing asymmetry
tasks.request: Four months of left-sided tinnitus; audiogram from 5/21 is in the chart. He had a brain scan in 2019 and asks whether more imaging is needed. Please advise on the workup and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Anaphylaxis documented on the problem list
2019 MRI had no posterior fossa thin sections

required.why: Unilateral non-pulsatile tinnitus with asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss (30-40 dB at 2-4 kHz) and poor left word recognition requires MRI of the internal auditory canals to exclude vestibular schwannoma (ACR Appropriateness Criteria; AAO-HNS tinnitus guideline). The 2019 brain MRI (5 mm slices, no posterior fossa thin sections) does not exclude a small intracanalicular tumor. With documented gadobutrol anaphylaxis, non-contrast high-resolution heavily T2-weighted 3D MRI (FIESTA/CISS), which detects vestibular schwannoma with sensitivity close to contrast-enhanced MRI, is the appropriate protocol (ACR Manual on Contrast Media: consider non-contrast alternatives after a severe reaction). The order must state the non-contrast protocol in its name or reason.

forbidden.why: Documented anaphylaxis to gadobutrol (hypotension 74/40, epinephrine twice); an equally appropriate non-contrast MRI protocol exists, so a gadolinium-enhanced study is ruled out.
Any gadolinium-based contrast agent is ruled out by the documented anaphylaxis.

extras.why: Auditory brainstem response testing is a reasonable adjunct, though less sensitive than MRI.
Neurotology or otology review of the result.
Hearing rehabilitation, tinnitus management or repeat audiometry.
Vestibular testing is a tolerated adjunct.
Allergy evaluation of the gadolinium reaction for future imaging decisions.

tasks.title: Post-Emergency Follow-Up: New Atrial Fibrillation and Acute Monoarthritis
tasks.subject: ED follow-up: palpitations and swollen knee
tasks.request: Seen 5/29 with new atrial fibrillation and an acutely swollen right knee that was aspirated. Rate control was started in the ED; stroke prevention and treatment of the knee were deferred to primary care. He is in clinic today. Please complete the plan and place the orders.
facts: Verapamil ER 180 mg daily started in the ED
Monosodium urate crystals in knee fluid

required.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age >=75 = 2, hypertension = 1): oral anticoagulation is indicated (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline; a DOAC is preferred). The 1.3 mg/dL creatinine was retracted (mislabeled specimen); the recollected creatinine is 1.62 mg/dL, consistent with his CKD 3b baseline of 1.5-1.7. Apixaban label: two of age >=80, weight <=60 kg, creatinine >=1.5 mg/dL means 2.5 mg twice daily; he meets age (81-84) and creatinine (1.62), so 2.5 mg twice daily (on the erroneous 1.3 he would have looked eligible for 5 mg). Cockcroft-Gault CrCl = (140 - 81..84) x 70.2 / (72 x 1.62) = about 34-36 mL/min, so edoxaban 30 mg once daily (CrCl 15-50). Rivaroxaban is excluded because verapamil is a combined P-gp and moderate CYP3A inhibitor and his CrCl is 15-80 (label: avoid).

Crystal-proven gout flare of the right knee (negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals, synovial culture negative). ACR 2020 gout guideline: colchicine, NSAIDs or glucocorticoids are first line, but colchicine is contraindicated (verapamil, a P-gp and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, with renal impairment: colchicine label) and NSAIDs are avoided (anticoagulation being started, CKD 3b, age over 80). Oral prednisone or prednisolone 30-40 mg/day (about 0.5 mg/kg) for 5-10 days (accepted 20-60 mg), a methylprednisolone dose pack, or an intra-articular or intramuscular corticosteroid are appropriate.
Transthoracic echocardiogram for new atrial fibrillation (chamber size, LV function, valve disease); he has never had one. TSH was already checked in the emergency department.

forbidden.why: Colchicine label: contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment who take a P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor; verapamil is a P-gp and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and he has CKD 3b (CrCl about 35).
NSAIDs with a new anticoagulant, CKD 3b and age over 80: bleeding and kidney injury risk (AGS Beers 2023: avoid NSAIDs with anticoagulants and with CrCl <30; ACR prefers alternatives in CKD).
The creatinine of 1.3 that would make him eligible for 5 mg was retracted; with age >=80 and creatinine 1.62 the label dose is 2.5 mg twice daily.
Rivaroxaban label: avoid in patients with CrCl 15 to <80 mL/min who receive a combined P-gp and moderate CYP3A inhibitor (verapamil).
Edoxaban label: CrCl 15-50 mL/min requires 30 mg once daily (CrCl about 34-36).
No vascular indication; adding an antiplatelet to anticoagulation raises bleeding risk.
ACR 2020: start allopurinol at no more than 100 mg/day (less in CKD stage 4 or worse) to reduce the risk of hypersensitivity syndrome.

extras.why: ACR 2020 conditionally supports starting low-dose urate-lowering therapy after a first flare with CKD stage 3 or worse, including during the flare with anti-inflammatory cover.
Inflammatory markers and serum urate monitoring are low-risk.
Knee radiograph or an intra-articular injection procedure is reasonable.
Low-risk baseline AF testing.
Specialist referral is reasonable.

tasks.title: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Consultation: Rising Creatinine
tasks.subject: PrEP: creatinine rising on Truvada
tasks.request: Truvada stopped 5/20 because his creatinine rose to 1.61. He wants to stay on HIV prevention and is interested in a long-acting injectable. Please advise on the best option and place the orders.

required.why: Two linked problems decide the regimen. (1) Hepatitis B: HBsAg reactive with core antibody on the 2021 outside intake report, never followed up; the PrEP tenofovir has been suppressing HBV, and ALT rose to 156 within two weeks of stopping it (withdrawal flare). A tenofovir-containing regimen must be resumed; cabotegravir or lenacapavir have no HBV activity (CDC 2021 PrEP guideline; AASLD HBV guidance). (2) Kidney: Cockcroft-Gault CrCl = (140 - 38..45) x 64 / (72 x 1.61) = about 52-56 mL/min, below 60, so emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate is not recommended for PrEP (label), and the creatinine rise, proteinuria, hypophosphatemia and euglycemic glycosuria suggest TDF tubulopathy. Emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 200/25 mg daily (label: CrCl >=30; men who have sex with men) treats HBV and provides PrEP; TAF is preferred over TDF for HBV with renal dysfunction (AASLD).
Quantitative HBV DNA characterizes the HBsAg-positive infection and the withdrawal flare and is the baseline for monitoring on tenofovir (AASLD).
CDC 2021 PrEP guideline: an HIV test (antigen/antibody, plus HIV RNA after recent exposure) is required before restarting PrEP; the last test was 2024-02-12 and exposures are ongoing.

forbidden.why: HBsAg reactive: long-acting cabotegravir or lenacapavir have no HBV activity, so tenofovir would stay off and the hepatitis flare would continue (CDC 2021 PrEP guideline).
Estimated CrCl about 52-56 mL/min (<60): TDF/FTC is not recommended for PrEP, and TDF is the probable cause of the kidney decline.
Single-agent HBV therapy does not provide HIV PrEP and, if HIV is acquired, selects resistant virus; a single F/TAF tablet covers both.

extras.why: HBeAg, hepatitis D antibody, hepatitis A immunity and confirmatory HBsAg are part of the initial HBV evaluation.
Liver or kidney imaging and fibrosis assessment are reasonable.
Urine studies for proximal tubulopathy are reasonable.
Routine sexually transmitted infection screening at a PrEP visit.
Synthetic function during a hepatitis flare.
Hepatology or nephrology referral is reasonable.

tasks.title: Cancer-Associated Deep Vein Thrombosis: Treatment Selection
tasks.subject: New DVT: treatment needed
tasks.request: Left femoral-popliteal DVT diagnosed overnight. No anticoagulant was started, pending your review of his cancer therapy and kidney function. He is in clinic this morning; nursing intake and recent labs are in the chart. Please start treatment and address any other issue that needs action today.
facts: Measured weight 82.0 kg; ED 96 kg incorrect
On denosumab; never started calcium/vitamin D

required.why: Cancer-associated proximal DVT needs anticoagulation (ASCO 2023, ASH 2021). Enzalutamide is a strong CYP3A4 inducer: apixaban and rivaroxaban labels say avoid combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers, and enzalutamide labeling advises avoiding warfarin. Measured weight is 82.0 kg (the 96 kg ED weight was a stated weight from last year, corrected by nursing). Cockcroft-Gault CrCl = (140 - 74..79) x 82 / (72 x 2.7) = about 26-28 mL/min (<30; with 96 kg it would wrongly be 30-33). Enoxaparin label for CrCl <30: 1 mg/kg once daily = 82 mg, so 80 mg (accepted 70-90 mg) once daily; twice-daily dosing and 1 mg/kg of 96 kg are wrong. Dalteparin once daily (with anti-Xa monitoring) and unfractionated heparin are accepted alternatives.

Symptomatic hypocalcemia on denosumab (calcium 7.4, corrected about 8.0 mg/dL, ionized 0.98 mmol/L, perioral tingling and cramps) with 25-hydroxyvitamin D 12 ng/mL and CKD 4. Denosumab (Xgeva) labeling: correct hypocalcemia and give calcium and vitamin D as needed; CrCl <30 raises the risk of severe hypocalcemia. Vitamin D repletion (cholecalciferol or ergocalciferol; calcitriol is reasonable in CKD 4) is required.
Symptomatic denosumab-associated hypocalcemia needs calcium replacement (oral elemental calcium 1-2 g/day, or IV calcium gluconate if severe), with close monitoring because of CKD 4.

forbidden.why: Enzalutamide is a strong CYP3A4 inducer: apixaban and rivaroxaban labels say avoid combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (loss of efficacy).
CrCl <30 requires once-daily enoxaparin, and the dose must use the measured 82 kg, not the retracted 96 kg stated weight.
Fondaparinux label: contraindicated with CrCl <30 mL/min.
Dabigatran label: no VTE treatment dosing for CrCl <=30 mL/min.
Enzalutamide labeling: avoid warfarin (CYP2C9 induction); LMWH is preferred for cancer VTE when DOACs are unsuitable.
Tinzaparin increased mortality in elderly patients with renal insufficiency (IRIS trial).
Already on denosumab; zoledronic acid is not recommended with CrCl <30 and would worsen hypocalcemia.

extras.why: A peak anti-Xa level after the third or fourth dose is recommended for LMWH with CrCl <30.
Repeat calcium, ionized calcium and PTH monitoring.
ECG for QT interval in symptomatic hypocalcemia.
Nephrology input or compression stockings are reasonable.
Compression stockings for symptoms.

tasks.title: Antidepressant Substitution After an Abnormal ECG
tasks.subject: Antidepressant change after ECG over-read
tasks.request: Citalopram and chlorthalidone stopped today after the cardiology ECG over-read and recent labs. She is on methadone through her treatment program and wants to stay on an antidepressant. Please choose a replacement and manage the ECG and lab findings; place the orders you recommend.

required.why: Recurrent depression needs continued treatment after citalopram was stopped for QTc 512 ms on methadone. Sertraline has the least QT effect among SSRIs and no methadone-raising interaction (start 25-50 mg, accepted up to 100 mg); bupropion (no seizure or eating disorder history) and vortioxetine have no meaningful QT effect. Escitalopram, tricyclics and fluvoxamine are avoided (2018 AHA/ACC/HRS ventricular arrhythmia guideline; FDA citalopram QT warning; CredibleMeds).

The 4.5 mmol/L potassium was hemolyzed and is invalid; the last valid potassium is 3.0 mmol/L after chlorthalidone, with QTc 512 ms and U waves. Hypokalemia must be corrected (target 4.0 or above in QT prolongation).
Magnesium 1.4 mg/dL from the thiazide contributes to QT prolongation and impairs potassium repletion; replace magnesium (target 2.0 or above).

Repeat ECG after electrolyte correction and citalopram withdrawal to confirm QTc improvement on methadone 90 mg (AHA scientific statement on drug-induced QT prolongation; SAMHSA methadone QT guidance).

forbidden.why: Dose-dependent QT prolongation (FDA warning); QTc 512 ms with methadone.
Tricyclic antidepressants prolong QT and are arrhythmogenic.
Fluvoxamine inhibits methadone metabolism and raises methadone levels, worsening QT prolongation.
Known QT-prolonging drugs with QTc 512 ms on methadone.
The thiazide caused the hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia driving the QT prolongation.

extras.why: A replacement antihypertensive (ideally potassium-neutral or potassium-sparing) is reasonable after the thiazide was stopped.
Recollection of the hemolyzed potassium and electrolyte monitoring.
Cardiology or psychiatry input or psychotherapy are reasonable.

tasks.title: Urgent Rheumatology Consultation: New Headache in an Older Adult
tasks.subject: Urgent: new temporal headache, ESR 88
tasks.request: Three weeks of new temporal headache with jaw pain on chewing, tender temporal artery, ESR 88 and CRP 64. No visual symptoms. Please see urgently, start management, arrange confirmation, and address her bone health during treatment.

required.why: Probable giant cell arteritis (age over 50, new temporal headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, abnormal temporal artery, ESR 88, CRP 64; ACR/EULAR 2022 criteria). ACR 2021 GCA guideline: start high-dose oral glucocorticoid without waiting for confirmation; prednisone 1 mg/kg up to 60 mg (48 kg: 40-60 mg accepted, or methylprednisolone 32-48 mg). No visual symptoms, so IV pulse therapy is not needed.
ACR 2021: temporal artery biopsy (or temporal artery ultrasound in experienced centers) to confirm GCA, ideally within 2 weeks of starting glucocorticoids.

High fracture risk on long-term glucocorticoids: prior low-energy distal radius fracture (2021, older orthopedic note) with femoral neck T-score -2.2 and age over 75 (ACR 2022 glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis guideline: treat adults with prior fragility fracture). The eGFR of 46 looks adequate, but Cockcroft-Gault CrCl = (140 - 77..81) x 48 x 0.85 / (72 x 1.2) = about 28-30 mL/min, below the labeled limits for alendronate and zoledronic acid (35) and for risedronate and ibandronate (30). Denosumab 60 mg every 6 months (calcium and vitamin D normal), teriparatide 20 mcg daily or abaloparatide 80 mcg daily are appropriate.

forbidden.why: Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about 28-30 mL/min: alendronate not recommended and zoledronic acid contraindicated below 35; risedronate and ibandronate not recommended below 30.
A polymyalgia-range prednisone dose (25 mg or less) undertreats GCA with jaw claudication and risks vision loss.

extras.why: ACR 2022: calcium and vitamin D for all adults on prolonged glucocorticoids.
Gastric protection is reasonable at her age on high-dose glucocorticoids.
ACR 2021 conditionally recommends tocilizumab with glucocorticoids for newly diagnosed GCA.
Large-vessel imaging and ophthalmology review are reasonable.
Baseline and pre-biologic screening labs, inflammatory marker monitoring and repeat densitometry are low-risk.

tasks.title: Migraine Classification and Preventive Treatment Plan
tasks.subject: Migraine: preventive treatment consult
tasks.request: Migraine frequency has increased to about 9 days per month with missed work despite an effective triptan. Please assess, start preventive treatment and advise on imaging.
facts: No red flags; normal neurological exam

required.why: Nine migraine days per month with severe disability (MIDAS 24) warrants prevention. She stopped contraception on 2024-03-01 to conceive, so the preventive must be compatible with an early unrecognized pregnancy: propranolol or metoprolol (beta-blockers with the most pregnancy experience) or low-dose amitriptyline or nortriptyline. Topiramate and valproate are teratogens, candesartan (and other RAS blockers) is fetotoxic, and CGRP-pathway drugs lack pregnancy data and carry long washouts (AHS 2021 consensus; ACOG; product labels).

forbidden.why: Actively trying to conceive: topiramate (oral clefts, low birth weight) and valproate (neural tube defects, neurodevelopmental harm) are contraindicated without highly effective contraception.
ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers are fetotoxic (boxed warning) in a woman trying to conceive.
No adequate pregnancy data; monoclonal antibodies persist about 5 months after the last dose; not appropriate when conception is being attempted.
Opioids and butalbital are not recommended for migraine and promote medication-overuse headache.

extras.why: Refill of the effective acute triptan, limited to under 10 days per month.
Adjunct nutraceutical prevention (AHS level B), compatible with conception planning.
Antiemetic for migraine-associated nausea, acceptable in early pregnancy.

tasks.title: Diabetes Management Reassessment After Marked A1C Improvement
tasks.subject: Hemoglobin A1c 6.2%
tasks.request: Hemoglobin A1c 6.2% on 2024-05-29 (10.4% in November 2023). Please review the diabetes regimen.

required.why: A 72-80-year-old man living alone with A1c 6.2%, recurrent fasting hypoglycemia (5 readings below 70) and a nocturnal level 3 event (48 mg/dL, needed assistance) after self-titrating glargine to 30 units: reduce the basal dose by at least 10-20% (to 27 units or less; up to a 50% cut, 15 units, is reasonable after a severe event) and relax the target (ADA Standards of Care 2024, older adults A1c <7.0-7.5% and hypoglycemia avoidance).
Repeat A1c in about 3 months to confirm the new target is met without hypoglycemia.

forbidden.why: Renewing or increasing basal insulin at 28 units or more a day continues the dose that produced a severe nocturnal hypoglycemic event.
Adding a sulfonylurea or glinide to an over-treated older adult on insulin increases hypoglycemia risk.
Prandial insulin is not indicated with A1c 6.2% and hypoglycemia.

extras.why: Glucagon is recommended for anyone on insulin at risk of level 2 or 3 hypoglycemia (ADA 2024).
Continuous glucose monitoring for an older insulin user with nocturnal hypoglycemia.
Diabetes education on hypoglycemia and dose adjustment.

tasks.title: Travel-Related Parasitic Infection Evaluation
tasks.subject: Eosinophilia after years of work abroad
tasks.request: Persistent eosinophilia (2.6 x10^3/uL) with recurrent forearm swelling after 4 years of work abroad. Please evaluate and treat.
facts: Long residence in the Cameroonian rainforest
Worm seen under the conjunctiva (urgent care note)

required.why: Calabar-type migratory forearm swellings and a worm seen crossing the conjunctiva after years in the Cameroonian rainforest, with eosinophilia and high IgE, indicate loiasis. Before any ivermectin or diethylcarbamazine, the Loa loa microfilarial load must be quantified on blood drawn between 10:00 and 14:00 (diurnal periodicity), because loads above 2,500-8,000/mL risk fatal encephalopathy with treatment (CDC; IDSA/ASTMH guidance).

forbidden.why: Empiric ivermectin for eosinophilia (presumptive Strongyloides treatment) in a Loa loa-exposed patient before the microfilarial load is known risks post-treatment encephalopathy.
Diethylcarbamazine is the definitive drug for loiasis but must not be given before the microfilarial load is quantified (encephalopathy, Mazzotti-type reactions).

extras.why: Filarial serology or Loa PCR supports the diagnosis.
Strongyloides serology is part of every eosinophilia workup after tropical residence.
Repeat stool microscopy is reasonable.
Ophthalmology examination after a subconjunctival worm.

tasks.title: Unilateral Tinnitus: Second Opinion and Imaging Decision
tasks.subject: Second opinion: left tinnitus before scheduled ear surgery
tasks.request: Left-sided tinnitus and low-frequency hearing loss; an outside otolaryngologist has booked her for left ear surgery on 2024-06-24. She would like a second opinion first. Outside audiology and consultation notes are scanned into the chart.
facts: Supranormal bone conduction -10 dB HL at low frequencies
Autophony including footsteps and eye movements
Outside diagnosis of otosclerosis with stapedotomy booked

required.why: Left low-frequency 'conductive' loss with supranormal bone conduction (-10 dB HL at 250 and 500 Hz), present acoustic reflexes and type A tympanograms, plus autophony (own voice, footsteps, eye movements) and sound- and strain-induced vertigo (Tullio and Hennebert phenomena), indicates a third-window lesion, most often superior semicircular canal dehiscence, not otosclerosis: stapes fixation abolishes the acoustic reflexes and does not produce supranormal bone conduction. High-resolution (thin-section, about 0.5-0.6 mm) CT of the temporal bones with reformats in the plane of the superior canal (Poschl and Stenvers) is the imaging test of choice.
