forbidden.why: The air-bone gap is from a third window, not stapes fixation (acoustic reflexes present, supranormal bone conduction). Stapes surgery will not close the gap and risks sensorineural hearing loss and vertigo.

extras.why: Cervical and ocular VEMP (low thresholds, large amplitudes) support a third-window lesion; vestibular testing and electrocochleography are reasonable.
Neurotology referral for confirmation and surgical counselling if dehiscence is confirmed.
MRI of the internal auditory canals, repeat audiometry with reflexes and a hearing aid evaluation are reasonable and not harmful.

tasks.title: Thrombocytopenia and Anticoagulation in a Patient on Immunotherapy
tasks.subject: Anticoagulation with immune-related thrombocytopenia
tasks.request: Immune-related thrombocytopenia on checkpoint inhibitor therapy (platelets 34, now 41 on prednisone). Full-dose anticoagulation has been stopped. Please advise on anticoagulation and enter the order.

required.why: Cancer-associated DVT and PE diagnosed 6 months ago (beyond the first 30 days) with platelets 25-50 x10^3/uL: continue anticoagulation at half the therapeutic dose or a prophylactic dose of LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg once or twice daily, or about 1 mg/kg once daily, 80 mg) until platelets exceed 50 x10^3/uL, then resume full dose; hold only below 25 (ISTH SSC guidance 2018, Samuelson Bannow; ASCO VTE guideline). DOACs are avoided below 50 x10^3/uL.

forbidden.why: Full therapeutic LMWH with platelets 34-41 x10^3/uL in subacute or chronic VTE carries a high bleeding risk without the high recurrence risk of the first 30 days.
DOACs and warfarin are not recommended with platelets below 50 x10^3/uL (ISTH 2018).

extras.why: Anti-Xa monitoring on reduced-dose LMWH.

tasks.title: Inflammatory Arthritis Serologic Workup
tasks.subject: New inflammatory polyarthritis
tasks.request: About two weeks of symmetric small-joint polyarthritis with a low-positive rheumatoid factor. Please review before the rheumatology appointment and order the serologic workup you recommend.

required.why: Acute (16-day) symmetric small-joint polyarthritis in a kindergarten teacher exposed to a slapped-cheek outbreak, with a preceding febrile illness, a lacy reticular rash, mild leukopenia and anemia, low-titer RF and negative anti-CCP: acute parvovirus B19 arthritis must be confirmed with B19 IgM (ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria require exclusion of other causes; B19 can produce transient RF positivity).

forbidden.why: Arthritis of 16 days with features of acute parvovirus B19 infection is usually self-limited within weeks; starting a DMARD before the cause is established and before 6 weeks of persistence is not indicated.

extras.why: ANA is reasonable in new polyarthritis.
Hepatitis B and C serologies in new polyarthritis.
HIV testing in new polyarthritis.
Symptomatic NSAID or acetaminophen.
Reticulocyte count with B19-related anemia.

tasks.title: Pruritic Papular Rash Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Still itching after two treatments
tasks.request: Still itching everywhere after two rounds of the scabies cream, and I am not sleeping. Could I get the scabies pill or a steroid shot to settle it?
facts: Two correctly applied permethrin courses failed

required.why: Generalized pruritus with excoriated papules that failed two correctly applied permethrin courses, negative scrapings and no affected contacts, plus B symptoms (drenching night sweats, 11.3% weight loss: 74.6 to 66.2 kg in 3 months), a 2.5 cm rubbery left supraclavicular node with alcohol-induced pain, anemia, leukocytosis, eosinophilia, thrombocytosis and ESR 54 point to Hodgkin lymphoma. The next step is cross-sectional imaging (contrast CT of neck, chest, abdomen and pelvis, or PET-CT) and excisional (or core) biopsy of the node; fine-needle aspiration alone is inadequate for lymphoma (NCCN Hodgkin lymphoma 2024).

forbidden.why: Scabies is effectively excluded (two correct permethrin courses, negative scrapings and dermoscopy, no affected contacts); further scabicide delays the diagnosis.
Systemic corticosteroids can partly treat lymphoma, shrink the node and compromise the biopsy and staging; they are not indicated for unexplained pruritus.

extras.why: Urgent hematology-oncology referral, or surgical referral for excisional node biopsy.
Chest radiograph, neck ultrasound or additional CT regions are reasonable alongside the required study.
Pre-staging and pruritus laboratory workup.
Symptomatic antipruritic therapy, including a topical corticosteroid, does not interfere with diagnosis.

tasks.role: Primary Care and Addiction Medicine Physician
tasks.title: Medication Treatment Initiation for Opioid Use Disorder
tasks.subject: Starting treatment for opioid use disorder
tasks.request: Patient seen at intake 2024-05-31 wants to start medication treatment for opioid use disorder. Results finalized after the visit are in the chart. Please review and place the medication order.

required.why: Severe opioid use disorder (daily illicit fentanyl, two overdoses) newly found to have a live 6-week intrauterine pregnancy: opioid agonist treatment is the standard of care in pregnancy (ACOG Committee Opinion 711, SAMHSA 2018 clinical guidance; ASAM 2020). Sublingual buprenorphine (mono-product or buprenorphine-naloxone) started at COWS 8 or more, or referral to an opioid treatment program for methadone, are both appropriate.

forbidden.why: Extended-release naltrexone (the requested monthly non-opioid injection) is not recommended to start in pregnancy (ACOG 711; SAMHSA 2018) and would require 7-10 opioid-free days with precipitated-withdrawal risk to the pregnancy; agonist treatment is preferred.
Withdrawal management without opioid agonist treatment is not recommended in pregnancy because of the high relapse and overdose risk.

extras.why: Naloxone rescue kit renewal.
Prenatal vitamin or folic acid.
Referral for prenatal care.
Infectious disease screening for people who use drugs and at the first prenatal visit.
Symptomatic adjuncts for withdrawal during induction.

tasks.title: Kidney Function Decline in a Patient on PrEP
tasks.subject: Creatinine 1.86 in a patient on PrEP
tasks.request: Creatinine 1.86 mg/dL (H) on 2024-05-28, rising over the past year, in a patient taking HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis. PrEP was held by primary care. Please assess and advise.

required.why: Subacute kidney injury (creatinine 0.98 to 1.86) with dipstick-negative proteinuria (protein-creatinine 1.9 g/g but albumin-creatinine only 42 mg/g, so mostly non-albumin protein), new anemia, hypercalcemia, a high total protein to albumin gap (globulin 5.3 g/dL) and lucent vertebral lesions with a compression deformity: light-chain cast nephropathy from multiple myeloma must be excluded with serum free light chains and serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation (IMWG; KDIGO). Tenofovir tubulopathy does not explain hypercalcemia, anemia or bone lesions.

He remains at ongoing HIV risk and is off PrEP. Tenofovir disoproxil-emtricitabine is not recommended with creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault about 41); emtricitabine-tenofovir alafenamide (CrCl 30 or more) or long-acting cabotegravir (no renal adjustment) are appropriate (CDC PrEP guideline 2021).

forbidden.why: Tenofovir disoproxil is not recommended for PrEP with CrCl below 60 mL/min and adds tubular toxicity to an unexplained kidney injury.
NSAIDs for back pain worsen acute kidney injury, particularly with hypercalcemia and possible cast nephropathy.

extras.why: Renal ultrasound is standard in kidney function decline.
Workup of hypercalcemia.
Skeletal imaging for lytic lesions.
Hematology referral for suspected plasma cell disorder.
Urine microscopy, beta-2 microglobulin or uric acid.
HIV testing is required with every PrEP prescription.

tasks.title: Post-GI Bleed Follow-Up Assessment
tasks.subject: Follow-up after upper GI bleed
tasks.request: Discharged 2024-05-22 after an upper GI bleed. Please review the discharge summary, reconcile medications and coordinate follow-up.
facts: Aspirin held at admission, decision deferred to PCP
Clean-based ulcer, H. pylori negative, NSAID cause removed

required.why: Secondary prevention after NSTEMI with a drug-eluting stent: low-dose aspirin should be resumed as soon as hemostasis is secure (ideally within days) together with a PPI; the ulcer is clean-based, H. pylori negative and NSAID-related, and the NSAID has been stopped. Withholding aspirin increases mortality (Sung, Ann Intern Med 2010; ACG 2021 ulcer bleeding guideline; ACG-CAG 2022 antithrombotics guideline).

forbidden.why: Recent NSAID-induced ulcer bleed on aspirin with coronary disease: systemic NSAIDs, including COX-2 inhibitors, should be avoided (ACG 2009 and 2021).

extras.why: Acetaminophen for knee osteoarthritis.
Topical NSAID or capsaicin for knee osteoarthritis (minimal systemic exposure).
PPI renewal or long-term gastroprotection while on aspirin.
Iron replacement after the bleed.
Iron studies after the bleed.
GI follow-up or repeat endoscopy to document gastric ulcer healing.

tasks.title: Elevated Liver Enzymes: Fibrosis Risk Assessment
tasks.subject: Persistently elevated transaminases
tasks.request: ALT 51 and AST 46 U/L on 2024-05-14, elevated for more than 6 months in a patient with fatty liver on ultrasound. Hepatology input requested on fibrosis assessment.

required.why: MASLD with FIB-4 about 2.1-2.5 (indeterminate, 1.3-2.67) needs a second-line fibrosis test (AASLD 2023 MASLD guidance; AGA 2023 pathway). Vibration-controlled transient elastography (FibroScan) is contraindicated by the manufacturer in patients with an active implantable device such as an ICD, and MR elastography is excluded because the ICD is not MR conditional. The Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) test, another serum panel, or ultrasound shear-wave elastography is appropriate.

forbidden.why: FibroScan labeling contraindicates use in patients with an active implanted medical device such as a pacemaker or defibrillator.
The ICD generator and lead are not MR conditional.
Liver biopsy is premature with an indeterminate FIB-4 before a non-invasive second-line test.

extras.why: Cardiometabolic risk assessment in MASLD.
Hepatitis A and B immunity before vaccination.
Lifestyle and weight-loss support.

tasks.title: Persistent Olecranon Bursitis Despite Antibiotics
tasks.subject: Recurrent elbow bursitis despite antibiotics
tasks.request: Right olecranon bursitis recurring for 4 months despite two antibiotic courses and two aspirations with negative routine cultures. Please advise on next steps.
facts: Aquarium-related abrasion of the same arm (nurse note)

required.why: Chronic culture-negative olecranon bursitis with a lymphocytic aspirate, failure of two beta-lactam courses and new violaceous nodules extending along the forearm, after an aquarium-related abrasion of the same arm: Mycobacterium marinum is the leading diagnosis. Bursal fluid or tissue needs AFB smear and mycobacterial culture with incubation at 28-32 C (ATS/IDSA 2007 NTM statement; IDSA 2020 NTM guideline).

forbidden.why: Intrabursal or systemic corticosteroids in an undiagnosed chronic (probably mycobacterial) infection worsen and disseminate it.
Steroid injection into a chronically infected bursa is contraindicated.

extras.why: Surgical bursectomy or biopsy gives tissue for histology and culture.
Imaging of the elbow to assess extent and bone involvement.
Fungal culture (sporotrichosis is in the differential).
Empiric two-drug therapy for M. marinum once specimens are obtained.

tasks.title: Dermatology E-Consult: Persistent Facial Rash
tasks.subject: Persistent facial rash
tasks.request: Four months of facial rash not responding to initial treatment. Photos and history are in the e-consult. Please advise and order the recommended treatment.
facts: Spared rim at the lip border
Rebound within 3 days of stopping triamcinolone
Daily potent topical steroid on the face

required.why: Monomorphous papules and pustules around the mouth and nasolabial folds with a spared rim at the vermilion border, worsening after initial topical steroid benefit and flaring within days of stopping triamcinolone: steroid-induced perioral (periorificial) dermatitis. Treatment is to stop the topical corticosteroid and use topical metronidazole, azelaic acid or a calcineurin inhibitor, or an oral tetracycline for more extensive disease (AAD; Tolaymat, Lancet/Am J Clin Dermatol reviews).

forbidden.why: Topical corticosteroids cause and perpetuate perioral dermatitis; continuing triamcinolone or escalating potency produces rebound flares.

extras.why: Some dermatologists taper briefly through a low-potency steroid to reduce rebound after a potent one.
A combined topical and oral regimen.

tasks.title: Positive QuantiFERON in a Tuberculosis Contact: Interpretation and Management
tasks.subject: Positive QuantiFERON in a pregnant TB contact
tasks.request: Repeat QuantiFERON positive (TB1 minus nil 1.86 IU/mL) in a patient named as a household tuberculosis contact by the health department; she is asymptomatic and her shielded chest radiograph is normal. Please interpret and advise on management, including timing.
facts: Household contact of smear-positive pulmonary TB
Active TB excluded: asymptomatic, normal radiograph

required.why: Latent TB infection acquired recently: QuantiFERON negative in March 2023 and positive in May 2024 after months of household exposure to smear-positive, drug-susceptible pulmonary TB; asymptomatic with a normal shielded chest radiograph, so active TB is excluded. Pregnant at about 22 weeks. Treatment is usually deferred until 2-3 months postpartum for low-risk pregnant women, but recent infection (and HIV) carries the highest risk of progression, so CDC/ATS/NTCA advise treating during pregnancy. Isoniazid 300 mg daily (5 mg/kg, maximum 300 mg; 66 kg) for 9 months, or twice weekly 900 mg by directly observed therapy, with pyridoxine; rifampin 600 mg daily for 4 months (10 mg/kg, maximum 600 mg) is an acceptable alternative because rifampin is considered safe in pregnancy and she takes no interacting drugs.

forbidden.why: Once-weekly isoniazid-rifapentine (3HP) is not recommended in pregnancy or for women who may become pregnant during treatment; its safety in pregnancy has not been established (CDC/NTCA 2020).
Active TB has been excluded (asymptomatic, normal chest radiograph); a multidrug active-TB regimen is not indicated, and pyrazinamide is avoided in pregnancy in the United States.
Fluoroquinolone-based LTBI therapy is reserved for contacts of multidrug-resistant TB; the source isolate is fully susceptible, and fluoroquinolones are generally avoided in pregnancy.

extras.why: Pyridoxine 25-50 mg daily is recommended with isoniazid in pregnancy and breastfeeding.
Rifampin added to isoniazid for 3 months (3HR) is an accepted LTBI regimen.
Reporting the treatment plan to the TB control program, as the health department requested.

tasks.title: Antidepressant Intolerance: Updated Medication Plan
tasks.subject: Sexual side effects on antidepressant
tasks.request: Stopped sertraline because of sexual side effects; depressive symptoms returning. Please review and send a new prescription.

required.why: Recurrent depression (PHQ-9 13) after stopping sertraline for SSRI-induced anorgasmia and loss of libido. Bupropion, the usual choice for SSRI sexual dysfunction, is contraindicated with a current or prior diagnosis of bulimia or anorexia nervosa (seizure risk; boxed label contraindication). Mirtazapine (7.5-15 mg at bedtime), vortioxetine (5-10 mg daily) or vilazodone (10 mg daily) have low rates of sexual dysfunction (APA 2010; CANMAT 2016).

forbidden.why: History of bulimia nervosa: bupropion is contraindicated (increased seizure risk), even when the eating disorder is in remission.

extras.why: Psychotherapy or psychiatry referral alongside medication.

tasks.title: Osteoporosis Treatment Initiation
tasks.subject: Osteoporosis: treatment initiation
tasks.request: New osteoporosis on DXA (lumbar spine T-score -2.9) without fractures. Please assess and start treatment.

required.why: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (spine T-score -2.9) warrants treatment (Endocrine Society 2019/2020; AACE 2020). Oral bisphosphonates are contraindicated with esophageal abnormalities that delay emptying, such as achalasia (label), so a parenteral agent is indicated: zoledronic acid 5 mg IV yearly (CrCl about 60), denosumab 60 mg every 6 months, or IV ibandronate 3 mg every 3 months; an anabolic agent is also acceptable. Calcium and vitamin D are replete; no dental procedures planned.

forbidden.why: Achalasia with delayed esophageal emptying (barium column 6 cm at 5 minutes): oral bisphosphonates are contraindicated (esophagitis, ulceration, stricture).

extras.why: Continuation of calcium and vitamin D supplementation.
Fall-prevention or physical therapy referral (one fall in the past year).

tasks.title: Iron Chelation in Lower-Risk MDS
tasks.subject: MRI liver iron quantification finalized
tasks.request: Liver iron concentration 14.2 mg Fe/g dry weight in a transfusion-dependent MDS patient. Please advise on iron chelation and place the order.

required.why: Lower-risk MDS, about 58 units transfused, ferritin 2960 and liver iron 14.2 mg/g with life expectancy over 2 years: chelation is indicated (NCCN MDS 2024). Deferasirox (Exjade/Jadenu), the oral option he prefers, is contraindicated with platelet counts below 50 x10^3/uL (label: GI hemorrhage); his platelets are 38-46. Deferiprone carries agranulocytosis risk and is not recommended in MDS. Subcutaneous deferoxamine 20-40 mg/kg over 8-12 hours, 5-7 nights a week, is the appropriate chelator.

forbidden.why: Deferasirox is contraindicated with platelet counts below 50 x10^3/uL (risk of fatal GI hemorrhage); platelets are 38 x10^3/uL.
Deferiprone causes agranulocytosis and is not recommended in a marrow failure disorder such as MDS.

extras.why: Baseline audiometry before deferoxamine (ototoxicity).
Baseline ophthalmologic examination before deferoxamine (retinal toxicity).
Low-dose vitamin C after a month of deferoxamine augments iron excretion (no cardiac iron).

tasks.title: Pulsatile Tinnitus Evaluation and Diagnostic Workup
tasks.subject: Right pulsatile tinnitus
tasks.request: One week of right-sided whooshing tinnitus in time with his pulse. He also has a red right eye treated as conjunctivitis and keeps asking for steroid eye drops. Please evaluate and order the indicated workup.
facts: Head trauma with sphenoid fracture on 2024-05-08
Raised intraocular pressure on the right
Normal renal function and no contrast allergy

required.why: Pulse-synchronous tinnitus beginning about 2.5 weeks after head trauma with a sphenoid fracture, together with chemosis, corkscrew episcleral vessels, proptosis (Hertel 20 vs 17 mm), abducens limitation, an orbital bruit and raised intraocular pressure (30 vs 15 mmHg) is a traumatic direct carotid-cavernous fistula until proven otherwise. Urgent CT angiography of the head including the orbits (dilated superior ophthalmic vein, enlarged cavernous sinus, early venous filling) is the appropriate first study; catheter angiography is the reference standard and MR angiography of the head is an alternative. Renal function is normal and there is no contrast allergy.

A direct high-flow carotid-cavernous fistula rarely closes spontaneously and threatens vision (raised intraocular pressure, proptosis, cranial nerve palsy); urgent referral for catheter angiography and endovascular occlusion is standard.

forbidden.why: The red eye is venous congestion from a carotid-cavernous fistula, not inflammation. Corticosteroid drops raise intraocular pressure further (already 30 mmHg) and delay the diagnosis; systemic corticosteroids are not indicated.

extras.why: Urgent ophthalmology or neuro-ophthalmology review for raised intraocular pressure, proptosis and diplopia.
Audiometry is part of a standard pulsatile tinnitus workup.
Additional orbital or brain imaging and pre-procedure coagulation tests are reasonable.
Aqueous suppressants for raised intraocular pressure and ocular lubrication are reasonable temporizing measures.

tasks.title: Peripheral Neuropathy and Gait Disorder Evaluation
tasks.subject: Progressive foot numbness and imbalance
tasks.request: Five months of foot numbness and unsteady gait in a patient with prior gastric bypass; B12 normal on injections. Please advise on the diagnostic evaluation.

required.why: Sensory ataxia with posterior column signs, brisk reflexes and extensor plantars (myeloneuropathy) plus anemia and neutropenia after gastric bypass, with normal B12 and methylmalonic acid: copper deficiency myeloneuropathy, worsened by 2.5 years of self-prescribed zinc 100 mg/day, which blocks copper absorption. Serum copper (with ceruloplasmin) is the decisive test (ASMBS 2019 micronutrient guideline; Kumar, Mayo Clin Proc 2006).

forbidden.why: Excess zinc induces copper deficiency by upregulating enterocyte metallothionein; continuing or prescribing zinc would worsen the myeloneuropathy.

extras.why: Serum zinc level to document excess.
Spinal MRI for dorsal column signal and to exclude compression.
Electrodiagnostic testing for the neuropathy component.
Other post-bariatric nutrient deficiencies causing neuropathy.
Empiric copper replacement after the copper level is drawn.
Paraprotein screen in neuropathy.

tasks.title: Tick-Borne Infection: Results Review and Management
tasks.subject: Abnormal ECG
tasks.request: Abnormal ECG on 2024-06-01 in a patient being treated for a tick-borne illness. Please review the result and update the plan.
facts: PR interval 340 ms with Mobitz I

required.why: Lyme carditis with PR prolongation to 340 ms (300 ms or more) and Mobitz I block with presyncope on oral doxycycline: hospitalize with continuous ECG monitoring and give IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily until the PR is below 300 ms, then complete 14-21 days orally (IDSA/AAN/ACR 2020 Lyme guideline). Babesia and Anaplasma PCR are negative, so no co-infection therapy is needed.
PR 300 ms or more or second-degree block requires hospital admission with continuous ECG monitoring because block can progress to complete heart block (IDSA 2020).

forbidden.why: Lyme AV block usually resolves with antibiotics; a permanent pacemaker is not indicated (temporary pacing only if needed).

extras.why: Echocardiogram or troponin to assess myocarditis.
Serial ECGs.
Lyme serology for documentation.
Temporary pacing if high-grade block develops.

tasks.title: Oligomenorrhea Evaluation
tasks.subject: Oligomenorrhea, possible PCOS
tasks.request: Eight months of irregular periods with weight gain and fatigue. Labs and pelvic ultrasound are back. Please evaluate for PCOS and start treatment as indicated.

required.why: Overt primary hypothyroidism (TSH 46.2, free T4 0.5, TPO antibodies 610: Hashimoto thyroiditis) explains the oligomenorrhea and the mild hyperprolactinemia (TRH stimulates prolactin) with galactorrhea; androgens, FSH and ovarian morphology do not support PCOS. Treat with levothyroxine (full replacement about 1.6 mcg/kg, about 100 mcg, is appropriate in a young woman without heart disease; a lower start is acceptable) (ATA 2014; Endocrine Society hyperprolactinemia guideline 2011).
Recheck TSH and free T4 6-8 weeks after starting levothyroxine (with prolactin) to titrate the dose.

forbidden.why: Prolactin 52 ng/mL is secondary to primary hypothyroidism; it normalizes with levothyroxine, so a dopamine agonist is not indicated (Endocrine Society 2011).

extras.why: Repeat prolactin once euthyroid.
Lipid profile in overt hypothyroidism.

tasks.title: Knee Osteoarthritis: Updated Treatment Plan
tasks.subject: Orthopedics: knee osteoarthritis
tasks.request: Bilateral knee OA, not ready for arthroplasty. Orthopedics recommends optimizing non-surgical management. Please update the treatment plan and place the orders.
facts: NSAID reactions to ibuprofen and naproxen
Patient asks about an OTC arthritis gel

required.why: Knee OA (KL grade 3) with persistent pain despite acetaminophen, exercise and weight loss. She has aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (positive aspirin challenge, reactions to ibuprofen and naproxen): all NSAIDs, including topical diclofenac (label contraindication in patients with aspirin-sensitive asthma), are excluded. ACR/AF 2019 options that remain: intra-articular corticosteroid injection (strong) or duloxetine (conditional), started at 30 mg daily.

forbidden.why: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease: oral and topical NSAIDs and aspirin can trigger severe bronchospasm; topical diclofenac labeling contraindicates use in patients with asthma, urticaria or allergic reactions after aspirin or other NSAIDs.

extras.why: Continuing acetaminophen.
Topical capsaicin (ACR conditional for knee OA).
Exercise, bracing or weight-management programs.
Combining duloxetine with an intra-articular injection.

tasks.title: Sexual Dysfunction: Results Review and Treatment
tasks.subject: Sexual health follow-up: results review
tasks.request: Follow-up on sexual health concerns; hormone results are back. Please review and start treatment.

required.why: Lifelong premature ejaculation without erectile dysfunction (IIEF-5 23, normal testosterone). First-line drug options are daily SSRIs, on-demand clomipramine or topical anesthetics (AUA 2020 disorders of ejaculation guideline; ISSM). He takes phenelzine, an MAOI: SSRIs, clomipramine, tramadol and other serotonergic drugs are contraindicated (serotonin syndrome; 14-day washout required) and his depression is in remission on it. Topical lidocaine-prilocaine cream or lidocaine spray before intercourse is the appropriate first-line treatment.

forbidden.why: Phenelzine (MAOI) with an SSRI, clomipramine, tramadol or other serotonergic drug risks fatal serotonin syndrome; contraindicated.

extras.why: Behavioral or psychosexual therapy, pelvic floor therapy or urology referral.

tasks.title: Persistent Diarrhea: Stool Results and Management
tasks.subject: Stool culture final
tasks.request: Stool culture finalized for a patient with bloody diarrhea after a foodborne illness. Please review and update the treatment plan.

required.why: Campylobacter jejuni enteritis with persistent bloody diarrhea and fever on day 11 after failure of ciprofloxacin, with documented ciprofloxacin and tetracycline resistance and erythromycin susceptibility: treat with azithromycin 500 mg daily for 3 days (or 1 g once); erythromycin is an alternative (IDSA 2017 infectious diarrhea guideline).

forbidden.why: The isolate is ciprofloxacin resistant (fluoroquinolone class resistance) and ciprofloxacin has already failed.
The isolate is tetracycline resistant.
Antimotility agents should be avoided with fever and bloody diarrhea (inflammatory enteritis) (IDSA 2017).

extras.why: Oral rehydration solution.
Antipyretic.

tasks.title: COVID-19 in an Immunocompromised Patient: Antiviral Treatment
tasks.subject: COVID-19 in a patient with lupus on immunosuppression
tasks.request: Home antigen test positive 2024-06-02 in a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus on azathioprine and prednisone; symptoms began 2024-06-02, no hypoxemia. She is requesting a specific oral antiviral. Please advise and place the treatment order.
facts: Immunosuppressed: azathioprine and prednisone for lupus

required.why: Mild COVID-19, day 2 of symptoms, not hypoxemic, at high risk of progression: pregnancy plus immunosuppression for lupus (azathioprine, prednisone, lymphocytes 0.8) and no booster since 2022. Antiviral treatment is indicated. She is about 24 weeks pregnant: molnupiravir is not recommended in pregnancy (FDA EUA not authorized; mutagenicity and fetal toxicity in animal studies). Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir 300/100 mg twice daily for 5 days (normal creatinine) is the preferred option in pregnancy (NIH, ACOG/SMFM); her medicines have no significant ritonavir interaction (azathioprine, hydroxychloroquine, low-dose aspirin none; prednisone a minor increase without dose change). A 3-day course of remdesivir (200 mg IV day 1, 100 mg days 2-3) is the accepted alternative.

forbidden.why: Molnupiravir is not recommended during pregnancy (not authorized under the FDA EUA; embryofetal toxicity in animal studies); nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and remdesivir are available and appropriate.
Not hypoxemic (oxygen saturation 98%): COVID-directed dexamethasone is not recommended; her maintenance prednisone continues.
No benefit for COVID-19 in trials; not recommended.

extras.why: Confirmatory SARS-CoV-2 PCR.
Notifying obstetrics or arranging fetal assessment.
Antipyretic for fever in pregnancy.

tasks.title: Asbestos Exposure: Risk Assessment and Testing
tasks.subject: Asbestos exposure: what testing is needed?
tasks.request: Patient with past shipyard asbestos work asks what testing he needs after a former co-worker was diagnosed with mesothelioma.
facts: Shipyard asbestos exposure with pleural plaques

required.why: Age 64-74, former smoker of 1.5 packs per day for 14 years (21 pack-years) who quit in January 2011 (13 years ago): eligible for annual low-dose CT lung cancer screening (USPSTF 2021: age 50-80, 20 pack-years or more, quit within 15 years). Asbestos exposure multiplies the smoking-related lung cancer risk. There is no validated screening test for mesothelioma.

forbidden.why: Serum biomarkers for mesothelioma screening are not recommended in asymptomatic exposed persons (ERS/ESTS/EACTS/ESTRO 2020 mesothelioma guideline; ATS).

extras.why: Baseline pulmonary function testing in asbestos-exposed workers (ATS 2004).
Shared decision-making visit for lung cancer screening.

tasks.title: Chronic Urticaria: Specialist Evaluation
tasks.subject: Chronic hives not controlled
tasks.request: Near-daily hives for 5 months despite updosed cetirizine; recurred after prednisone. Please evaluate and advise on the next treatment step.

required.why: Wheals lasting 2-4 days (confirmed unchanged at 48 hours), burning rather than itch, residual purpura and bruise-like hyperpigmentation, arthralgia, raised ESR/CRP and low C3 and C4: features of hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis, not chronic spontaneous urticaria. A punch biopsy of a lesion with direct immunofluorescence is required for diagnosis (EAACI/GA2LEN/EuroGuiDerm/APAAACI 2022 urticaria guideline; AAAAI/ACAAI 2014 practice parameter).

forbidden.why: Omalizumab is the next step for antihistamine-refractory chronic spontaneous urticaria, but these lesions have urticarial vasculitis features; starting a CSU biologic before biopsy misdirects treatment.

extras.why: C1q and anti-C1q antibodies in hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis.
Screen for systemic lupus erythematosus.
Secondary causes of urticarial vasculitis.
Renal involvement screening.
Dermatology for biopsy or rheumatology for systemic evaluation.

tasks.title: Fatty Liver with Elevated Ferritin: Hepatology Evaluation
tasks.subject: Fatty liver with high ferritin
tasks.request: Patient with fatty liver on ultrasound, ALT 84 U/L and ferritin 1,060 ng/mL that has risen since November. Please evaluate and place the appropriate orders.
facts: Blisters and erosions on sun-exposed dorsal hands with skin fragility
Urgent care proposed oral prednisone for a presumed autoimmune blistering disease

required.why: Blisters and erosions on the sun-exposed dorsal hands with skin fragility, milia, atrophic scars, facial hypertrichosis and reddish-brown urine are the typical picture of porphyria cutanea tarda, and he has its classic susceptibility factors: alcohol, smoking and hepatic iron (ferritin 1,060 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 65%), with HFE not yet tested. HCV and HIV are negative. The diagnosis is made by a markedly raised plasma total porphyrin level (fluorescence emission peak near 619 nm) or raised urine porphyrins with a uroporphyrin and heptacarboxylporphyrin predominance (American Porphyria Foundation and ACG porphyria guidance; Singal 2019).

forbidden.why: Antimalarials are started only after porphyria cutanea tarda is confirmed and the iron status is defined. At standard daily doses they mobilize hepatic porphyrins and cause an acute hepatitis-like reaction with fever and worsening photosensitivity in PCT; only low-dose regimens (100 mg hydroxychloroquine twice weekly) are used, and phlebotomy is preferred when ferritin is high or HFE status is unknown, because antimalarials work poorly in C282Y homozygotes.

The eruption is confined to sun-exposed dorsal hands with fragility, milia and hypertrichosis and no mucosal or truncal involvement: this is not an autoimmune blistering disease, systemic corticosteroids do not treat porphyria cutanea tarda, and they would worsen his prediabetes and steatosis.

extras.why: HFE genotyping is recommended in every patient with porphyria cutanea tarda and is reasonable now given ferritin 1,060 and transferrin saturation 65%.
Non-invasive fibrosis staging with MASLD, alcohol use and ferritin above 1,000 ng/mL.
Repeating or extending viral serologies (HCV RNA, hepatitis A and B immunity) is reasonable in PCT and MASLD.
Urine porphobilinogen and ALA, often sent with porphyrins to exclude an acute porphyria with skin lesions (variegate porphyria, hereditary coproporphyria).
Expedited dermatology review or skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence is reasonable.
Repeat iron indices before planning iron reduction.

tasks.title: Anemia Management in Pregnancy with Known Thalassemia Trait
tasks.subject: Anemia at 20 weeks, known beta-thalassemia trait
tasks.request: Hb 9.1 g/dL at 20 weeks in a patient with beta-thalassemia trait; MCV now 83. Please advise on the cause, whether IV iron or transfusion is needed, and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: Vitamin B12 deficiency (128 pg/mL) after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with supplements stopped: her thalassemia MCV of about 66 has "normalized" to 83 because of a superimposed macrocytic process (RDW 19.8, dimorphic smear, hypersegmented neutrophils, mild leukopenia and thrombocytopenia), with glossitis and neuropathy. B12 replacement is required now (1,000 mcg IM preferred with neurologic signs; high-dose oral 1,000-2,000 mcg daily or intranasal also accepted).

forbidden.why: Ferritin 64 ng/mL: iron replete; the new anemia is from B12 deficiency on top of thalassemia trait.
Hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, stable, with a treatable cause: transfusion is not indicated.

extras.why: Confirmatory MMA or homocysteine.
Reticulocyte count to monitor response.
Pernicious anemia antibodies.
Other post-bypass micronutrients.
Neurology review of the neuropathy.

tasks.title: VTE Prophylaxis Medication Substitution
tasks.subject: Substitute needed for bemiparin obtained abroad
tasks.request: Patient needs a substitute for bemiparin 3,500 IU daily (prescribed in Turkey after bariatric surgery, not available in the US) for VTE prophylaxis; 3 doses left; she would prefer tablets. Please review and send a prescription.

required.why: Extended prophylaxis after bariatric surgery with BMI about 52 (weight 146 kg): fixed once-daily LMWH doses under-dose severe obesity; ASMBS and ACCP-based practice use enoxaparin 40 mg every 12 hours (60 mg every 12 hours is used by some above BMI 50), or dalteparin 5,000-7,500 units every 12 hours, for the remaining 3 weeks. DOACs are not recommended early after bariatric surgery (uncertain absorption, ISTH 2021).

forbidden.why: Absorption of DOACs early after bariatric surgery is unpredictable; ISTH advises against their use in this period.

extras.why: Anti-Xa level to confirm dosing in severe obesity.
Platelet monitoring.

tasks.title: Atrial Fibrillation in an Older Adult: Stroke Prevention Decision
tasks.subject: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: stroke prevention
tasks.request: Patch monitor shows paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (burden 31%), now on metoprolol. Please advise on stroke prevention given his history and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: CHA2DS2-VASc at least 4 (age 75 or older, hypertension, diabetes) with paroxysmal AF, but prior lobar ICH from probable cerebral amyloid angiopathy (strictly lobar microbleeds, cortical superficial siderosis): a nonreversible contraindication to long-term oral anticoagulation. The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline supports referral for percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion in this setting (2a).

forbidden.why: Probable cerebral amyloid angiopathy with prior lobar ICH, 14 lobar microbleeds and disseminated superficial siderosis: very high risk of recurrent ICH on oral anticoagulation, as documented by neurology.

extras.why: Pre-procedure appendage imaging.
12-lead ECG.
Thyroid function in new atrial fibrillation.
Neurology input on peri-procedural antiplatelet therapy.

tasks.title: Thyroid Medication Management and Follow-up Planning
tasks.subject: Thyroid replacement after desiccated thyroid stopped
tasks.request: New atrial fibrillation with suppressed TSH and high free T3 on Armour Thyroid 120 mg, which we stopped today. Please choose and order her thyroid replacement and follow-up.
facts: Suppressed TSH 0.02 with high free T3 6.4

required.why: Iatrogenic T3 excess on desiccated thyroid (TSH 0.02, free T3 6.4, normal free T4) with new atrial fibrillation in a 60 kg woman aged 62-72. Standard therapy is levothyroxine monotherapy (ATA 2014); she was euthyroid on 88 mcg. With AF, restart at or below her prior dose (50-100 mcg daily; about 1.3-1.6 mcg/kg is the upper bound), not a grain-for-grain conversion of 2 grains (about 150-200 mcg).
Recheck TSH (and free T4) in 6-8 weeks.

forbidden.why: T3-containing preparations caused the T3 excess and atrial fibrillation.
A grain-for-grain conversion (about 150-200 mcg) would continue over-replacement in a patient with new AF.

extras.why: Free thyroid hormone levels with the TSH.

tasks.title: Elevated Liver Enzymes in Pregnancy: Hepatology Review
tasks.subject: Elevated alkaline phosphatase in pregnancy
tasks.request: ALP 336 U/L (H) at 34 weeks, up from 78 in the first trimester. Please advise on liver workup and place any orders you recommend.

forbidden.why: Isolated ALP rise with a normal GGT, normal transaminases and bilirubin, normal bile acids and a predominantly placental (heat-stable) isoenzyme fraction is physiologic in the third trimester; cross-sectional imaging, ERCP or biopsy is not indicated.
No intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy: no pruritus and bile acids 4.6 micromol/L.

extras.why: Repeat ALP postpartum.

tasks.title: Abnormal Liver Imaging and Gallbladder Polyp Evaluation
tasks.subject: Abdominal ultrasound finalized; contraceptive refill request
tasks.request: Abdominal ultrasound report finalized on 5/24 and is ready for review. The patient has also requested a refill of her oral contraceptive.
facts: Refill request for the combined pill

required.why: A 4.8 cm solid, vascular, indeterminate liver lesion in a non-cirrhotic woman after 12 years of combined oral contraceptives: hepatocellular adenoma versus focal nodular hyperplasia must be characterized with contrast MRI (preferably with a hepatobiliary agent) or multiphase CT (ACG 2014 focal liver lesion guideline; contrast-enhanced ultrasound also accepted).

forbidden.why: Estrogen-containing contraception should be stopped while a solid liver lesion that may be a hepatocellular adenoma is evaluated (ACG 2014); estrogen promotes adenoma growth and bleeding.
Biopsy is not the first step: contrast imaging characterizes most lesions, and biopsy of a possible adenoma carries bleeding risk.

extras.why: Non-estrogen contraception (progestin-only pill, intrauterine device, implant).
AFP is reasonable for a solid liver lesion.
Pregnancy test before changing contraception.
Gynecology referral for contraception.

tasks.title: Chronic Cough Evaluation and Stepwise Management Plan
tasks.subject: Chest radiograph for persistent cough
tasks.request: Chest radiograph for 9 weeks of cough is finalized and ready for review. The patient has asked for a stronger antibiotic.
facts: Right upper lobe opacities with possible cavitation

required.why: Nine weeks of productive cough with hemoptysis, night sweats, weight loss and low-grade fever in a man from Vietnam (high TB incidence), no response to azithromycin, and right upper lobe nodular opacities with possible cavitation: pulmonary tuberculosis until proven otherwise. Three sputum specimens for AFB smear and mycobacterial culture with NAAT (ATS/CDC/IDSA 2017 diagnosis guideline).

forbidden.why: Fluoroquinolones partially treat tuberculosis, delaying diagnosis, reducing culture yield and selecting fluoroquinolone resistance.

extras.why: HIV testing in suspected tuberculosis.
IGRA (supportive only).
Chest CT.
Baseline tests before possible treatment.
Public health or specialist referral.

tasks.title: Incidental Pulmonary Findings Evaluation
tasks.subject: Incidental lung cysts on abdominal CT
tasks.request: Incidental cystic changes at the lung bases on an abdominal CT done for flank pain (5/10). Please evaluate and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: The cysts were seen only at the lung bases on abdominal CT; a dedicated (high-resolution) chest CT is needed to characterize diffuse cystic lung disease.

Woman with multiple thin-walled lung cysts, prior spontaneous pneumothorax and a renal angiomyolipoma: lymphangioleiomyomatosis. ATS/JRS 2017: serum VEGF-D (800 pg/mL or more is diagnostic with typical cysts) should be measured before considering lung biopsy.

forbidden.why: Lung biopsy is not the first step: typical CT plus angiomyolipoma or VEGF-D at or above 800 pg/mL establishes LAM without tissue (ATS/JRS 2017).

extras.why: Baseline lung function with DLCO.
Exercise oximetry.
Screening for tuberous sclerosis complex.
Angiomyolipoma follow-up.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult
tasks.subject: Patch monitor finalized: pregnant patient with palpitations
tasks.request: Patch monitor shows paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with fast rates in a patient who is 22 weeks pregnant. Echocardiogram is in the chart. Please review and complete the management plan.

required.why: Symptomatic paroxysmal AF with rates up to 162 at 22 weeks, structurally normal heart, no pre-excitation. Beta-1-selective blockers (metoprolol) are first-line rate control in pregnancy (ESC 2018 pregnancy guideline; ACOG); propranolol, bisoprolol and labetalol are accepted. Atenolol is avoided because of fetal growth restriction. CHA2DS2-VASc is 1 (female sex only): no anticoagulation.

forbidden.why: Associated with fetal growth restriction; not recommended in pregnancy.
Fetal thyroid toxicity; reserved for life-threatening arrhythmias.
CHA2DS2-VASc 1 from female sex alone, structurally normal heart: anticoagulation not indicated; DOACs and warfarin are also avoided in pregnancy.

extras.why: Digoxin as an add-on rate-control agent in pregnancy.
Rhythm control with flecainide plus a beta-blocker in a structurally normal heart.
Repeat ECG or rhythm monitoring.
Maternal-fetal medicine coordination.

tasks.title: Urinary Retention Management and Workup Planning
tasks.subject: Acute urinary retention: voiding trial and BPH management
tasks.request: Acute urinary retention on 5/29, Foley placed, started tamsulosin. Please see for a voiding trial and management of the enlarged prostate.

required.why: PSA 31 ng/mL three months before the retention (2.6 in 2021, drawn without catheter or infection) and a hard nodule on rectal exam: prostate cancer must be evaluated. Multiparametric prostate MRI (or prostate biopsy) is the next step (AUA/SUO 2023 early detection guideline). The post-catheter PSA of 58 is unreliable.

forbidden.why: Starting a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor before the cancer evaluation halves the PSA and obscures the diagnosis and staging.

extras.why: Staging if high-risk disease is confirmed (PSA above 20, back pain).
Urine studies or a voiding trial.
Baseline chemistry.

tasks.title: Skin Rash Evaluation and Treatment
tasks.subject: Rash in the groin folds
tasks.request: Same-day visit for a red, itchy rash in the groin folds that did not improve with an antifungal cream. He asks whether he can use his existing prescription ointment there.
facts: Plaques in groin folds and gluteal cleft
Asks to use clobetasol on the groin

required.why: Inverse (intertriginous) psoriasis in a patient with plaque psoriasis: shiny, sharply demarcated, non-scaly plaques in the folds, KOH negative, no response to clotrimazole. AAD-NPF 2021: use low-potency corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors (off label), vitamin D analogues or roflumilast cream on intertriginous skin; super-potent steroids cause atrophy and striae in occluded folds.

forbidden.why: High- and super-potent corticosteroids under occlusion in skin folds cause atrophy, striae and systemic absorption.
Systemic steroids can provoke unstable or pustular psoriasis on withdrawal.

tasks.title: Headache and Facial Pain Classification and Management Plan
tasks.subject: Paroxysmal right facial pain
tasks.request: Brief, shock-like right facial pain attacks for 3 months, not helped by tooth extraction or gabapentin. Please classify and advise on treatment and testing, and place orders.
facts: Brief electric-shock pain in V2 triggered by touch

required.why: Classical trigeminal neuralgia (ICHD-3 13.1.1): paroxysmal 1-2 second electric-shock pains in V2, triggered by innocuous stimuli, normal exam, failed gabapentin and needless dental extraction. First-line therapy is carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine, but in patients of Han Chinese and other Asian ancestry the FDA requires HLA-B*15:02 screening before starting (risk of SJS/TEN).
MRI of the brain with trigeminal nerve sequences to identify neurovascular compression and exclude secondary causes (tumor, multiple sclerosis) (AAN/EFNS, EAN 2019).

forbidden.why: Carbamazepine (and oxcarbazepine/eslicarbazepine) must not be started before HLA-B*15:02 is known in a patient of Han Chinese ancestry (FDA boxed warning).
Opioids are ineffective for trigeminal neuralgia.

extras.why: Baclofen as interim therapy while awaiting HLA results.
Baseline sodium, liver tests and blood count before an anticonvulsant.
Neurosurgery referral if medication fails or for microvascular decompression.

tasks.title: Diabetes Management Reassessment After Dramatic A1C Improvement
tasks.subject: Hemoglobin A1c markedly improved
tasks.request: Hemoglobin A1c 6.4% on 2024-05-28, down from 11.3% in November 2023. Please review the diabetes regimen and follow-up.

required.why: Rapid A1c reduction (11.3% to 6.4% in 6 months) on semaglutide in a patient with known moderate nonproliferative retinopathy, overdue for review, now with new blurred vision: early worsening of diabetic retinopathy (seen with rapid glycemic improvement, including semaglutide in SUSTAIN-6) needs a prompt dilated retinal examination (ADA Standards 2024).

forbidden.why: A1c 6.4% is at goal; further rapid intensification while retinopathy is unassessed is not indicated.
No indication to intensify at A1c 6.4%.

extras.why: A1c in 3 months.
Routine diabetes monitoring.
Continuing semaglutide at the current 1 mg dose.

tasks.title: Travel- and Migration-Related Parasitic Infection Evaluation
tasks.subject: Reactive Chagas screen at blood donation in early pregnancy
tasks.request: Reactive T. cruzi antibody screen at blood donation in a woman from Bolivia who is 11 weeks pregnant. Please evaluate, advise on treatment and place orders.
facts: Childhood in rural Bolivia, adobe house

required.why: A single reactive donor screen does not establish Chagas disease; CDC requires two different serologic assays (for example a second ELISA with a different antigen, or trypomastigote excreted-secreted antigen immunoblot) for diagnosis.
Every patient with suspected or confirmed chronic T. cruzi infection needs a baseline 12-lead ECG to look for cardiomyopathy (conduction disease) (CDC, AHA 2018 Chagas statement).

forbidden.why: Benznidazole and nifurtimox are contraindicated in pregnancy; treatment of chronic infection is deferred until after delivery (and breastfeeding considerations).

extras.why: Echocardiogram if the ECG is abnormal or symptoms develop.
Ambulatory ECG monitoring.
Other screening in an immigrant from an endemic area.
Pediatric or maternal-fetal medicine coordination for congenital transmission testing.

tasks.title: Unilateral Tinnitus with Persistent Middle Ear Effusion
tasks.subject: Audiology results available
tasks.request: Audiology evaluation completed 5/28 for left ear fullness and tinnitus. Report is in the chart.

required.why: A persistent unilateral middle ear effusion in an adult (over 12 weeks, type B tympanogram, conductive loss) without a preceding upper respiratory infection, with blood-streaked nasal mucus and a level II neck node in a man from southern China, requires urgent otolaryngology examination of the nasopharynx (endoscopy, with biopsy if abnormal) to exclude nasopharyngeal carcinoma (AAO-HNS otitis media with effusion guidance).

forbidden.why: Antibiotics do not treat otitis media with effusion and already failed; they delay the nasopharyngeal evaluation.
Systemic steroids are not recommended for otitis media with effusion and may mask a nasopharyngeal lesion.

extras.why: Cross-sectional imaging of the nasopharynx and neck.
EBV DNA or VCA IgA serology.
Neck node ultrasound or aspiration.

tasks.title: Thrombocytopenia Evaluation for an Oncology Patient
tasks.subject: Severe thrombocytopenia on nivolumab
tasks.request: Platelets 13 on adjuvant nivolumab (now held), petechiae without bleeding. Please advise on the cause and management and place orders.
facts: No heparin exposure or new drugs

required.why: Isolated severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 13, grade 4) on nivolumab with a smear confirming true thrombocytopenia (no clumping, no schistocytes, no blasts), normal coagulation, no heparin or new drugs, HIV/HCV negative: immune-related ITP. ASCO 2021 irAE guideline: hold the checkpoint inhibitor and give prednisone 1-2 mg/kg/day (61-122 mg at 61 kg; accepted 60-125 mg) or dexamethasone 40 mg daily, or IV methylprednisolone.

forbidden.why: No active bleeding: prophylactic platelet transfusion is not indicated in immune thrombocytopenia.
As above.
Grade 4 hematologic irAE: immunotherapy must stay on hold.

extras.why: IVIG may be added for grade 4 thrombocytopenia or bleeding.
GI prophylaxis on high-dose glucocorticoids.
Screen for associated hemolysis (Evans syndrome).
Glucose monitoring on high-dose steroids.

tasks.title: Acute Inflammatory Arthritis: Diagnostic Workup
tasks.subject: Urgent: new inflammatory arthritis with fever
tasks.request: New migratory polyarthritis with fever, negative RF and ANA, CRP 64. Please see urgently, recommend testing and treatment, and place orders.

required.why: Fever, migratory polyarthralgia, extensor tenosynovitis and painless pustules after new unprotected sex: arthritis-dermatitis syndrome of disseminated gonococcal infection. NAAT of urogenital, pharyngeal and rectal sites (with blood and joint cultures as acceptable additions) confirms it (CDC STI guidelines 2021).

CDC 2021: disseminated gonococcal infection with arthritis-dermatitis is treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IM or IV every 24 hours (hospitalization recommended), not the 500 mg single dose for uncomplicated infection.

forbidden.why: Immunosuppression for presumed inflammatory arthritis would worsen a disseminated bacterial infection.
A single 500 mg dose treats only uncomplicated gonorrhea, not disseminated infection.

extras.why: Blood cultures.
Joint aspiration if an effusion is present.
Other STI testing.
Doxycycline for chlamydia if not excluded.
Complement testing (recurrent neisserial infection).
Hospital admission for parenteral therapy.

tasks.title: Pruritic Papular Rash Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Same-day visit: itchy rash after a weekend trip
tasks.request: Same-day visit for an itchy rash that started after a weekend away. The patient requests an antibiotic.

forbidden.why: Hot tub (Pseudomonas) folliculitis in a healthy, afebrile host is self-limited within 7-14 days; anti-staphylococcal antibiotics do not cover Pseudomonas and fluoroquinolones are reserved for severe or immunocompromised cases.
Systemic corticosteroids are not indicated for an infectious folliculitis.

extras.why: Oral antihistamine for itch.
Topical antipruritic.
Pustule culture if atypical or persistent.

tasks.title: Medication Treatment for Opioid and Alcohol Use Disorders
tasks.subject: Patient requests treatment for opioid and alcohol use
tasks.request: Patient with opioid and alcohol use disorders wants medication treatment for both and asks for naltrexone. Please review and place the orders.
facts: Daily oxycodone, last use last night
Moderate alcohol use disorder without complicated withdrawal

required.why: Moderate opioid use disorder with daily non-prescribed oxycodone (last use last night): buprenorphine (buprenorphine-naloxone or mono-product) is first-line in primary care (ASAM 2020).

Moderate alcohol use disorder in a patient who wants treatment: pharmacotherapy is recommended (APA 2018). Naltrexone is incompatible with buprenorphine (opioid antagonist; would block it and precipitate withdrawal), so acamprosate (normal kidney function) is first-line; gabapentin or topiramate are accepted alternatives.

forbidden.why: Naltrexone would precipitate opioid withdrawal (daily oxycodone) and blocks buprenorphine; it cannot be combined with opioid agonist treatment.
No alcohol withdrawal requiring treatment (CIWA-Ar 2); benzodiazepines with opioids and alcohol add respiratory depression risk.
Methadone for opioid use disorder is dispensed only by an opioid treatment program.

extras.why: Naloxone rescue kit.
Thiamine or folate supplementation with heavy drinking.
Withdrawal symptom relief.
Infection screening.
Counseling referral.

tasks.role: Infectious Diseases Physician and PrEP Prescriber
tasks.title: Rising Creatinine in a Patient on HIV PrEP
tasks.subject: High creatinine in a patient on PrEP; renewal pending
tasks.request: Creatinine 1.56 mg/dL (H) on 2024-05-24, previously 0.98 mg/dL, in a patient on HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis. His 90-day PrEP renewal is due 2024-06-05, and he also requests an anti-inflammatory for training injuries. Please review and act.
facts: Gain in lean mass; weight 94 kg

required.why: Creatinine rose from 0.98 to 1.56 mg/dL after he started creatine monohydrate 10 g daily, a high-protein diet and intensive training with a 13 kg gain in lean mass; creatine is converted to creatinine and muscle mass raises creatinine production, so creatinine overstates any loss of function. There is no sign of tenofovir toxicity (no proteinuria or glycosuria, albumin-to-creatinine ratio 9 mg/g, phosphate 3.5, normal blood pressure, no NSAIDs). KDIGO 2024 recommends cystatin C (eGFRcys or eGFRcr-cys) when creatinine is unreliable because of muscle mass or creatine supplements.

Ongoing HIV exposure risk. Even taking creatinine 1.56 at face value, Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is about 90-95 mL/min at 94 kg and age 27-32 ((140 - age) x 94 / (72 x 1.56)), and about 74 mL/min with ideal body weight: well above the 60 mL/min threshold for F/TDF (CDC 2021). HIV antigen/antibody was nonreactive on 2024-05-24, so the 90-day renewal of emtricitabine/tenofovir DF should go ahead without a gap; F/TAF is an acceptable alternative.

forbidden.why: Regular systemic NSAIDs add nephrotoxicity to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (label: acute kidney injury reported with high-dose or multiple NSAIDs) while kidney function is being clarified; acetaminophen and physical therapy are preferred.
No proteinuria, hematuria or other evidence of kidney disease; an invasive biopsy is not indicated for an explained creatinine rise.

extras.why: HIV testing with the PrEP renewal (CDC recommends a test within the previous 3 months; it was done 2024-05-24).
Quantified urine protein or albumin.
Non-nephrotoxic analgesia for tendinopathy.
Physical therapy for tendinopathy.

tasks.title: Post-GI Bleed Follow-Up Assessment
tasks.subject: Restart anticoagulation after GI bleed?
tasks.request: Post-discharge follow-up after a diverticular bleed (5/18-5/21). Anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation has been held. Please decide on anticoagulation and update the medication plan.

required.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 4 with a diverticular bleed that stopped spontaneously 16 days ago, no other source, stable hemoglobin: resuming anticoagulation reduces thromboembolism and death (ACG-CAG 2022 periendoscopic guideline suggests resumption; 2023 ACC/AHA AF guideline). Apixaban dose reduction requires 2 of age 80 or more, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 1.5 or more; he meets none (age 72-78, 81 kg, creatinine 1.1), so 5 mg twice daily; off-label under-dosing increases stroke risk. Other full-dose DOACs accepted (CrCl about 65-70 mL/min).

forbidden.why: He meets no apixaban dose-reduction criterion; 2.5 mg twice daily is off-label under-dosing.
Antiplatelet therapy is not an effective substitute and still causes bleeding.
NSAIDs increase diverticular rebleeding.

extras.why: CBC after resumption.
Iron studies.
Oral iron.
Dietary fiber for diverticular disease.

tasks.title: Abnormal Liver Enzymes Workup and Fibrosis Assessment
tasks.subject: Persistently elevated ALT in a young adult
tasks.request: Persistently elevated ALT in a 21-year-old with a low ceruloplasmin; viral, autoimmune and iron studies negative. Please advise on further workup and place the orders.

required.why: Young adult with transaminase elevation, ceruloplasmin 8 mg/dL, low alkaline phosphatase, mild anemia and thrombocytopenia, splenomegaly, new tremor and school decline, and a brother who died of unexplained acute liver failure: Wilson disease. AASLD 2022 guidance: confirm with 24-hour urinary copper (and/or ATP7B genetic testing or hepatic copper).
Slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings (likely with neurologic symptoms) is part of the diagnostic score.

forbidden.why: Lifelong copper-lowering therapy is started after the diagnosis is confirmed; penicillamine can worsen neurologic Wilson disease and choice of agent depends on the confirmed presentation.

extras.why: Serum copper or exchangeable copper.
Liver biopsy with copper quantification if non-invasive tests are inconclusive.
Brain MRI or neurology referral for tremor.
Hemolysis screen for anemia.
Fibrosis assessment.

tasks.title: Septic Olecranon Bursitis in an Immunocompromised Patient: Culture Follow-up
tasks.subject: Urgent care follow-up: right elbow bursitis on oral antibiotics
tasks.request: Patient on long-term prednisone seen in urgent care on 2024-05-29 for septic right olecranon bursitis and discharged on cephalexin. Culture results were phoned to your clinic. He is feeling better and would like to continue treatment at home. Please review at today's visit and place orders.
facts: Blood cultures positive in 2 of 2 sets
No implanted devices or valve disease
Patient wants to continue oral pills at home

required.why: Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (MSSA in 2 of 2 blood culture sets) from septic olecranon bursitis in a patient on prednisone with diabetes. Every S. aureus bacteremia needs intravenous therapy; for MSSA an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam (cefazolin 2 g every 8 hours, or nafcillin/oxacillin) is the treatment of choice (IDSA 2011 MRSA guideline principles; 2019 JAMA/ESCMID SAB management consensus; Holland et al. JAMA 2014). Oral cephalexin is inadequate even though he is improving. No dose constraint: the decision is the IV beta-lactam.

Echocardiography is recommended in every patient with S. aureus bacteremia to detect endocarditis, which changes duration and management (2023 ESC endocarditis guideline class I; 2015 AHA infective endocarditis statement). Transthoracic first; transesophageal accepted.

Follow-up blood cultures 2-4 days after the first positive set and until negative are a core quality indicator in S. aureus bacteremia: clearance defines uncomplicated versus complicated bacteremia and so the duration (IDSA 2011; Liu et al.). His only cultures predate antibiotics; clearance on oral cephalexin is undocumented.

forbidden.why: An oral (or bacteriostatic) regimen as the treatment of S. aureus bacteremia at this stage is inadequate: continuing or substituting oral agents risks relapse, endocarditis and metastatic infection. Any early oral step-down comes only after IV therapy, documented clearance and exclusion of complications.

extras.why: Source control of the still fluctuant bursa.
Imaging of the elbow for residual collection or osteomyelitis.
Admission and vascular access for intravenous therapy.
Glycemic and inflammatory monitoring; repeat bursal culture.
Continuing chronic prednisone (not to be stopped abruptly), inpatient insulin for hyperglycemia, analgesia.

tasks.title: Dermatology Consultation: Recurrent Rash
tasks.subject: Recurrent erythema multiforme
tasks.request: Recurrent erythema multiforme, 5 episodes in a year, treated with prednisone bursts each time. Please advise on management to prevent further episodes and place any orders.
facts: Each episode follows a cold sore

required.why: Recurrent HSV-associated erythema multiforme (each episode 7-10 days after an HSV-1 cold sore), 5 episodes a year; episodic antiviral did not prevent it and prednisone bursts have not reduced recurrences. Continuous antiviral suppression for at least 6 months is first-line (acyclovir 400 mg twice daily, valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily or 1 g daily, famciclovir 250 mg twice daily); normal renal function.

forbidden.why: Repeated steroid bursts do not prevent HSV-associated erythema multiforme and may increase recurrence frequency.

extras.why: Symptomatic lip care.

tasks.title: Positive QuantiFERON Evaluation and Treatment
tasks.subject: Positive QuantiFERON on employment screening
tasks.request: Positive QuantiFERON on employment screening; chest X-ray clear and no symptoms. Please advise on treatment and place the orders.

required.why: Latent TB infection (positive QFT, no symptoms, clear radiograph) in a man from a high-incidence country: treatment is indicated. Alcohol-associated liver disease with advanced fibrosis (11.8 kPa) and persistently raised transaminases makes isoniazid-containing regimens (6-9H, 3HP, 3HR) higher risk; 4 months of daily rifampin has lower hepatotoxicity (CDC 2020, ATS/IDSA/CDC). Dose 10 mg/kg = 650 mg, capped at 600 mg daily. No interacting drugs.

forbidden.why: Isoniazid hepatotoxicity risk is higher with chronic liver disease and active transaminase elevation; rifampin alone is preferred.
No active tuberculosis; pyrazinamide is also hepatotoxic.

extras.why: Baseline and monthly liver tests.
Viral hepatitis serologies.
Hepatology coordination.

tasks.title: Depression Medication Management After an Adverse Reaction
tasks.subject: Reaction to new antidepressant
tasks.request: Patient started on sertraline 5 weeks ago; the on-call physician stopped it last night because of a reaction. She is seen today; please review and update the treatment plan.

required.why: Five weeks after starting sertraline: 6 days of decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, increased goal-directed activity and spending, without psychosis or suicidality: antidepressant-emergent hypomania, with a first-degree relative with bipolar I disorder. This suggests bipolar spectrum disorder; urgent psychiatric evaluation is needed for diagnosis and mood-stabilizing treatment.

forbidden.why: Another antidepressant (SSRI, SNRI, bupropion, mirtazapine, TCA) as monotherapy risks worsening the hypomania and destabilizing a probable bipolar disorder.

extras.why: An antimanic agent pending psychiatry is reasonable.
Short-term benzodiazepine for sleep in hypomania.
Thyroid function.
Urine drug screen.
Pregnancy test before mood stabilizers.

tasks.title: Osteoporosis Evaluation and Metabolic Assessment
tasks.subject: Osteoporosis in a 39-year-old man after a wrist fracture
tasks.request: Low bone density (Z-score -2.9) with a low-trauma wrist fracture in a 39-year-old man. Please evaluate and start osteoporosis treatment.

required.why: Young man with low bone mass, chronic bulky diarrhea, weight loss, iron deficiency anemia and severe vitamin D deficiency: malabsorption from celiac disease is the leading secondary cause; tTG-IgA (with total IgA) is the first test.

25-OH vitamin D 7 ng/mL with low calcium and phosphate, high alkaline phosphatase, secondary hyperparathyroidism, bone pain and proximal weakness: osteomalacia. High-dose vitamin D repletion (for example ergocalciferol 50,000 units weekly, or cholecalciferol daily) with calcium comes first.

forbidden.why: Bisphosphonates or denosumab with untreated osteomalacia (vitamin D 7, calcium 8.2) risk severe hypocalcemia and do not treat the mineralization defect; they are deferred until vitamin D and calcium are replete and the cause is addressed.

extras.why: Calcium supplementation with vitamin D.
Iron replacement.
Total IgA.
Gastroenterology referral for duodenal biopsy.
Urine calcium after repletion.
Magnesium level.

tasks.title: Iron Overload Management After Treatment of MDS
tasks.subject: MRI liver iron quantification finalized
tasks.request: MRI liver iron quantification finalized (liver iron concentration 10.4 mg Fe/g) for a patient followed after transplant for MDS. Please advise on iron removal and place orders.

required.why: Iron overload (ferritin 2,780, transferrin saturation 81%, liver iron 10.4 mg/g, ALT raised) after allogeneic transplant, now transfusion independent with hemoglobin 13.8 and full donor engraftment: therapeutic phlebotomy is the preferred, safest and cheapest method of iron removal (ASTCT/EBMT post-transplant survivorship guidance). Deferasirox is contraindicated with eGFR below 40.

forbidden.why: Contraindicated with eGFR below 40 mL/min/1.73m2 (eGFR 36).
No anemia (hemoglobin 13.8); no ESA indication.

extras.why: Ferritin monitoring every 4-6 phlebotomies.
Hemoglobin before each phlebotomy.
Liver test monitoring.
HFE genotyping.

tasks.title: Pulsatile Tinnitus Evaluation and Workup
tasks.subject: Headache, pulsing ear noise and eyelid droop; requesting migraine medicine
tasks.request: Patient with known migraine seen today for a week of right neck and head pain with a pulse-synchronous noise in the right ear and a droopy right eyelid. Her usual migraine tablet has not helped; she asks for a refill or something stronger. Please review and complete the plan.
facts: Rotational neck manipulation the day before symptoms

required.why: New pulse-synchronous tinnitus with ipsilateral neck pain and retro-orbital headache, and a partial Horner syndrome (ptosis with miosis greater in dim light, sweating preserved), beginning the day after rotational neck manipulation: internal carotid artery dissection until proven otherwise. Same-day CT angiography or MR angiography of the head and neck is required (AHA/ASA scientific statement on cervical artery dissection); the headache differs from her usual migraine.

forbidden.why: Triptans and ergots are vasoconstrictors and are contraindicated in cervical artery dissection and other cerebrovascular disease; this headache is not her migraine.
Further cervical manipulation can extend a dissection.

extras.why: Antithrombotic therapy once dissection is confirmed and hemorrhage excluded, or simple analgesia.
MRI brain for silent infarction, stroke neurology involvement or emergency department transfer for same-day imaging.
Audiometry later in the tinnitus evaluation.

tasks.title: Progressive Sensory Neuropathy: Etiologic Evaluation
tasks.subject: Numb, burning feet and unsteady gait
tasks.request: Ten months of progressive numbness and burning in the feet and fingertips with unsteadiness in the dark. Diabetes screening, B12, thyroid and protein studies are normal. Please evaluate the cause and direct the workup.
facts: Pyridoxine 250 mg twice daily since 2022 (pharmacist reconciliation only)
Total B6 intake about 600 mg/day for over 2 years
Primary care suggested more B vitamins

required.why: Large-fiber sensory neuropathy or ganglionopathy with sensory ataxia; diabetes, B12 (with normal methylmalonic acid), thyroid and paraprotein causes already excluded. The pharmacist reconciliation documents about 600 mg/day of vitamin B6 (pyridoxine 500 mg plus a B-complex 100) for over 2 years, well above the 100 mg/day upper intake level; chronic high intake causes a dose-dependent sensory neuropathy or neuronopathy. Plasma pyridoxal 5'-phosphate confirms the exposure before attributing the neuropathy to it.

forbidden.why: Further pyridoxine or B6-containing supplements would continue the likely toxic exposure; the primary care suggestion of more B vitamins is the trap.

extras.why: Nerve conduction studies and EMG to characterize a sensory axonal neuropathy or neuronopathy.
Symptomatic treatment of neuropathic pain.
Remaining causes of sensory neuronopathy or neuropathy.
Gait and balance therapy for sensory ataxia.
Spine imaging to exclude dorsal column disease in sensory ataxia.

tasks.title: Tick-Borne Infection Assessment and Treatment
tasks.subject: Expanding rash after tick bite
tasks.request: Expanding red patch at the site of a tick bite from 9 days ago, with fatigue and headache, in a patient taking isotretinoin for acne. Seen today; please complete the assessment and treatment plan.
facts: Expanding lesion 9 x 7 cm with central clearing
Tick attached about two days in an endemic area

required.why: A 9 cm expanding erythematous lesion with central clearing at the site of a deer-tick bite in an endemic area, 6-8 days after a 2-day attachment, is erythema migrans: early localized Lyme disease is a clinical diagnosis and serology is not needed. Doxycycline is the usual first choice, but tetracyclines must be avoided with isotretinoin (both cause intracranial hypertension; labeled warning against concomitant use), and the acne course is mid-way. IDSA/AAN/ACR 2020 first-line alternatives: amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily or cefuroxime axetil 500 mg twice daily for 14 days. No penicillin allergy.

forbidden.why: Concomitant tetracyclines and isotretinoin should be avoided (labeled warning): both cause idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri), and equally effective beta-lactams exist for erythema migrans.

extras.why: Baseline serology or coinfection screening; not needed for erythema migrans but harmless.

tasks.title: Oligomenorrhea and Hyperandrogenism: Results Review and Plan
tasks.subject: High testosterone result; patient requesting treatment
tasks.request: Total testosterone 214 ng/dL (H; reference 8-60) collected 2024-05-21 for a patient with irregular menses and excess hair growth. The patient has called asking to start treatment.
facts: Patient request for oral contraceptives and spironolactone

required.why: Rapidly progressive hyperandrogenism with virilization (voice deepening, clitoromegaly, temporal balding) and total testosterone 214 ng/dL (above the 150-200 ng/dL threshold) requires exclusion of an androgen-secreting ovarian or adrenal tumor (Endocrine Society hirsutism guideline). DHEA-S points to an adrenal source.

Transvaginal (pelvic) ultrasound is the first study for an androgen-secreting ovarian tumor (Sertoli-Leydig or steroid cell tumor), the commonest source with this testosterone level and normal-range LH; pelvic MRI is an alternative.

forbidden.why: Virilization with testosterone above 200 ng/dL is not PCOS until a tumor is excluded; starting oral contraceptives or antiandrogens now suppresses testosterone and symptoms, masks progression and delays diagnosis of a possibly malignant tumor.

extras.why: Adrenal CT or MRI, often ordered together with pelvic imaging when testosterone exceeds 200 ng/dL.
Non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, androgen precursors and Cushing screening.
Endocrinology referral for the workup.

tasks.title: Knee Osteoarthritis Pain Management in a Patient Who Cannot Take Oral NSAIDs
tasks.subject: Knee pain before surgery - can I get a cortisone shot?
tasks.request: My right knee is getting worse while I wait for my knee replacement. The Tylenol is not enough. Can I come in for a cortisone shot in the knee like the one I had a few years ago?
facts: Patient requests a knee steroid injection

required.why: Knee OA pain uncontrolled on acetaminophen 3 g/day. Oral NSAIDs including celecoxib are excluded (prior bleeding ulcer with a visible vessel; GI advised permanent avoidance; CKD 3a). Intra-articular corticosteroid within 3 months before total knee arthroplasty is associated with higher periprosthetic joint infection risk (AAHKS/AAOS guidance: avoid within 3 months), and his arthroplasty is in 5 weeks. Guideline options that remain (ACR/Arthritis Foundation 2019): topical diclofenac (strongly recommended for knee OA; minimal systemic exposure, acceptable at eGFR 54) or duloxetine.

forbidden.why: Intra-articular corticosteroid within 3 months of total knee arthroplasty increases periprosthetic joint infection risk; surgery is in 5 weeks.
Same as above: no knee injection within 3 months of arthroplasty.
Prior bleeding gastric ulcer on naproxen with GI advice to avoid oral NSAIDs permanently; CKD 3a.

extras.why: Topical capsaicin as an adjunct.
Prehabilitation and walking aids.

tasks.title: Erectile Dysfunction Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Erectile dysfunction: results review and treatment
tasks.request: Follow-up to review hormone results and start treatment for erectile dysfunction. Patient would like a prescription.

required.why: Organic-pattern erectile dysfunction, eugonadal, no nitrates, good exercise tolerance: a PDE5 inhibitor is first line. Ritonavir is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (sildenafil exposure rises about 11-fold) and the HIV regimen cannot be changed. Label limits with ritonavir: sildenafil 25 mg, no more than once in 48 hours; tadalafil 5 mg as needed, no more than once in 72 hours (2.5 mg for once-daily use); vardenafil 2.5 mg, no more than once in 72 hours; avanafil not recommended.

forbidden.why: With ritonavir, sildenafil must not exceed 25 mg in 48 hours (hypotension, syncope, priapism, visual disturbance).
With ritonavir, tadalafil as needed must not exceed 5 mg in 72 hours.
With ritonavir, vardenafil must not exceed 2.5 mg in 72 hours.
Avanafil is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ritonavir.
Morning testosterone 486 ng/dL is normal; testosterone therapy is not indicated.

tasks.title: Chronic Diarrhea Evaluation
tasks.subject: Chronic watery diarrhea, infectious studies negative
tasks.request: Ten weeks of watery diarrhea including nocturnal stools, 3 kg weight loss. Stool infectious studies and celiac serology negative. Please evaluate and treat.
facts: Negative celiac serology with normal IgA

required.why: Chronic watery diarrhea with nocturnal stools in a woman over 60 taking a PPI, sertraline and an NSAID, with negative infectious studies, normal TSH and negative celiac serology: microscopic colitis is the leading diagnosis and is diagnosed only by histology. Colonoscopy with random biopsies from the right and left colon is required (AGA 2016); the 2016 colonoscopy took no biopsies.

forbidden.why: Starting budesonide or another glucocorticoid before colonoscopic biopsies can blunt the histologic findings and commits her to treatment without a diagnosis; the diagnosis must be made first.
Comprehensive stool infectious testing is negative; empiric antimicrobials are not indicated.

extras.why: Symptomatic antidiarrheal therapy while awaiting colonoscopy.
Bowel preparation, or an H2 blocker in place of the PPI (a microscopic colitis risk drug).
Bile acid diarrhea or pancreatic insufficiency testing if biopsies are normal.

tasks.title: COVID-19 Treatment in an Immunocompromised Patient
tasks.subject: SARS-CoV-2 PCR positive in an immunosuppressed patient
tasks.request: SARS-CoV-2 PCR positive, collected 2024-06-03; symptom onset 2024-06-01. Patient on azathioprine and prednisone for autoimmune hepatitis. Please advise on treatment.

required.why: Mild COVID-19, day 3 of symptoms, not hypoxemic, at high risk of progression (azathioprine plus prednisone, decompensated cirrhosis): antiviral treatment is indicated. Decompensated cirrhosis, Child-Pugh class C (bilirubin 3.6 = 3, albumin 2.5 = 3, INR 2.0 = 2, ascites controlled on diuretics = 2, encephalopathy on lactulose = 2; total 12): the nirmatrelvir/ritonavir label states it is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), as no data exist. Remdesivir needs no hepatic dose adjustment (ALT 64, under 2x the upper limit, well below the stop threshold; normal kidney function): 200 mg IV on day 1, then 100 mg on days 2-3 within 7 days of onset. Molnupiravir 800 mg twice daily for 5 days (no hepatic adjustment; she is 44-64 and not pregnant) is the accepted alternative if infusion is not feasible.

forbidden.why: Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C) per the label; no pharmacokinetic or safety data, and ritonavir is itself hepatically metabolized and hepatotoxic.
Not hypoxemic (oxygen saturation 96%): COVID-directed dexamethasone is not recommended; her maintenance prednisone continues.
No benefit for COVID-19 in trials; not recommended.

extras.why: Baseline hepatic tests and prothrombin time before remdesivir; infusion scheduling.
Acetaminophen up to 2 g/day is the preferred antipyretic in cirrhosis.
Informing hepatology or the transplant team.

tasks.title: Asbestos Exposure Assessment and Testing Request
tasks.subject: Asbestos in my ceiling - need a CT scan?
tasks.request: We scraped our bedroom ceiling a few weeks ago and the test came back positive for asbestos. I breathed in a lot of dust. Can I get a CT scan of my lungs and a blood test for asbestos? I am really scared about mesothelioma.
facts: Request for CT and blood test

forbidden.why: A single 6-hour household chrysotile exposure 3 weeks ago in an asymptomatic patient: asbestos-related pleural and lung disease appear only after a latency of 15-40 years and are dose-related; a CT now cannot detect any effect of this exposure, adds radiation and invites incidental findings.
No validated blood test detects asbestos exposure or early mesothelioma in asymptomatic people; PET has no role.

extras.why: Baseline spirometry is harmless if the patient remains anxious, though not required.

tasks.title: Refractory Chronic Urticaria: Allergy Evaluation
tasks.subject: Refractory chronic urticaria: biologic candidate?
tasks.request: Recurrent swelling of the lips, eyelids and hands every 1-2 weeks despite fourfold-dose cetirizine and a prednisone course; working diagnosis chronic spontaneous urticaria. Is she a candidate for anti-IgE injection therapy? Please evaluate and place orders.
facts: Mother with lifelong recurrent swelling (older note)
Grandfather died of throat swelling (older note)
Abdominal attack with jejunal wall edema
No response to fourfold cetirizine or prednisone

required.why: Recurrent non-itchy swelling lasting 2-4 days without wheals, a bowel-wall edema attack (jejunal wall thickening with free fluid, resolved in 3 days), no response to fourfold antihistamine, corticosteroid or epinephrine, worse on an estrogen-containing contraceptive, no ACE inhibitor, and a family history (mother with lifelong swelling; grandfather died of throat swelling): suspected hereditary angioedema, a bradykinin-mediated disease, not chronic spontaneous urticaria.
