Screening is C4 with C1-inhibitor level and function (WAO/EAACI 2021 HAE guideline; EAACI/GA2LEN 2022 urticaria guideline on angioedema without wheals).
C1-inhibitor antigenic level and function distinguish HAE type I (low level) from type II (normal level, low function); C4 alone can be normal between attacks. Any C1-inhibitor test is accepted here.

forbidden.why: Anti-IgE therapy treats mast-cell-mediated urticaria and is ineffective for bradykinin-mediated angioedema; starting it would delay the diagnosis of a potentially fatal disease.
Corticosteroids do not treat bradykinin-mediated angioedema (already failed) and add toxicity.
Estrogens increase attack frequency and severity in hereditary angioedema; a new estrogen-containing prescription is harmful.

extras.why: C1q to exclude acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency; genetic testing.
Progestin-only or non-hormonal contraception in place of the estrogen-containing pill.
Contraception counseling.
General angioedema and urticaria workup.

tasks.title: Hyperferritinemia in Steatotic Liver Disease
tasks.subject: Elevated ferritin and ALT with fatty liver
tasks.request: Ferritin 940 ng/mL and ALT 66 in a man with fatty liver on ultrasound and obesity. Please evaluate whether the ferritin needs further workup and advise on management.

required.why: Fasting transferrin saturation = serum iron / TIBC = 198 / 288 = 69%, well above 45%, with ferritin 940 ng/mL: this pattern is not explained by dysmetabolic hyperferritinemia of MASLD, in which transferrin saturation is normal. HFE genotyping (C282Y, H63D) is the next step (EASL 2022, AASLD 2011, ACG 2019).

forbidden.why: Chelation has no role in a non-anemic patient with possible hemochromatosis; phlebotomy is the treatment once the diagnosis is made.

Liver biopsy is not needed to diagnose hemochromatosis when genotyping is available, and with ferritin below 1000 ng/mL, normal platelets and AST, advanced fibrosis is unlikely; non-invasive staging comes first.

extras.why: Non-invasive fibrosis assessment for MASLD and possible iron overload.
Repeat fasting iron studies, MRI liver iron quantification and other chronic liver disease screening.
Metabolic risk assessment in MASLD.

tasks.title: Microcytosis in Pregnancy: Hemoglobinopathy Evaluation
tasks.subject: Hemoglobin electrophoresis result, 9 weeks pregnant
tasks.request: Hemoglobin electrophoresis normal (HbA2 2.4%) in a pregnant patient with microcytosis (MCV 70). Please review and complete the anemia evaluation.
facts: Microcytosis MCV 70 with high RBC count

required.why: Microcytosis (MCV 70, MCH 22, RBC 5.3, Mentzer index 13) with replete iron (ferritin 62) and a normal HbA2 points to alpha-thalassemia trait, which hemoglobin electrophoresis cannot detect. Her partner carries the alpha-zero deletion (--SEA); if she also carries an alpha-zero deletion, the fetus has a 25% risk of hemoglobin Bart's hydrops fetalis. ACOG recommends DNA-based alpha-globin testing in this setting, and at 11 weeks the result is needed promptly so that genetic counseling and chorionic villus sampling remain possible. A genetics or maternal-fetal medicine referral that arranges the testing is acceptable.

forbidden.why: Ferritin 62 ng/mL: she is iron replete; therapeutic oral or intravenous iron for thalassemia-related microcytosis gives no benefit and risks iron loading (her prenatal vitamin is sufficient).
Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL: no indication for transfusion.

extras.why: Supporting hematologic tests.
Prenatal diagnosis planning if she is found to carry an alpha-zero deletion.

tasks.title: VTE Prophylaxis Medication Substitution
tasks.subject: Substitute needed for nadroparin (not available in US)
tasks.request: Pregnant patient (11 weeks) on nadroparin 3800 IU daily started abroad for prior DVT; supply ends 2024-06-08 and nadroparin is not available here. She asks whether she can switch to the oral pill she used before. Please prescribe a substitute.
facts: Prior DVT provoked by estrogen-containing contraception
Patient asks to return to the oral pill

required.why: A single prior DVT provoked by estrogen-containing contraception is a hormonally associated event: ACOG Practice Bulletin 196 and ASH 2018 recommend antepartum prophylactic (or intermediate) LMWH plus 6 weeks postpartum. Nadroparin 3800 IU daily is a prophylactic dose; the US equivalent at 71 kg with normal renal function is enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously daily (intermediate 40 mg twice daily also acceptable) or dalteparin 5000 units daily. Direct oral anticoagulants and warfarin are not used in pregnancy.

forbidden.why: DOACs cross the placenta and lack safety data in pregnancy; warfarin is teratogenic (embryopathy at 6-12 weeks). LMWH is the anticoagulant of choice in pregnancy.
Weight-adjusted treatment dosing (1 mg/kg twice daily) is not indicated for prophylaxis after a remote provoked DVT and increases bleeding risk.
Aspirin is not an adequate substitute for LMWH thromboprophylaxis after prior VTE.

extras.why: Baseline platelet count or anti-Xa level.

tasks.title: Atrial Fibrillation Anticoagulation Review: Unstable INR Control
tasks.subject: Unstable INR on warfarin for atrial fibrillation
tasks.request: Warfarin for atrial fibrillation with poor INR control over the past year despite verified adherence; INR 4.1 last month, then 1.6 and 1.5 today. Warfarin held this morning pending your decision. Please decide the anticoagulation plan and enter the order.
facts: Time in therapeutic range 44% over 12 months
Adherence verified, diet and drug factors addressed
No mitral stenosis, no prosthetic valve
Primary care suggests a lower dose because of age

required.why: Nonvalvular AF (no mechanical valve, no mitral stenosis on echo) with CHA2DS2-VASc at least 3 (age, hypertension, diabetes) and time in therapeutic range 44% on warfarin despite verified adherence, consistent diet and no interacting drugs: switching to a DOAC is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, class 1 for low TTR; 2018 CHEST TTR below 65%). Apixaban dose reduction needs 2 of age 80 or more, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or more; he meets none (age 74-78, 78 kg, creatinine 1.0), so 5 mg twice daily. Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about 67-72 mL/min ((140-age) x 78 / 72): rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (CrCl above 50), edoxaban 60 mg daily (CrCl 50-95) and dabigatran 150 mg twice daily (US label) also meet their full-dose criteria. INR 1.5 today is below 2.0, so the DOAC can start now.

forbidden.why: A new warfarin order or dose adjustment continues a strategy that has failed (TTR 44% despite verified adherence and addressed diet and drug factors); a DOAC is indicated.
Antiplatelet therapy adds bleeding risk without stroke benefit in AF on an anticoagulant and has no other indication here.

He meets no dose-reduction criterion (age under 80, 78 kg, creatinine 1.0, CrCl about 67-72 mL/min); off-label under-dosing raises stroke risk without a proven bleeding benefit. Age alone and the earlier warfarin INR of 4.1 are not reasons to reduce the dose.

extras.why: INR before the first DOAC dose to confirm it is below 2.0.
DOAC education and transition by the anticoagulation service.

tasks.title: Thyroid Medication Management and Follow-up Planning
tasks.subject: Rising TSH on levothyroxine - dose increase?
tasks.request: TSH 9.6 (H) with free T4 1.0 on levothyroxine 50 mcg for Hashimoto hypothyroidism; fatigue and weight loss. Should the levothyroxine dose be increased? Please manage.
facts: Weight loss and salt craving (not hypothyroid features)

required.why: Weight loss (not gain), salt craving, orthostatic hypotension, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and gums, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and fasting hypoglycemia in a woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis: primary adrenal insufficiency (autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 2) until proven otherwise. A morning cortisol with simultaneous ACTH (and a cosyntropin test if needed) is required now (Endocrine Society 2016). Untreated adrenal insufficiency itself raises TSH, which often normalizes with glucocorticoid replacement.

forbidden.why: Increasing thyroid hormone before glucocorticoid replacement accelerates cortisol clearance and can precipitate adrenal crisis; the TSH rise may resolve once adrenal insufficiency is treated.

extras.why: Glucocorticoid (and mineralocorticoid) replacement after the cortisol and ACTH samples are drawn, given the symptoms and electrolytes.
Mineralocorticoid axis, adrenal autoantibodies, electrolyte monitoring, other autoimmune screening, or emergency evaluation for orthostatic hypotension.
Repeat thyroid tests after glucocorticoid replacement.

tasks.title: Markedly Abnormal Liver Tests in the Third Trimester: Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Critical liver tests in obstetric triage
tasks.request: ALT 1,486 U/L (critical), AST 1,920 U/L (critical), WBC 2.4 and platelets 104 in a febrile patient at 32 weeks' gestation in obstetric triage. Please review.
facts: Labial sores 10 days ago (buried in nursing note)
No pruritus and normal bile acids (not cholestasis of pregnancy)
Normal blood pressure and no proteinuria (not HELLP or preeclampsia)
Viral hepatitis A, B, C negative

required.why: Fever, anicteric hepatitis with aminotransferases rising above 1,000 U/L (ALT 612 then 1,486; bilirubin 0.9), leukopenia (WBC 2.4) and thrombocytopenia in the third trimester, with labial sores 10 days ago, is herpes simplex hepatitis until proven otherwise. Untreated it progresses to fulminant liver failure with high maternal and fetal mortality, so intravenous acyclovir is started empirically without waiting for the PCR (ACOG and CDC guidance on disseminated HSV in pregnancy; AASLD acute liver failure guidance). Dose 10 mg/kg every 8 hours: 10 x 78 kg = 780 mg (550 mg by ideal body weight 55 kg); creatinine 0.62, no renal adjustment. Accepted range 500-1,200 mg every 8 hours.
HSV-1/2 DNA PCR of blood (plasma or whole blood) confirms disseminated HSV infection with high sensitivity; serology is often negative in primary infection and the labial lesions have crusted.

forbidden.why: This is not intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy: there is no pruritus, bile acids are 7 umol/L (normal) and aminotransferases above 1,000 with fever and leukopenia point to acute viral hepatitis. Treating it as cholestasis with ursodiol delays the antiviral therapy that determines survival.

extras.why: Serial coagulation, glucose, lactate and ammonia to detect progression to acute liver failure; blood cultures for fever.
Repeat liver or obstetric ultrasound.
Admission and hepatology, infectious disease, neonatology or transplant involvement.
Other viral causes of acute hepatitis, HSV type-specific serology or a lesion swab.
Fetal surveillance during maternal febrile illness.
Antenatal corticosteroids at 32 weeks are reasonable if delivery within 7 days becomes likely.

tasks.title: Abnormal Liver Imaging: Evaluation of an Enlarging Liver Cyst
tasks.subject: Liver cyst: request to order procedure
tasks.request: Outside surgeon requests that you place the order for ultrasound-guided percutaneous aspiration and alcohol sclerotherapy of the patient's enlarging liver cyst, with pre-procedure labs. Please review and place the appropriate orders.
facts: Raised on a sheep farm with herding dogs in Kyrgyzstan (endemic area)
Enlarging since 2021 (5.1 to 7.6 cm); 2021 'simple cyst' reading outdated
Outside surgeon did not see the new ultrasound

required.why: A man raised on a sheep farm with herding dogs in Kyrgyzstan (hyperendemic for cystic echinococcosis) with an enlarging 7.6 cm hepatic cyst that has a thick double-line wall and a honeycomb of internal daughter cysts has cystic echinococcosis (WHO-IWGE stage CE2) until proven otherwise; mild eosinophilia supports it. The 2021 'simple cyst' reading is outdated. Echinococcus serology (IgG ELISA or indirect hemagglutination, with immunoblot confirmation) supports the diagnosis before treatment planning (WHO-IWGE 2010 expert consensus; Brunetti 2010).

forbidden.why: Puncturing a hydatid cyst without the PAIR protocol and albendazole cover risks anaphylaxis and spillage with secondary peritoneal echinococcosis; alcohol sclerotherapy risks sclerosing cholangitis if the cyst communicates with the bile ducts. A multivesicular CE2 cyst with daughter cysts is in any case unsuitable for PAIR (WHO-IWGE) and is managed by surgery with perioperative albendazole. Laparoscopic deroofing for a presumed simple cyst carries the same spillage risk.

extras.why: CT or MRI (with MRCP) to characterize the cyst, look for biliary communication and plan surgery.
Specialist or contrast-enhanced ultrasound for WHO-IWGE staging.
Referral to hepatobiliary surgery, infectious diseases or hepatology.
Albendazole 400 mg twice daily (or 10-15 mg/kg/day) is used around surgery or PAIR and as medical therapy; reasonable once the diagnosis is supported.
Chest radiograph for pulmonary cysts and baseline blood tests.

tasks.title: Persistent Cough Evaluation and Management Plan
tasks.subject: Worsening cough in a postpartum patient
tasks.request: Cough for about 2.5 weeks in a patient 5 weeks postpartum who is breastfeeding; urgent care diagnosed viral bronchitis on 2024-05-24. She is exhausted and requests codeine cough syrup. Please review and decide the plan.

required.why: Cough of about 17 days with paroxysms, inspiratory whoop and post-tussive vomiting, afebrile with clear lungs, after a catarrhal prodrome, in an adult who declined Tdap in pregnancy: this meets the CDC clinical case definition of pertussis, not viral bronchitis. She lives with a 5-week-old infant, the group at highest risk of death from pertussis, and is within 3 weeks of cough onset, so treatment is indicated without waiting for testing (CDC). Azithromycin (500 mg day 1, then 250 mg days 2-5) is first-line and compatible with breastfeeding; clarithromycin or erythromycin are alternatives. The infant and partner need post-exposure prophylaxis through their own clinicians (azithromycin is preferred for infants under 1 month and acceptable at 5 weeks).

forbidden.why: Codeine and tramadol are not recommended during breastfeeding (FDA 2017-2018: infant sedation, respiratory depression and death in ultrarapid CYP2D6 metabolizers); opioid antitussives are restricted to adults and avoided in lactation, and they do not shorten pertussis cough.
Beta-lactams do not eradicate Bordetella pertussis and leave the infant exposed; a macrolide is required.

extras.why: Nasopharyngeal Bordetella pertussis PCR (still useful within about 3-4 weeks of onset) to confirm for public health.
Chest radiograph is reasonable to exclude pneumonia, although lungs are clear.
Pertussis is nationally notifiable; reporting supports contact prophylaxis.
Pediatric contact for the infant's prophylaxis and monitoring.
Non-opioid symptomatic measures compatible with breastfeeding (limited efficacy in pertussis).
Tdap is recommended immediately postpartum when it was not given in pregnancy (it does not treat the current infection).

tasks.title: Incidental Pulmonary Findings Evaluation
tasks.subject: Incidental ground-glass lung nodule on CT angiogram
tasks.request: Incidental right upper lobe ground-glass nodule on a CT angiogram done in the ED for chest pain (no pulmonary embolism). Patient is anxious and asking about a PET scan or biopsy. Please advise and arrange follow-up.
facts: Patient asks about PET or biopsy

required.why: A single incidental pure ground-glass nodule of 6 mm or more (9 mm) on thin-section CT: Fleischner Society 2017 recommends a non-contrast chest CT at 6-12 months to confirm persistence, then every 2 years until 5 years. An earlier scan is not recommended because many such lesions are transient; the patient's risk category does not change this recommendation for subsolid nodules.

forbidden.why: PET-CT is not recommended for pure ground-glass nodules: they are typically FDG-avid only minimally, so the test has low sensitivity and frequent false results (Fleischner 2017).
Tissue sampling or resection is not indicated for a new 9 mm pure ground-glass nodule before persistence is established.

extras.why: Optional baseline lung function or a clinic visit to discuss results.

tasks.title: Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult: Episodic Treatment Plan
tasks.subject: Medicine to take at home for AFib episodes?
tasks.request: The ER stopped my last AFib episode with pills in about three hours. My episodes come every few months. Can I have those pills to keep with me so I don't have to go to the ER each time? I'd rather not take a medicine every day.
facts: Safe monitored first dose with AV nodal blocker

required.why: Infrequent, hemodynamically tolerated paroxysmal AF with a structurally normal heart (LVEF 62%, normal wall thickness), no ischemia on stress testing, normal QRS and a monitored first dose that converted safely: an as-needed oral class IC 'pill-in-the-pocket' strategy is reasonable (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline). Single dose by weight: flecainide 300 mg if 70 kg or more (200 mg if under 70 kg) or propafenone 600 mg (450 mg if under 70 kg); he weighs 84 kg.

A class IC agent can organize AF into atrial flutter with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction; a beta-blocker or non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker is taken at least 30 minutes before the dose (as in the monitored ED trial).

forbidden.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 0 in a man: long-term antithrombotic therapy is not indicated, and aspirin is not recommended for stroke prevention in AF.
Infrequent episodes in a patient who prefers no daily therapy: daily antiarrhythmics (and amiodarone's toxicity) are not warranted.

extras.why: ECG or ambulatory monitoring to document episodes.
Discussion of catheter ablation as an alternative.

tasks.title: Urinary Retention Management and Workup Planning
tasks.subject: Urinary retention: urethral catheter could not be passed
tasks.request: Young man with acute urinary retention on 2024-05-29; urethral catheter could not be passed and a suprapubic catheter was placed. Please evaluate the cause and plan definitive management.
facts: Straddle injury with urethral bleeding at age 19
Impassable obstruction 5 cm from the meatus
Years of a thin, split stream

required.why: A young man with years of a thin, split stream after a straddle injury, a small normal prostate, and an impassable obstruction about 5 cm from the meatus with blood at the meatus: a bulbar urethral stricture is the cause of retention, not prostatic enlargement or a neurogenic bladder. Retrograde urethrography (with voiding cystourethrography through the suprapubic tube) and/or urethrocystoscopy defines stricture location and length before definitive treatment (AUA urethral stricture guideline 2023).

forbidden.why: The obstruction is a fixed urethral stricture with a small normal prostate; alpha-blockers, 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors or bethanechol cannot relieve it and would delay definitive diagnosis.
Prostate procedures are not indicated, and a voiding trial before the stricture is defined and treated will fail and risks recurrent retention.

extras.why: Baseline urine studies or referral to a reconstructive urologist for urethroplasty planning.

tasks.title: Skin Rash Evaluation and Treatment
tasks.subject: Rash treatment request
tasks.request: Patient seen 2024-05-30 for light-colored spots on the trunk (skin scraping done in clinic) asks for a prescription in pill form rather than a cream. Please review and prescribe.
facts: KOH: short hyphae and yeast clusters
No liver disease or interacting drugs

required.why: Hypopigmented, finely scaling, coalescing macules on the upper trunk with a KOH preparation showing short hyphae and yeast clusters: pityriasis (tinea) versicolor caused by Malassezia. Topical azoles (ketoconazole 2% shampoo or cream), selenium sulfide or ciclopirox are first line; for extensive disease (about 12% BSA) or when topical treatment is impractical, oral fluconazole (for example 300 mg weekly for 2 weeks) or itraconazole (200 mg daily for 5-7 days) is appropriate. Oral ketoconazole must not be used for skin fungal infections (FDA 2013 safety communication: hepatotoxicity, adrenal insufficiency, drug interactions).

forbidden.why: FDA (2013) limits oral ketoconazole to serious endemic fungal infections when no alternative exists, because of severe hepatotoxicity, adrenal insufficiency and dangerous drug interactions; it must not be used for skin infections such as tinea versicolor.
The rash is a superficial fungal infection; corticosteroids do not treat it and can worsen it.
Oral terbinafine is ineffective for pityriasis versicolor because it does not reach the stratum corneum adequately.

extras.why: A topical agent added to oral therapy, or monthly topical prophylaxis to prevent recurrence.

tasks.title: New Daily Headache: Classification and Workup
tasks.subject: New daily headache since late April, ED follow-up
tasks.request: New daily headache since 2024-04-29 in a woman with joint hypermobility; CT head negative. Please evaluate and direct the workup.
facts: Headache appears upright and resolves lying flat

required.why: Daily headache of abrupt onset after exertion that is absent on waking, appears within minutes of being upright and resolves within minutes of lying flat, with neck stiffness, nausea and muffled hearing, in a patient with hypermobile connective tissue disorder and no prior dural puncture: spontaneous intracranial hypotension (ICHD-3 7.2.3). MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium is the first diagnostic test (pachymeningeal enhancement, brain sagging, venous engorgement, subdural collections); the CT head is insensitive.

forbidden.why: A diagnostic lumbar puncture is not needed (opening pressure is often normal) and creates a further dural hole that can worsen the CSF leak; MRI comes first.
Opioids and butalbital do not treat a CSF leak and carry dependence and medication-overuse risk.

extras.why: Spinal MRI or myelography to localize a leak, or neuroradiology referral for an epidural blood patch.
Caffeine and simple analgesia or antiemetics during conservative management.

tasks.title: Type 2 Diabetes: Glycemic Intensification
tasks.subject: A1c above goal on metformin
tasks.request: Hemoglobin A1c 8.7% (H), collected 2024-05-28, in a patient with type 2 diabetes and prior myocardial infarction on metformin. Please review and adjust therapy.
facts: Family history: brother with RET-positive MEN2A and MTC
Patient declined his own RET testing

required.why: Type 2 diabetes above goal (A1c 8.7%) on metformin with established ASCVD (NSTEMI with stent): ADA 2024 recommends adding a GLP-1 receptor agonist or an SGLT2 inhibitor with proven cardiovascular benefit, independent of A1c. His brother has RET-positive MEN2A with medullary thyroid carcinoma: GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide carry a boxed contraindication for a personal or family history of MTC or MEN2. An SGLT2 inhibitor with cardiovascular benefit (empagliflozin, canagliflozin, or dapagliflozin) is therefore the choice; eGFR 74, no genital infections or ketoacidosis.

forbidden.why: Boxed contraindication: family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN2 (brother with RET mutation); the patient has declined his own RET testing.

extras.why: A1c in 3 months and renal function after SGLT2 inhibitor initiation.
Renewed offer of RET genetic testing or calcitonin screening given the family history.

tasks.title: Returned Traveler with Eosinophilia and Liver Lesions
tasks.subject: Positive parasite serology in a returned traveler
tasks.request: Parasitology serology resulted for a returned traveler from highland Peru with eosinophilia, right upper quadrant pain and hepatic tract-like lesions on CT. Please review and treat.
facts: Andean watercress and alfalfa juice exposure

required.why: Acute (hepatic migratory) fascioliasis: watercress and alfalfa juice exposure in the Andean highlands, eosinophilia 3.1, RUQ pain, fever and urticaria, subcapsular tortuous hepatic tracks on CT, positive Fasciola antibody, and negative stool ova (eggs appear only in the later biliary phase). Triclabendazole is the treatment of choice (FDA approved 2019; WHO, CDC): 10 mg/kg orally for 2 doses 12 hours apart, with food. At 75 kg this is 750 mg per dose (three 250 mg tablets).

forbidden.why: Fasciola hepatica, unlike other trematodes, does not respond to praziquantel, and albendazole and mebendazole are ineffective; using them delays curative treatment.
Corticosteroids do not treat the infection and are not indicated for eosinophilia from a defined helminth infection.

extras.why: Follow-up eosinophil count, liver tests, stool examination for eggs at 2-3 months and repeat imaging.
Symptomatic relief of urticaria or pain.

tasks.title: Tinnitus Evaluation and Imaging Decision
tasks.subject: New bilateral ear ringing and muffled hearing
tasks.request: Older woman with 10 days of ringing in both ears and muffled hearing; audiology screening done the same day. Please review and decide on workup, including whether imaging is needed.

required.why: Bilateral, symmetric high-pitched tinnitus with a symmetric mild flat sensorineural loss beginning after three weeks of self-directed aspirin about 3.9 g/day (67 mg/kg/day at 58 kg) in an older woman, with nausea, a low bicarbonate (21) and an anion gap of 15: chronic salicylate toxicity (salicylism). A serum salicylate level is needed now, because chronic toxicity in older adults can be serious at modest levels; the tinnitus and hearing loss are usually reversible after stopping aspirin.

forbidden.why: Symmetric, bilateral, non-pulsatile tinnitus with symmetric hearing loss and a clear reversible cause does not need imaging (AAO-HNSF tinnitus guideline recommends against imaging unless tinnitus is unilateral, pulsatile, or with focal neurologic or asymmetric hearing loss).
This is not sudden idiopathic sensorineural hearing loss; corticosteroids are not indicated.
Further salicylate (or another oral NSAID) is inappropriate in suspected salicylate toxicity.

extras.why: Acid-base and metabolic assessment, coagulation, repeat audiometry after stopping aspirin, or emergency referral if the level is high.
Safer arthritis analgesia (acetaminophen, topical diclofenac or capsaicin).

tasks.title: Thrombocytopenia Evaluation for an Oncology Patient
tasks.subject: New thrombocytopenia on nivolumab
tasks.request: Platelets 61 (from 184 in February) with anemia and low white count in a patient on nivolumab for gastric cancer. Considering steroids for an immune-related cause. Please evaluate and advise on workup.
facts: Ineffective erythropoiesis: high LDH, low reticulocytes

required.why: Pancytopenia with MCV 116, macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils, low reticulocytes, very high LDH, low haptoglobin and indirect hyperbilirubinemia (ineffective erythropoiesis with intramedullary hemolysis), with normal INR and fibrinogen, three years after total gastrectomy and two years after B12 injections stopped, plus new toe paresthesias: vitamin B12 deficiency (megaloblastic anemia) is the leading cause and mimics both an immune-related adverse event and a microangiopathy. A serum B12 level (with methylmalonic acid) confirms it.

forbidden.why: The findings point to B12 deficiency rather than immune thrombocytopenia; high-dose glucocorticoids, IVIG or thrombopoietin agonists would add harm and could lead to unnecessary discontinuation of effective immunotherapy.
Platelets 61 without bleeding: no indication for transfusion.
Bone marrow examination is premature when a B12 level is likely to explain the findings; megaloblastic marrow can also be mistaken for myelodysplasia or leukemia.

extras.why: Folate and homocysteine, and exclusion of microangiopathy or immune hemolysis.
Parenteral B12 replacement after the level is drawn (lifelong after total gastrectomy); folic acid only with B12.

tasks.title: Inflammatory Polyarthritis: Serologic Evaluation and Plan
tasks.subject: Polyarthritis with strongly positive ANA and pleuritic chest pain
tasks.request: Seven weeks of inflammatory polyarthritis, low-grade fevers and pleuritic chest pain with a small effusion; ANA 1:640 homogeneous, dsDNA negative, complements normal. Please evaluate for lupus and advise on treatment.
facts: High-titer homogeneous ANA with negative dsDNA

required.why: Inflammatory polyarthritis, myalgia, fever and pleuritis with a high-titer homogeneous ANA, negative anti-dsDNA, normal complements and a bland urinalysis, after nearly 3 years of hydralazine 150 mg/day: hydralazine-induced lupus is the leading diagnosis. Anti-histone antibodies (positive in more than 90% of hydralazine-induced lupus) support it; the treatment is withdrawal of hydralazine.

forbidden.why: Drug-induced lupus resolves within weeks to months after the drug is stopped; methotrexate or other immunosuppressants are not indicated, and treating as rheumatoid arthritis or SLE exposes her to unnecessary toxicity.
Re-prescribing hydralazine perpetuates drug-induced lupus and risks hydralazine-associated ANCA vasculitis.

extras.why: ANCA (hydralazine-associated vasculitis), extractable nuclear antigens, anti-chromatin antibodies, renal monitoring and echocardiography for pericardial involvement.
Replacement antihypertensive for resistant hypertension (spironolactone preferred; potassium 4.1), an NSAID for symptoms or a short low-dose prednisone course if serositis is troublesome.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult
tasks.subject: New atrial fibrillation after ED visit
tasks.request: New paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on 5/26, converted in the ED. The ED felt no stroke-prevention therapy was needed at his age. He has epilepsy followed by neurology. Please review and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (septum 22 mm, provocable LVOT gradient 58 mmHg on the 2019 outside echo) with clinical atrial fibrillation: anticoagulation is recommended regardless of CHA2DS2-VASc (2024 AHA/ACC HCM guideline; 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline), so the ED score of 0 does not apply. Carbamazepine is a strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inducer: DOACs are to be avoided (2023 AF guideline drug-interaction table; ISTH 2021 guidance on DOACs with enzyme-inducing anti-seizure medicines). His anti-seizure regimen cannot simply be changed (levetiracetam and lamotrigine failed). Warfarin with INR target 2-3 and close INR monitoring.
Thyroid function is part of the evaluation of every new atrial fibrillation (2023 AF guideline) and has never been checked.

Transthoracic echocardiography is recommended for new atrial fibrillation; the only study is a 2019 outside echo showing obstructive physiology that has never been reassessed (gradient, left atrial size, wall thickness for risk stratification). Cardiac MRI is an accepted alternative in HCM.

forbidden.why: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp induction by carbamazepine lowers DOAC levels and stroke protection; avoid.
Digoxin is potentially harmful in obstructive HCM (2024 AHA/ACC HCM guideline).
Aspirin is not adequate stroke prevention in AF with HCM and adds bleeding risk to anticoagulation.

extras.why: INR monitoring for warfarin initiation.
Beta-blockade is first-line in obstructive HCM and for rate control.
HCM center or electrophysiology referral, genetic counselling and testing, ambulatory monitoring, neurology input.

tasks.title: Headache Classification and Management
tasks.subject: Persistent right-sided headache, not responding to treatment
tasks.request: Five months of side-locked right headache with eye tearing during flares, diagnosed as cluster headache in urgent care; sumatriptan is not helping. Please classify the headache and start treatment; place the orders you recommend.

required.why: Continuous side-locked unilateral headache for over 3 months with ipsilateral autonomic features (lacrimation, conjunctival injection, ptosis, nasal congestion) and restlessness during exacerbations, without circadian attacks or remission: probable hemicrania continua (ICHD-3 3.4), which by definition requires an absolute response to indomethacin. The urgent-care label of cluster headache does not fit (continuous pain, no attack periodicity, no triptan response). Start indomethacin 25 mg three times daily, titrating to 50 mg three times daily if needed (accepted 25-75 mg per dose).

Prior duodenal ulcer hemorrhage (2019 gastroenterology note, buried) makes her high GI risk on a full-dose NSAID; H. pylori was eradicated. A PPI is required with indomethacin (ACG 2009 NSAID ulcer-prevention guideline; ACG 2017 peptic ulcer guideline).

Trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias have secondary mimics (pituitary and posterior fossa lesions, carotid dissection); MRI brain with pituitary views is recommended for every new TAC phenotype, and she has never had head imaging.

forbidden.why: A cluster-type steroid bridge is not indicated for hemicrania continua and, with indomethacin, raises the ulcer bleeding risk after a prior ulcer hemorrhage.
Opioids and butalbital worsen chronic headache (medication overuse) and are not indicated.
A second NSAID with indomethacin adds GI bleeding risk without benefit.

extras.why: Vascular imaging to exclude dissection is reasonable.
Ophthalmology review of the ptosis is reasonable.
Additional gastroprotection is reasonable.

tasks.title: Progressive Sensory Symptoms: Neurology E-Consult
tasks.subject: Progressive numbness and falls in a young man
tasks.request: Progressive numbness in hands and feet with falls; Romberg positive. B12 was normal in April. Could this be Guillain-Barre? Please advise and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: Nitrous oxide inactivates cobalamin (oxidizes it to an inactive form), so serum B12 can be normal in nitrous oxide myeloneuropathy; here the 412 pg/mL value was also drawn 35 hours after a 1000 mcg IM dose (pathology comment) and is uninterpretable. Methylmalonic acid and/or homocysteine are the functional markers that confirm deficiency (draw before further B12 doses if possible).

Myeloneuropathy (sensory ataxia, absent vibration, extensor plantars with absent ankle jerks: subacute combined degeneration pattern) after heavy nitrous oxide use: start parenteral B12 1000 mcg now (for example IM daily for a week, then weekly, then monthly), without waiting for the confirmatory results, and stop nitrous oxide.
Upper motor neuron signs with posterior column loss localize to the spinal cord; MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine shows the dorsal column T2 signal and excludes compressive myelopathy.

forbidden.why: Brisk knee jerks, extensor plantars and posterior column loss with nitrous oxide exposure indicate myelopathy, not Guillain-Barre syndrome; IVIG is not indicated.
Not indicated; this is not Guillain-Barre syndrome.

extras.why: Electrodiagnostic testing and in-person neurology follow-up are reasonable.
Additional deficiency and infectious screening of myelopathy is reasonable.
Folate is reasonable once B12 has been started.
Substance use counselling and physical therapy for gait.

features: a fact in an older note

tasks.title: Incidental Pulmonary Nodule Evaluation
tasks.subject: Incidental 11 mm lung nodule
tasks.request: Incidental 11 mm solid right upper lobe nodule on CT angiography; radiology suggests repeat CT in 3 months. Former heavy smoker. Please review and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: The nodule grew from 5 mm (outside screening CT 2022-11-08) to 11 mm (2024-05-15) over 554 days. Volume doubling time = 554 x ln2 / (3 x ln(11/5)) = 384 / 2.37 = about 160 days, well inside the malignant range (under 400 days). With a 41 pack-year history and lobulated margins this is a high-probability solid nodule over 8 mm: PET-CT for characterization and staging (ACCP 2013 lung nodule guideline; Fleischner 2017 recommends comparison with prior imaging). Waiting 3 months is not appropriate.

A growing high-probability nodule needs tissue diagnosis or resection planning now: thoracic surgery referral, multidisciplinary nodule program, or a direct tissue-sampling procedure (navigational bronchoscopy, EBUS or CT-guided biopsy).

forbidden.why: This nodule needs diagnostic evaluation, not screening; a screening CT in 3-12 months delays the diagnosis of a probable cancer.

extras.why: Preoperative pulmonary function testing.
Brain MRI for staging is reasonable if malignancy is confirmed.

tasks.title: Thromboprophylaxis Review Before Myeloma Therapy
tasks.subject: Verify thromboprophylaxis before cycle 1 lenalidomide
tasks.request: Cycle 1 lenalidomide-dexamethasone starts 2024-06-05. The fellow ordered aspirin 81 mg as thromboprophylaxis. Please confirm the prophylaxis or substitute an appropriate regimen.

required.why: IMWG thromboprophylaxis model for lenalidomide: individual risk factors include previous VTE (provoked popliteal DVT 2019 in the scanned outside record, missed by the fellow) and obesity (BMI = 104 / 1.75^2 = 34.0, over 30); the myeloma itself and the IMiD add disease and treatment risk. Two or more individual/disease risk factors: LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg daily) or full-dose warfarin rather than aspirin (IMWG 2014; NCCN; ASCO 2023 accepts apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily or rivaroxaban 10 mg daily). IMPEDE VTE: IMiD +4, BMI 25 or more +1, prior VTE +5, low-dose dexamethasone +2 = 12 points (high risk). Enoxaparin stays 40 mg (BMI under 40, CrCl about 95 mL/min).

forbidden.why: Aspirin is adequate only with at most one risk factor; with prior VTE and BMI 34 it is insufficient, and adding it to an anticoagulant only increases bleeding.

extras.why: Monitoring blood counts or INR.
Baseline venous duplex is low value but harmless.

features: a fact in an older note

tasks.title: Hyperferritinemia With Steatotic Liver Disease
tasks.subject: Ferritin over 1000 with fatty liver
tasks.request: Fatty liver with ALT 61, ferritin 1120 and high iron saturation; also isolated high bilirubin. Worried about hemochromatosis. Please advise and place the orders you recommend, scheduling any repeat testing for the appropriate date.

required.why: FIB-4 = age x AST / (platelets x sqrt(ALT)) = about 52 x 48 / (182 x 7.81) = 1.76 (1.69-1.82 across ages 50-54), indeterminate (1.3-2.67): a second-line test, vibration-controlled transient elastography or ELF, is indicated (AASLD 2023 MASLD guidance).

Transferrin saturation 188/241 = 78% and ferritin 1120 were measured 14 days after the second ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg infusion (infusion-center note, not on the medication list); IV iron raises ferritin and saturation for weeks, and she was iron deficient (ferritin 6) in February, so these values do not indicate iron overload. Repeat ferritin and transferrin saturation at least 8 weeks after the last infusion (on or after 2024-07-01, day 28 or later) before any hemochromatosis-directed treatment.

forbidden.why: Ferritin and saturation are inflated by recent IV iron after iron deficiency; phlebotomy would cause recurrent iron deficiency anemia.
No iron overload is established.
Premature: non-invasive fibrosis assessment comes first.

extras.why: HFE genotyping is unaffected by IV iron and is low risk, although the pretest probability is low.
Phosphate check after ferric carboxymaltose (hypophosphatemia risk).
Gilbert confirmation and viral hepatitis screening are reasonable.

tasks.title: Dermatology E-Consult: Nonhealing Leg Ulcer
tasks.subject: Enlarging painful shin ulcer despite antibiotics and debridement
tasks.request: Her shin ulcer has more than doubled in size since surgical debridement, despite two antibiotic courses. Surgery is offering repeat debridement and grafting and I am considering another antibiotic. Please advise on the diagnosis and treatment and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Ulcer enlarged from 3.0 x 2.5 cm to 7.5 x 6 cm after debridement (pathergy)
New ulcer at a venipuncture site
Dense neutrophilic infiltrate, stains and cultures negative
Active ulcerative colitis with bloody diarrhea (telephone note)

required.why: Pyoderma gangrenosum: rapidly enlarging, very painful ulcer with a violaceous undermined border; pathergy (3.0 x 2.5 cm before the 2024-05-06 debridement, 7.5 x 6 cm after, and a new ulcer at a venipuncture site); no response to two antibiotic courses; swab grew skin flora only; the final pathology (dense neutrophilic infiltrate, stains and tissue cultures negative) supersedes the preliminary 'consistent with infection'; and active ulcerative colitis. First-line systemic therapy for extensive or rapidly progressive PG is prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day (STOP GAP trial, Ormerod BMJ 2015; Maverakis JAMA Dermatol 2018 diagnostic criteria; BAD guidance). Current weight 68 kg: 0.5 x 68 = 34 mg to 1 x 68 = 68 mg per day; accepted 35-70 mg once daily (e.g. 40-60 mg), methylprednisolone equivalent 28-56 mg. Prednisone also treats the moderate ulcerative colitis flare.

The GI telephone note (2024-04-23) documents an unevaluated ulcerative colitis flare (5 to 7 bloody stools a day, missed mesalamine) that she never followed up; PG activity often parallels IBD activity, and escalation to therapy that treats both (e.g. anti-TNF) belongs with gastroenterology. A flare after two antibiotic courses needs activity assessment and C. difficile exclusion (ACG 2019 ulcerative colitis guideline): gastroenterology referral, fecal calprotectin, C. difficile testing or endoscopy are each accepted.

forbidden.why: Pathergy: the ulcer more than doubled after debridement and a new ulcer formed at a venipuncture site. Debridement or grafting while PG is active extends the ulcer and is avoided until the disease is controlled.

No evidence of infection: two courses failed, the swab grew skin flora only, tissue stains and cultures are negative and she is afebrile. A third empiric course delays treatment of PG and adds C. difficile risk during an ulcerative colitis flare.

extras.why: Super-potent topical corticosteroid or topical tacrolimus to the ulcer border, or intralesional triamcinolone at the border, as adjuncts.
Re-prescribing or optimizing maintenance mesalamine.
Screening before possible anti-TNF therapy.
Non-surgical moist wound care and in-person dermatology follow-up.
Inflammatory markers, iron studies for the anemia, stool pathogens and glucose monitoring on steroids.
Bone and gastric protection on high-dose prednisone, and analgesia.

tasks.title: Atrial Fibrillation Management in an Older Adult
tasks.subject: New persistent atrial fibrillation: rate control and stroke prevention
tasks.request: Older man with persistent atrial fibrillation on a 14-day monitor; ejection fraction reportedly normal. I plan diltiazem for rate control and aspirin 81 mg. Please review and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Immunofixation negative and normal free light-chain ratio (AL excluded)
Persistent AF on monitor with nocturnal slow rates

required.why: Persistent AF (100% burden) in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. AF with cardiac amyloidosis warrants anticoagulation regardless of CHA2DS2-VASc (2023 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway on cardiac amyloidosis; 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline), and his score is at least 4 anyway (age 75 or older 2, hypertension 1, heart failure 1). Aspirin is not effective stroke prevention. Apixaban dose-reduction needs 2 of age 80 or older, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or more: age 76-79, weight 79 kg, creatinine 1.12, so 5 mg twice daily. Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about (140-78) x 79 / (72 x 1.12) = 61 mL/min also supports full-dose rivaroxaban 20 mg daily, edoxaban 60 mg daily or dabigatran 150 mg (110 mg outside the US for age 75 or older) twice daily.

ATTR cardiomyopathy was established noninvasively at the outside clinic (Perugini grade 3 pyrophosphate uptake with no monoclonal protein on serum and urine immunofixation and a normal free light-chain ratio; these supersede the 'possible faint band' on electrophoresis, so AL amyloidosis is excluded and no biopsy is needed), but it has never been treated because he moved. Refer to an amyloidosis or heart failure cardiology program for a TTR stabilizer (tafamidis: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline class 1 for NYHA I-III ATTR-CM), TTR genotyping and the rhythm strategy.

forbidden.why: Non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers bind amyloid fibrils and cause profound hypotension, heart block and heart-failure decompensation in cardiac amyloidosis despite a normal ejection fraction (2023 ACC Expert Consensus); his blood pressure is 104/66 and nocturnal rates fall to 41 bpm.
Antiplatelet therapy is not adequate stroke prevention in AF, and adding it to an anticoagulant raises bleeding risk without a coronary indication.
No dose-reduction criteria are met (age under 80, weight 79 kg, creatinine 1.12, CrCl about 61); underdosing loses stroke protection.

extras.why: TTR gene sequencing is recommended for every patient with ATTR cardiomyopathy (hereditary versus wild-type).
Repeat echocardiogram or ECG, cardiac biomarkers and thyroid function in new AF.
Electrophysiology input on rhythm control and nocturnal conduction disease.
Cautious low-dose digoxin or amiodarone are rate or rhythm options in ATTR cardiomyopathy (2023 ACC Expert Consensus); see clinician questions.
A cardiologist may start the TTR stabilizer directly.

tasks.title: Recurrent Olecranon Bursitis: Preventing Further Episodes
tasks.subject: Recurrent MRSA olecranon bursitis: preventing another episode
tasks.request: Three episodes of left olecranon septic bursitis in 11 months, MRSA each time; the current episode has resolved after drainage and doxycycline. He wants to stop this from happening again and asks for a cortisone injection for the leftover swelling. Please advise and place orders.
facts: April nasal PCR 'not detected' retracted (mislabelled specimen)
Son with recurrent MRSA boils; shared towels and razor

required.why: Recurrent MRSA infection (three episodes in 11 months) with confirmed nasal MRSA carriage (the April 'not detected' PCR was retracted as a mislabelled specimen; the repeat nares swab on 2024-05-08 grew MRSA) and ongoing household transmission (wife and son with MRSA abscesses, shared towels and razor, documented in a January telephone note). IDSA 2011 MRSA guideline: when recurrent SSTI continues despite hygiene measures, or with transmission among household members, decolonize with nasal mupirocin twice daily for 5-10 days plus chlorhexidine body washes. Povidone-iodine nasal antiseptic accepted.
Skin decolonization with chlorhexidine gluconate 4% body wash daily for 5-14 days accompanies nasal mupirocin (IDSA 2011); dilute bleach baths are an accepted alternative.

Three episodes of septic olecranon bursitis with a thickened, fibrotic bursa and persistent swelling: elective bursectomy once infection is quiescent is the definitive treatment for recurrent septic bursitis.

forbidden.why: Intrabursal corticosteroid after three septic episodes in an MRSA carrier risks reinfection, skin atrophy and a chronic draining sinus; corticosteroid injection is avoided in septic and recently septic bursitis.
Same reason: no corticosteroid injection into the bursa.

extras.why: Imaging of the residual bursal swelling before surgery.
Repeat colonization screening after decolonization.
Diabetes monitoring.
Elbow protection and work modification.

tasks.title: Diabetes Reassessment After Marked A1c Improvement
tasks.subject: A1c improved from 9.1 to 6.0: add a GLP-1 agonist?
tasks.request: A1c fell from 9.1% to 6.0% over six months on the same metformin dose, and he has lost 8 kg. I would like to add a weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist to keep the momentum. Please advise and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Diabetes new after a normal A1c in 2021

required.why: Diabetes that began after age 50 (A1c 5.6% in 2021, 8.6% in 2023, no family history) followed six months later by an unexplained fall in A1c from 9.1% to 6.0% on an unchanged metformin dose, with unintentional loss of 8 kg (85 to 77 kg, 9.4%), poor appetite and early satiety, pale greasy floating stools (nurse intake 2024-05-29) and boring epigastric-to-mid-back pain worse lying flat (telephone note 2024-04-18): the A1c is valid (normal hemoglobin, no transfusion or iron) and the pattern of new-onset diabetes followed by weight loss and falling glucose is a red flag for pancreatic adenocarcinoma (ENDPAC model; AGA 2020 clinical practice update on pancreatic cancer risk). A pancreas-protocol multiphasic contrast CT is the first test (NCCN pancreatic adenocarcinoma guideline; ACR Appropriateness Criteria); MRI/MRCP or endoscopic ultrasound are accepted.

forbidden.why: Glycemia is already at target (A1c 6.0%). A GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide would deepen unexplained weight loss and early satiety, confound the evaluation, and is not started while pancreatic disease is suspected.
A1c 6.0% with poor oral intake: a sulfonylurea or insulin adds hypoglycemia risk without indication.

extras.why: Tumor markers as an adjunct to imaging (not diagnostic alone).
Pancreatic enzymes, liver tests (alkaline phosphatase is mildly raised) and fecal elastase for exocrine insufficiency.
Gastroenterology or pancreatic specialist referral alongside imaging.
Basic evaluation of weight loss and a second glycemic marker.
Chest CT for staging may be combined with the abdominal study.

Antimuscarinics worsen retention.

tasks.title: Antidepressant Switch After SSRI Intolerance
tasks.subject: Antidepressant after sertraline intolerance; painful neuropathy
tasks.request: Moderately severe depression (PHQ-9 18); sertraline stopped for nausea, loose stools and insomnia. He also has painful alcohol-related neuropathy. I am considering duloxetine to cover both. Please advise and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Outdated problem-list entry and 2019 liver tests

required.why: Moderately severe recurrent depression (PHQ-9 18) needs a new antidepressant after sertraline intolerance. The hepatology note (2024-04-15) documents decompensated alcohol-associated cirrhosis, Child-Pugh B (score 8: bilirubin 2.6, albumin 2.9, INR 1.6, controlled ascites, no encephalopathy), which supersedes the problem-list entry 'fatty liver, mild' and the normal 2019 liver tests. Hepatic-impairment limits (FDA labeling): escitalopram 10 mg/day maximum (accepted 5-10 mg), citalopram 20 mg/day maximum (accepted 10-20 mg), mirtazapine at a low starting dose because clearance falls by about 30% (accepted 7.5-15 mg); vortioxetine needs no adjustment in Child-Pugh B (accepted 5-10 mg). Sodium 132-133 on diuretics: monitor sodium with an SSRI.

Painful alcohol-related axonal polyneuropathy (7/10, waking him) still needs treatment once duloxetine is excluded, and amitriptyline already caused confusion and constipation (tricyclics also risk precipitating encephalopathy in cirrhosis). Gabapentinoids are renally cleared without hepatic metabolism (start low, for example pregabalin 25-75 mg or gabapentin 100-300 mg at night, watching for sedation); topical lidocaine or capsaicin 8% are alternatives (AAN 2021 painful polyneuropathy guideline; NICE CG173).

forbidden.why: Duloxetine labeling: avoid in chronic liver disease or substantial alcohol use (hepatotoxicity; exposure several-fold higher in hepatic impairment). Child-Pugh B alcohol-associated cirrhosis.
Escitalopram maximum is 10 mg/day in hepatic impairment.
Citalopram maximum is 20 mg/day in hepatic impairment (QT and exposure).
Nefazodone is hepatotoxic; tricyclics caused confusion and constipation in this patient and risk precipitating hepatic encephalopathy.

extras.why: Sodium monitoring on an SSRI with sodium 132-133 on diuretics.
Psychotherapy and relapse-prevention support.
Hepatology medication review, neurology or pain follow-up, foot care.
Baseline ECG before citalopram or escitalopram (QT prolongation is common in cirrhosis).
Nutritional support in alcohol-related neuropathy; acetaminophen up to 2 g/day is acceptable analgesia in cirrhosis.

tasks.title: Neurology Visit: Headache with Pulsatile Tinnitus
tasks.subject: ED follow-up: headache and pulsatile tinnitus, probable IIH
tasks.request: Seen 2024-05-24 with ten days of headache, right pulsatile tinnitus and bilateral optic disc swelling; impression probable idiopathic intracranial hypertension. Please see in neurology clinic. She is booked for 2024-06-03.
facts: Outside CT venogram: right transverse-sigmoid sinus thrombosis
Stale chart weight 68 kg (2022) copied by the ED

required.why: The scanned outside CT venogram final report (issued after ED discharge) shows acute right transverse-sigmoid sinus thrombosis extending to the jugular bulb; the 'probable IIH' label is wrong. AHA 2024 scientific statement on cerebral venous thrombosis and ESO 2017 guideline: start therapeutic anticoagulation with weight-adjusted LMWH (preferred over unfractionated heparin), even with headache and papilledema; no hemorrhage here and platelets 268, INR 1.0, creatinine 0.7. Dosing must use today's measured weight of 86.0 kg (nursing intake), not the 2022 chart weight of 68 kg that the ED copied. Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg every 12 h = 86 mg (accepted 75-100 mg twice daily; edges 12.8% below and 16.3% above 86; the stale-weight dose of 68 mg is outside). Enoxaparin 1.5 mg/kg once daily = 129 mg (accepted 115-150 mg; edges 10.9% below and 16.3% above; stale-weight 102 mg is outside). Dalteparin 200 IU/kg once daily = 17,200 IU (accepted 15,000-19,500 IU; stale-weight 13,600 IU outside). A continuous unfractionated heparin infusion by nomogram is also acceptable.

Papilledema from venous outflow obstruction threatens vision even with normal acuity; formal visual fields and fundus assessment by (neuro-)ophthalmology guide monitoring and the need for intracranial pressure treatment (AHA 2024 statement).

forbidden.why: Estrogen-containing contraception is a provoking factor for cerebral venous thrombosis and is contraindicated after it; the refill request must be declined and the pill stopped.
Prophylactic enoxaparin (30-40 mg) does not treat sinus thrombosis, and doses based on the 2022 chart weight of 68 kg (about 68 mg twice daily or 102 mg once daily) underdose her at 86 kg.
Subcutaneous prophylactic heparin is not treatment for cerebral venous thrombosis.
Antiplatelet therapy is not a treatment for cerebral venous thrombosis and adds bleeding risk on anticoagulation.

extras.why: Many neurologists would admit a newly recognized sinus thrombosis with papilledema to start anticoagulation and monitor.
MRI with MR venography to confirm the extent and look for parenchymal lesions, or repeat venous imaging, is reasonable.
Pregnancy test, coagulation baseline, anti-Xa monitoring and selected thrombophilia testing are reasonable.
Progestin-only or non-hormonal contraception is appropriate in place of the combined pill.
Contraception counselling or IUD placement, and hematology input on anticoagulation duration, are reasonable.
Analgesia for headache.

Annual MRCP surveillance for cholangiocarcinoma and disease progression was due in March 2024 and is overdue; it also stages the bile ducts before cholecystectomy.

extras.why: CA 19-9 with MRCP is commonly used in PSC surveillance.
Annual colonoscopy (also due), elastography and specialist follow-up.
A preoperative ultrasound is low value but harmless.

tasks.title: Skin Rash Evaluation and Treatment
tasks.subject: Rash spreading despite antifungal cream
tasks.request: The ringworm on my back and arms is spreading, especially where I was in the sun, even though I am on the antifungal pills for my toenails and the cream. Can you send something stronger? I also need my toenail pill refilled to finish the 12 weeks.

Anti-Ro/SSA is positive in most cases and supports the diagnosis (with ANA; leukopenia 3.6 is consistent).
Stop the trigger and treat the lesions on the trunk and arms with a medium- to high-potency topical corticosteroid, plus strict photoprotection.

forbidden.why: Terbinafine is the probable trigger of SCLE and must be stopped, not refilled; griseofulvin is photosensitizing and can also exacerbate lupus.

extras.why: ANA, systemic lupus screening, skin biopsy or dermatology referral.
Photoprotection, hydroxychloroquine for persistent disease, or topical nail therapy instead of terbinafine.

tasks.title: Hip and Thigh Pain in an NSAID-Intolerant Older Adult
tasks.subject: Thigh and hip pain, NSAID intolerant; alendronate renewal request
tasks.request: Right hip osteoarthritis with thigh pain for 3 months despite acetaminophen; ibuprofen caused an ulcer bleed and her eGFR is 37. Orthopedics suggested a hip steroid injection, and the mail-order pharmacy is asking to renew her alendronate. Please assess and place the orders you recommend.
facts: Lateral cortical beaking on the radiograph addendum
Medication list says drug holiday since 2019 (superseded)
Thigh rather than groin pain, not reproduced by hip rotation

required.why: Prodromal anterolateral thigh pain (with a milder left-sided ache) after about 12 years of continuous alendronate (dispensing record in the pharmacist note of 2024-05-08; the 'drug holiday since 2019' on the medication list is wrong), plus focal lateral cortical beaking of the subtrochanteric femoral shaft on the radiograph addendum: an incomplete atypical femoral fracture until proven otherwise (ASBMR task force 2014; Endocrine Society 2020 osteoporosis guideline). Image both full-length femurs (contralateral involvement is common); MRI, CT or bone scan if radiographs are equivocal. Hip rotation does not reproduce the pain, so hip osteoarthritis does not explain it.

A painful incomplete atypical femoral fracture with cortical beaking needs orthopedic surgical evaluation for prophylactic intramedullary nailing versus protected weight-bearing (ASBMR task force 2014).

forbidden.why: Suspected atypical femoral fracture after 12 years of alendronate: all bisphosphonates must be stopped (ASBMR). Her Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is about 32-35 mL/min (61 kg, creatinine 1.42, age 72-82), also at or below the alendronate label limit of 35.

The pain arises from the femoral shaft, not the joint (thigh rather than groin; rotation does not reproduce it); a hip injection treats the wrong structure and delays management of an impending fracture.
Same as the hip injection: the joint is not the pain generator.
Prior ibuprofen-associated bleeding gastric ulcer and CKD stage 3b (eGFR 37).

extras.why: Cross-sectional imaging if radiographs are equivocal.
Bone health reassessment.
Protected weight-bearing and gait aids until surgical review.
Vitamin D and calcium repletion.
Safe analgesia; a topical NSAID is acceptable despite the ulcer history and CKD.
Endocrinology or bone health service for the future fracture-prevention plan.

tasks.title: Tinnitus With Hearing Loss: Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Audiogram result: left tinnitus
tasks.request: Audiogram for long-standing left tinnitus (since last fall) shows left sensorineural loss. Please review and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: Asymmetric sensorineural loss (left-right differences 35-40 dB at 1-4 kHz; word recognition 60% versus 100%) with unilateral tinnitus: MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium to exclude vestibular schwannoma (AAO-HNS 2019 sudden hearing loss guideline; AAO-HNS 2014 tinnitus guideline).

The loss is sudden (woke with it on 2024-05-29, nurse telephone note), not part of the chronic tinnitus labelled in 2023 (normal hearing then): idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss within the 14-day treatment window. Corticosteroid therapy should be offered, but systemic steroids caused a psychotic disorder in 2019 (psychiatry discharge summary): intratympanic corticosteroid is the recommended route when systemic steroids are contraindicated (AAO-HNS 2019), so urgent otolaryngology for intratympanic dexamethasone or methylprednisolone.

forbidden.why: Prior corticosteroid-induced psychotic disorder on prednisone 60 mg; intratympanic delivery avoids systemic exposure.

extras.why: Intratympanic dexamethasone or methylprednisolone ordered for the otolaryngologist to inject.
Repeat audiometry to monitor recovery.
Hyperbaric oxygen within 2 weeks is an AAO-HNS option.

tasks.title: Iron Overload Management in Transfusion-Dependent MDS
tasks.subject: Iron chelation start (planned at April visit)
tasks.request: Ferritin 2,810 after 38 units. Dr. Achterberg-Moss planned to start chelation if ferritin stayed above 2,500 and she is away this month. His repeat marrow was done in May. Please place the chelation order with the dose.
facts: CD34 blasts 12% supersede the 4% aspirate count

required.why: The 2024 addendum supersedes the preliminary 4% blast count and the 2022 low-risk diagnosis: CD34 blasts 12% (>10%: 3 points), complex karyotype with 4 abnormalities (very poor: 4), hemoglobin 8.2 (8 to <10: 1), platelets 62 (50 to <100: 0.5), ANC 0.9 (>=0.8: 0). IPSS-R = 8.5, very high risk (>6). Using the superseded data (blasts 4%: 1, normal karyotype: 1) gives 3.5, which would wrongly classify him as lower risk. He is not a transplant candidate (documented). NCCN MDS 2024: higher-risk MDS not eligible for transplant is treated with a hypomethylating agent (azacitidine preferred, AZA-001 survival benefit), decitabine, or a clinical trial; chelation is not indicated. Mosteller BSA = sqrt(172 x 70 / 3600) = sqrt(3.344) = 1.83 m2; azacitidine 75 mg/m2 x 1.83 = 137 mg daily on days 1-7 of a 28-day cycle, subcutaneous or IV (band 120-155 mg; 150 mg vial rounding accepted). Decitabine 20 mg/m2 x 1.83 = 36.6 mg IV daily x 5 days (band 32-42 mg). Oral decitabine-cedazuridine 35/100 mg daily x 5 days is a fixed dose.

forbidden.why: Iron chelation is recommended for lower-risk transfusion-dependent MDS with long expected survival or for transplant candidates; in IPSS-R very-high-risk MDS (median survival under a year) without a transplant plan it adds toxicity without benefit and delays disease-directed therapy (NCCN MDS).

Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (erythropoietin 860 mIU/mL predicts no response), luspatercept and lenalidomide are lower-risk MDS therapies; with 12% blasts and a complex karyotype (del(5q) is not isolated) they are not indicated.

extras.why: Antiemetic premedication for a hypomethylating agent.
Ongoing transfusion support.
Molecular profiling (IPSS-M, TP53), clinical trial evaluation and supportive or palliative care referral are reasonable in very-high-risk MDS.

tasks.title: Inflammatory Arthritis Serologic Workup
tasks.subject: Seronegative polyarthritis: start a DMARD?
tasks.request: Ten weeks of wrist, knee and ankle synovitis, RF and CCP negative, ESR 52. Wrist and ankle films are back. Please see him and start methotrexate or another DMARD if you agree; place the orders you recommend.
facts: Digital clubbing described only in the nursing intake
Symmetric periostitis of the distal long bones

required.why: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy: digital clubbing (documented only in the nursing intake), symmetric periostitis of the distal radius, ulna, tibia and fibula on radiographs, shin pain worse with dependency, large-joint effusions sparing the small finger joints, negative RF and anti-CCP, raised alkaline phosphatase, 7 kg weight loss, in a current smoker with 60 pack-years (older tobacco note). Secondary (pulmonary) hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is a paraneoplastic syndrome of lung cancer in about 80-90% of adult cases, so diagnostic CT of the chest (contrast-enhanced preferred; non-contrast CT or PET-CT accepted) is required before any immunosuppression. A screening low-dose CT is for asymptomatic people and is not accepted.

forbidden.why: This is not rheumatoid arthritis: it is hypertrophic osteoarthropathy, most often due to lung cancer. A DMARD treats the wrong disease, delays the cancer diagnosis and adds immunosuppression.
Biologic and targeted synthetic DMARDs are not indicated and are unsafe while a probable malignancy is unexplained.

extras.why: Smoking cessation pharmacotherapy.
NSAIDs are the symptomatic treatment of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (normal kidney function, no ulcer or bleeding history); gastroprotection with them is reasonable.
Pulmonology referral, a chest radiograph alongside the CT, and tobacco treatment are reasonable.
Additional laboratory tests or bone scintigraphy are low-risk parts of the evaluation.

tasks.title: Travel-Related Parasitic Infection Evaluation
tasks.subject: Neurocysticercosis on MRI: start antiparasitic treatment
tasks.request: First seizure, MRI shows multiple parenchymal neurocysticercosis cysts. Seizure-free on levetiracetam. Please start antiparasitic treatment and place the orders you recommend.

required.why: IDSA/ASTMH 2017 neurocysticercosis guideline: a funduscopic examination before antiparasitic therapy in every patient (strong), because treating intraocular cysticercosis causes inflammation and blindness. He reports 2 weeks of right blurred vision with a moving dark floater (nurse telephone note), so an urgent dilated ophthalmologic examination is mandatory before albendazole.

Antiparasitic therapy for multiple cysts is given with corticosteroids; he is from rural Guatemala, so Strongyloides must be screened (or treated empirically with ivermectin) before steroids to prevent hyperinfection (IDSA 2017).
Serum enzyme-linked immunotransfer blot (EITB) is recommended to support the diagnosis (IDSA 2017).

forbidden.why: Antiparasitic therapy before excluding ocular cysticercosis (symptomatic right eye) risks permanent visual loss; it is started only after the funduscopic examination.
Corticosteroids are started with the antiparasitic course, after Strongyloides screening or empiric ivermectin.

extras.why: Empiric ivermectin before corticosteroids is an accepted alternative to waiting for serology.
TB screening before prolonged steroids, HIV, stool examination for Taenia, neurology follow-up.

tasks.title: Asbestos-Related Lung Disease Management
tasks.subject: Asbestosis: patient requests prednisone
tasks.request: Former insulator with asbestosis, more breathless this year. He felt better after a prednisone burst at urgent care in February and asks for a longer course. His saturation was 95% after walking at urgent care and 95% at rest today. Please advise and place the orders you recommend.
facts: 6-minute walk nadir SpO2 86% with good waveform

required.why: The formal 6-minute walk (good waveform, forehead sensor) shows a nadir SpO2 of 86%, sustained to the end of the walk, correcting to 92% with 2 L/min pulsed oxygen. The urgent-care 95% after walking was flagged as low signal with cold fingers and does not count, and resting saturation (95%, PaO2 71) does not reflect exertion. ATS 2020 home oxygen guideline: adults with interstitial lung disease and severe exertional hypoxemia (SpO2 88% or below) should receive ambulatory oxygen (conditional; improves exercise capacity and dyspnea); he also meets CMS ambulatory oxygen criteria with documented improvement on oxygen. Resting PaO2 71 mmHg does not qualify for continuous oxygen.

The ATS 2023 clinical practice guideline on pulmonary rehabilitation recommends rehabilitation for adults with interstitial lung disease (improves exercise capacity, dyspnea and quality of life; BTS 2013 likewise). He has mMRC grade 2 dyspnea and a 6-minute walk of 312 m.

forbidden.why: Asbestosis is a non-inflammatory fibrosing pneumoconiosis: systemic corticosteroids have no proven benefit and cause harm (ATS 2004 statement on nonmalignant asbestos-related disease; fibrotic ILD data). The February improvement was from acute bronchitis, not the asbestosis.

extras.why: Vaccination is recommended in chronic lung disease.
Pulmonary follow-up and serial lung function to monitor for progression.
Screening for pulmonary hypertension or nocturnal desaturation is reasonable with exertional hypoxemia and a low DLCO.

tasks.title: Buprenorphine Initiation for Chronic Opioid Transition
tasks.subject: Transition from fentanyl and oxycodone to buprenorphine
tasks.request: Chronic back pain on long-term fentanyl and oxycodone (see medication list). He is motivated to switch to buprenorphine. Please start the induction and place the orders you recommend.
facts: PDMP fills of 75 and 25 mcg/h patches
Clinic list at 50 mcg/h is outdated

required.why: Current regimen (pain clinic letter and PDMP; the clinic list showing 50 mcg/h is outdated): fentanyl 100 mcg/h (x 2.4 = 240 MME) plus oxycodone 40 mg/day (x 1.5 = 60 MME) = about 300 MME. A standard induction requires stopping the full agonist and waiting for moderate withdrawal (about 72 hours after removing high-dose fentanyl patches, with a high risk of precipitated withdrawal), and withdrawal causes a catecholamine surge. Four weeks after an NSTEMI with a residual 70% RCA stenosis, cardiology asks to avoid sympathetic surges, and he fears withdrawal. A low-dose (micro) induction overlaps buprenorphine with the unchanged full agonist (SAMHSA/ASAM low-dose initiation guidance; Bernese method): for example buprenorphine 0.5 mg SL once daily day 1, 0.5 mg twice daily day 2, 1 mg twice daily day 3, 2 mg twice daily day 4, 3 mg twice daily day 5, 4 mg twice daily day 6, then 12-16 mg daily on day 7 with removal of the fentanyl patches and stopping oxycodone. Accepted starting doses: sublingual or buccal 0.05-1 mg, or a transdermal buprenorphine patch (5-20 mcg/h) as the bridge.

CDC 2022 opioid prescribing guideline and SAMHSA: offer naloxone to patients on 50 MME or more; he is on about 300 MME with daytime sedation and has none at home. Overlapping opioids during the induction add risk.

forbidden.why: A standard starting dose (2-4 mg or more, or extended-release injectable buprenorphine) requires a withdrawal period off the full agonist and risks precipitated withdrawal with high-dose fentanyl; the resulting sympathetic surge is dangerous four weeks after an NSTEMI with residual coronary stenosis.
An opioid antagonist on top of about 300 MME of full agonists would precipitate severe withdrawal and provides no analgesia.

Re-prescribing fentanyl at the outdated 50 mcg/h on the clinic list halves his actual 100 mcg/h dose (a drop of about 120 MME) during the induction, provoking withdrawal and a sympathetic surge four weeks after an NSTEMI.

extras.why: The full agonists continue unchanged during a low-dose induction and prescribing has been transferred from the pain clinic, so continuation at the current dose (fentanyl 100 mcg/h, oxycodone 10 mg) is reasonable.
Symptomatic adjuncts for mild withdrawal symptoms, pain or constipation during the transition (NSAIDs avoided after the myocardial infarction).
Baseline urine drug testing, ECG and liver tests before buprenorphine are reasonable.
Coordination with cardiology and pain services and non-drug pain treatment are reasonable.

tasks.title: Pruritic Papular Rash Evaluation and Management
tasks.subject: Itchy rash not improving on antifungal cream
tasks.request: Itchy rash on the wrists and shins, no better after 7 weeks of antifungal cream; he asks for the antifungal pills that urgent care mentioned. I saw him today and sent liver tests. Please review the records and complete the plan.
facts: Violaceous polygonal flat-topped papules with Wickham striae
KOH corrected to artifact; culture negative
Past injection drug use with shared needles (2016 note)

required.why: Lichen planus (especially erosive oral disease) is associated with hepatitis C. He injected heroin with shared equipment in 2008-2013 (2016 addiction medicine note), declined testing then, has never been tested and now has ALT 71 and AST 58. HCV antibody with reflex HCV RNA is indicated (CDC 2020 and USPSTF 2020: screen all adults and test anyone with past injection drug use; AAD lichen planus workup).

tasks.subject: Low TSH on levothyroxine

She has no thyroid gland; the low TSH is from levothyroxine.

Thyroglobulin and antibodies at the next surveillance visit are reasonable.

tasks.subject: Itchy rash getting worse
tasks.request: I'm 34 weeks pregnant and the itchy bumps on my belly and legs are getting worse, and my hands and feet itch at night. Urgent care said my blood tests would go to you. Can you prescribe something?

Primigravida (polymorphic eruption is most common in a first pregnancy)

No cholestasis; a bile acid sequestrant also impairs vitamin K absorption late in pregnancy.
No burrows, clear finger webs and no itching contacts make scabies unlikely, and oral ivermectin is avoided in pregnancy.

extras.why: Emollients and soothing topical preparations are reasonable adjuncts.
Continuing a sedating antihistamine at night alongside the main treatment is tolerated.
Repeating bile acids later is reasonable because cholestasis can develop later in the third trimester.

tasks.request: Patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma on carboplatin, pemetrexed and pembrolizumab, started in Germany, now continuing care here. She was given tinzaparin injections there, which are not available in the US, and has a few syringes left. Please review and advise; place any orders needed before cycle 4 on 6/5.
facts: Score abroad used the pneumonia blood count of 2024-03-18
BMI inputs: weight 74 kg, height 165 cm

forbidden.why: Khorana score from the pre-chemotherapy values of 2024-04-08 is 1 (lung 1; platelets 268, leukocytes 8.4, hemoglobin 12.1 and BMI 27.2 score 0). The score of 3 recorded abroad used the blood count of 2024-03-18, taken during postobstructive pneumonia (platelets 486, leukocytes 16.8). ASCO 2023: routine thromboprophylaxis is not offered to ambulatory cancer patients below a Khorana score of 2; continuing an anticoagulant adds bleeding risk without indication, and there is no VTE (the suspected DVT was excluded).
Aspirin is not a recommended thromboprophylaxis for solid-tumor outpatients (ASCO 2023; it is used only in myeloma on immunomodulatory drugs).

extras.why: Informing oncology of the decision is reasonable.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult
tasks.subject: Ambulatory ECG monitor report: atrial fibrillation
tasks.request: The 14-day ambulatory ECG monitor final report for your patient shows paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (burden 4%). Please review and place orders.
facts: Neurology: migraine with aura, not a TIA
Known migraine with typical march of sensory aura
No hypertension, diabetes, heart failure or vascular disease

required.why: New paroxysmal AF (burden 4%) in a 38-46-year-old man: a transthoracic echocardiogram is recommended for all patients with newly diagnosed AF to assess cardiac structure, left atrial size and ventricular function, and to guide rhythm-control options (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS). None has been done: the May admission was observation only and neurology excluded a TIA, so no stroke work-up echocardiogram was performed. TSH (1.6) is already normal.

forbidden.why: CHA2DS2-VASc 0 (man under 65, no hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, vascular disease, stroke or TIA): annual stroke risk below 1%, so oral anticoagulation is not recommended. The emergency department "suspected TIA" was superseded by normal diffusion-weighted MRI and the neurology diagnosis of migraine with aura.
CHA2DS2-VASc 0: antiplatelet therapy for stroke prevention in AF is not recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS, class 3: no benefit) and adds bleeding risk.

extras.why: Referral to discuss rhythm control or ablation in a young symptomatic patient is reasonable.
A beta-blocker or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blocker for symptomatic rate control is reasonable.
Screening for sleep apnea as an AF risk factor is reasonable.
Repeat thyroid or lipid testing is harmless.

tasks.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in a Young Adult
tasks.subject: Ambulatory ECG monitor report: atrial fibrillation
tasks.request: The 14-day ambulatory ECG monitor final report for your patient shows paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (burden 4%). Please review and place orders.
facts: Diffusion-weighted MRI: 9 mm acute embolic infarct
Stroke service diagnosis: embolic stroke of undetermined source
No dose-reduction criteria: weight 86 kg, creatinine 0.94

required.why: Paroxysmal AF found on the monitor arranged after an embolic stroke of undetermined source: diffusion-weighted MRI showed a 9 mm acute embolic-pattern cortical infarct on 2024-05-10, so the event is a stroke, not a migraine aura. CHA2DS2-VASc = stroke 2 (no hypertension, diabetes, heart failure or vascular disease; age under 65; male) = 2: oral anticoagulation is recommended for secondary prevention, and a DOAC is preferred over warfarin (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS, AHA/ASA 2021). The infarct is small and 3 weeks old, so starting now is appropriate. Dose: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (no reduction criteria: age under 80, weight 86 kg, creatinine 0.94); Cockcroft-Gault CrCl = (140 - age) x 86 / (72 x 0.94) = 119-126 mL/min for ages 38-46, so rivaroxaban 20 mg daily or dabigatran 150 mg twice daily are full-dose alternatives. Edoxaban is not used because CrCl above 95 mL/min reduces its efficacy (FDA boxed warning). The echocardiogram was already done during the stroke admission.

forbidden.why: No dose-reduction criterion applies (age under 80, weight 86 kg, creatinine 0.94, CrCl about 120 mL/min); a reduced dose leaves a patient with a recent embolic stroke under-protected.
Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about 119-126 mL/min: edoxaban should not be used in nonvalvular AF with CrCl above 95 mL/min (FDA boxed warning, higher ischemic stroke rate).

Once anticoagulated for AF, adding or continuing aspirin without a separate vascular indication (no coronary or carotid disease) raises bleeding risk without reducing stroke (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS; AHA/ASA 2021 secondary prevention). The ESUS aspirin plan is superseded by the AF diagnosis.

extras.why: Referral to discuss rhythm control or ablation is reasonable.
A beta-blocker or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blocker for symptomatic rate control is reasonable.
Continuing atorvastatin after ischemic stroke is appropriate.
Sleep apnea screening or a lipid recheck on high-intensity statin is reasonable.
