tasks.title: Refractory Urinary Retention: Urodynamic Interpretation and Management
tasks.subject: Pressure-flow urodynamic study completed
tasks.request: Pressure-flow study completed today for your patient with refractory urinary retention and an indwelling catheter. The raw study values are in the chart for your interpretation and management plan.
facts: Two failed trials on combination medical therapy

required.why: Refractory retention: two failed trials without catheter despite tamsulosin and finasteride, prostate 64 mL. The seated pressure-flow study gives Qmax 6 mL/s and PdetQmax 94 cmH2O: bladder outlet obstruction index BOOI = PdetQmax - 2 x Qmax = 94 - 12 = 82 (obstructed above 40); bladder contractility index BCI = PdetQmax + 5 x Qmax = 94 + 30 = 124 (normal 100-150). High-pressure, low-flow obstruction with preserved contractility: a bladder outlet procedure is indicated for retention refractory to medical therapy (AUA BPH guideline 2021/2023, EAU 2023). For 64 mL, TURP, holmium or thulium enucleation, photoselective vaporization, aquablation or simple prostatectomy are appropriate. The May 7 'no detrusor contraction recorded' came from an incomplete supine study in which he could not void with catheters in place; it does not mean an acontractile bladder.

forbidden.why: Parasympathomimetics do not restore voiding in retention (no efficacy evidence; EAU 2023, AUA) and cause cholinergic adverse effects; tempted by the incomplete May 7 study that recorded no detrusor contraction.
Antimuscarinics worsen retention; there is no detrusor overactivity.

extras.why: Preoperative cystoscopy to assess the median lobe and urethra is reasonable.
Intermittent catheterization as a bridge to surgery is reasonable.
Preoperative urine culture is standard.
Upper-tract imaging in chronic retention is reasonable.

tasks.title: Refractory Urinary Retention: Urodynamic Interpretation and Management
tasks.subject: Pressure-flow urodynamic study completed
tasks.request: Pressure-flow study completed today for your patient with refractory urinary retention and an indwelling catheter. The raw study values are in the chart for your interpretation and management plan.
facts: Weak contraction with straining and interrupted flow
Good dexterity and willing to self-catheterize
Two failed trials on combination medical therapy
Perineal sensation and anal tone normal

required.why: Refractory retention: two failed trials without catheter despite tamsulosin and finasteride, prostate 64 mL. The seated pressure-flow study gives Qmax 3 mL/s and PdetQmax 22 cmH2O: BOOI = PdetQmax - 2 x Qmax = 22 - 6 = 16 (unobstructed, below 20); BCI = PdetQmax + 5 x Qmax = 22 + 15 = 37 (weak, below 100), with straining and interrupted flow. Retention is due to detrusor underactivity, not outlet obstruction, so an outlet procedure is unlikely to restore voiding. Clean intermittent self-catheterization is preferred over a chronic indwelling catheter for chronic retention from detrusor underactivity (EAU 2023; AUA/SUFU chronic retention guidance), and he has the dexterity, cognition and willingness to do it. Diabetes (A1c 5.4), B12 deficiency (512) and neurological signs have been excluded. The January 'presumed' prostatic obstruction is superseded by the pressure-flow study.

forbidden.why: BOOI 16 (unobstructed) with BCI 37 (weak detrusor): relieving a non-existent obstruction will not restore voiding and exposes him to surgical risk; outlet surgery is not indicated for retention from detrusor underactivity without obstruction (EAU 2023). This is the consequence of acting on the superseded January presumption of prostatic obstruction.

Parasympathomimetics do not restore voiding in retention (no efficacy evidence; EAU 2023, AUA) and cause cholinergic adverse effects; tempted by the incomplete May 7 study that recorded no detrusor contraction.
Antimuscarinics worsen retention; there is no detrusor overactivity.

extras.why: A urine culture before switching catheter strategy is reasonable.
Upper-tract imaging in chronic retention is reasonable.
Evaluation for an occult neurological cause of detrusor underactivity is reasonable.
Cystoscopy to exclude a urethral cause is tolerated.

tasks.title: Fatty Liver Disease with Elevated Ferritin: Hepatology Evaluation
tasks.subject: High ferritin with fatty liver; genotype and MRI back
tasks.request: Patient with type 2 diabetes, fatty liver, raised liver enzymes and a high ferritin. The HFE genotype and the liver MRI have resulted. Please evaluate and place the appropriate orders.
facts: Liver R2* 210 s^-1 at 1.5 T with calibration LIC = 0.0254 x R2* + 0.202 (LIC about 5.5 mg/g, above 1.8)
Calibration and upper limit stated, LIC not reported
Hemoglobin 15.2 and good venous access permit phlebotomy

required.why: LIC = 0.0254 x R2* + 0.202 = 0.0254 x 210 + 0.202 = 5.33 + 0.20 = 5.54 mg Fe/g dry weight (about 99 umol/g), about 3.1 times the 1.8 mg/g upper limit: MRI-confirmed hepatic iron overload. Transferrin saturation = iron / TIBC = 142 / 268 = 53% (raised, above 45%); ferritin 1,040 ng/mL on a non-inflamed repeat (CRP 3.1). The H63D/H63D genotype does not by itself explain overload, but once hepatic iron overload is proven, iron depletion by therapeutic phlebotomy is indicated (EASL 2022 haemochromatosis CPG: venesection can be offered for confirmed overload in non-C282Y genotypes; ACG 2019). Hemoglobin 15.2 g/dL and good venous access permit about 500 mL every 1-2 weeks to a ferritin of about 50-100 ng/mL.

FIB-4 = age x AST / (platelets x sqrt(ALT)) = age x 46 / (196 x sqrt(58)) = age x 46 / 1492.7 = 1.60 at 52 to 1.79 at 58, between the 1.3 and 2.67 cut-offs (indeterminate; AASLD 2023 MASLD guidance). MASLD with type 2 diabetes, obesity and proven hepatic iron overload with ferritin above 1,000 ng/mL: stage fibrosis by liver stiffness measurement (transient elastography; MR elastography, shear-wave elastography or ELF acceptable).

forbidden.why: Chelation is reserved for iron overload when phlebotomy is impossible (anemia, cardiac disease, poor venous access). The ferritin of 2,860 ng/mL that would suggest severe overload was drawn during febrile influenza pneumonia with CRP 186 mg/L; the non-inflamed ferritin is 1,040, LIC is about 5.5 mg/g, hemoglobin is 15.2 and venous access is good.
Iron and vitamin C supplements increase iron absorption and are contraindicated with proven hepatic iron overload.

extras.why: Hepatitis A and B immunity testing and vaccination in chronic liver disease.
Repeating iron indices and an inflammatory marker is reasonable.
Lifestyle support for MASLD.
Intensifying diabetes therapy with an agent with liver or weight benefit (GLP-1 receptor agonist, tirzepatide, pioglitazone, SGLT2 inhibitor) is reasonable in MASLD with A1c 7.2%.
Liver biopsy (histological iron grading and fibrosis staging) is reasonable with proven overload, ferritin above 1,000 ng/mL and raised aminotransferases.
Rare non-HFE hemochromatosis gene testing or genetic counseling for proven overload unexplained by H63D homozygosity.

tasks.title: Chronic Cough Follow-up Visit
tasks.subject: Chest x-ray final report and breathing tests
tasks.request: He is roomed for his cough follow-up. The final chest x-ray report and the breathing tests from 5/21 are back. Please review, update his plan and his other chronic care, and arrange any follow-up.
facts: Lisinopril started 2024-01-08 with no cough that day
Cough onset about 2024-02-05, about 4 weeks after lisinopril
Normal spirometry, no bronchodilator response, low FeNO
LDL 141 mg/dL with diabetes, no statin
Declined lipid-lowering therapy in 2021, willing now

required.why: Dry cough began about 4 weeks after lisinopril was started (2024-01-08; no cough that day; cough since about 2024-02-05) and persisted despite antibiotics and benzonatate; spirometry and FeNO are normal and there are no upper-airway or reflux symptoms. ACE inhibitor cough is a class effect (bradykinin), so CHEST guidance is to stop the ACE inhibitor in any patient with chronic cough. He still needs renin-angiotensin blockade for albuminuric diabetic kidney disease (UACR 96 mg/g; KDIGO 2022: ACE inhibitor or ARB at the maximum tolerated dose), and ARBs do not cause bradykinin cough. Dose equivalent to lisinopril 20 mg: losartan 50-100 mg, valsartan 80-320 mg, irbesartan 150-300 mg, candesartan 8-32 mg, telmisartan 40-80 mg, olmesartan 20-40 mg or azilsartan 40-80 mg daily. Blood pressure is at goal (128/78), so amlodipine alone would drop kidney protection and is not sufficient.

Creatinine and potassium are rechecked 2-4 weeks after starting a new renin-angiotensin blocker (KDIGO 2022 diabetes in CKD; ADA Standards of Care section 11). Potassium is 4.6 mmol/L. Window accepted: days 7-28 (2024-06-10 to 2024-07-01); reference day 14.

Type 2 diabetes, age 56-66, LDL 141 mg/dL, with hypertension and albuminuria: statin therapy is indicated regardless of the risk estimate (ACC/AHA 2018 class I moderate intensity; ADA 2024: high intensity with additional risk factors). He declined in 2021 and today asks to follow the recommended plan. Moderate- or high-intensity doses accepted (atorvastatin 10-80, rosuvastatin 5-40, simvastatin 20-40, pravastatin 40-80, lovastatin 40-80, pitavastatin 2-4, fluvastatin 80 mg).
ACC/AHA 2018 (class I): a fasting or non-fasting lipid panel 4-12 weeks after starting a statin to assess adherence and LDL response. Window accepted: days 28-84; reference day 56.

forbidden.why: ACE inhibitor cough is a class effect; re-ordering lisinopril or any other ACE inhibitor continues the cause of the cough.
Aliskiren with an ARB is contraindicated in diabetes (FDA label; ALTITUDE).
No evidence of bacterial infection; a second antibiotic course for a chronic dry cough is not indicated.

extras.why: Albuminuria and glycemic monitoring are routine in diabetic kidney disease.
A return visit to confirm resolution of the cough (ACE inhibitor cough usually resolves within 1-4 weeks, sometimes up to 3 months) is reasonable.

tasks.title: COVID-19 in a Patient on B-cell Depleting Therapy: Same-day Visit
tasks.subject: Positive COVID-19 PCR: patient on rituximab
tasks.request: SARS-CoV-2 PCR positive this morning; symptoms started Saturday. He gets rituximab for RA and has heart disease with a defibrillator. Morning labs are back. He is waiting in room 4 for you to decide on treatment and review his other results.
facts: IgG 310 mg/dL on an outside report

required.why: Mild COVID-19, symptom onset 2024-06-01 (day 3), in a man at high risk of progression: age 64-70, B-cell depletion with rituximab, methotrexate and prednisone, coronary disease and cardiomyopathy. Treatment is indicated (NIH COVID-19 guidelines). Amiodarone is still listed as active, but electrophysiology discontinued it on 2023-06-26 after a successful ablation and there have been no fills since June 2023; nearly a year exceeds its long elimination, so it does not preclude nirmatrelvir-ritonavir. Accepted: nirmatrelvir 300 mg with ritonavir 100 mg twice daily for 5 days (eGFR 79: no renal adjustment; hold simvastatin during the course and for 5 days after), or remdesivir 200 mg IV on day 1 then 100 mg on days 2-3, or molnupiravir 800 mg twice daily for 5 days.

New neutropenia: absolute neutrophils 1.2 x10^3/uL today, 4.1 before the March rituximab course, with lymphopenia; late-onset neutropenia after rituximab or viral marrow suppression. It is mild and he is not febrile neutropenic, so no growth factor; repeat a blood count with differential in about a week (days 4-10; reference day 7, 2024-06-10) to confirm recovery or a fall below 0.5.

Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia after repeated rituximab: IgG 310 mg/dL (outside report, November 2023) with two pneumonia admissions in 2023 and now COVID-19. Low IgG with recurrent serious infections warrants referral to clinical immunology for assessment of immunoglobulin replacement (BSR 2019 rituximab guidance; AAAAI). Rheumatology should also reconsider the next rituximab course.

Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis: prednisone at least 5 mg daily since 2013, a new T12 compression fracture on the January 2024 radiograph (not present in 2021) and a femoral neck T-score of -2.2. A vertebral fracture on long-term glucocorticoids puts him at very high fracture risk, so pharmacologic treatment is indicated (ACR 2022 glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis guideline): an oral or intravenous bisphosphonate, denosumab, or teriparatide or abaloparatide. Romosozumab is not approved for men.

forbidden.why: Neutrophils 1.2 x10^3/uL without febrile neutropenia: a growth factor is not indicated.
NIH COVID-19 guidelines recommend against dexamethasone or other systemic glucocorticoids for outpatients who do not need supplemental oxygen.
No evidence of bacterial pneumonia (oxygen saturation 95%, no consolidation symptoms); antibacterials are not indicated for COVID-19.
Romosozumab is not approved for men and carries a boxed warning for myocardial infarction and stroke; he has coronary disease.

extras.why: Current immunoglobulin levels before the immunology visit are reasonable.
Bone and mineral laboratory tests before antiresorptive therapy are reasonable.
Calcium and vitamin D with osteoporosis treatment.
Symptomatic treatment for fever, aches or cough.
Home pulse oximetry or a follow-up visit for a high-risk outpatient with COVID-19.
Thyroid and liver tests in a patient with an amiodarone history.

tasks.title: Hospital Follow-up After Post-polypectomy Bleeding
tasks.subject: Post-discharge visit after lower GI bleeding
tasks.request: Discharged 5/22 after bleeding from a colon polyp resection site, treated with clips and 2 units of blood. She is booked with you on 6/3; please address her held antiplatelet medicine, her blood count and the follow-up plan for the colon findings.
facts: Long-term clopidogrel for secondary stroke prevention
No bleeding after clip hemostasis on 2024-05-20

required.why: She takes long-term single antiplatelet therapy for secondary prevention after an ischemic stroke (2021); clopidogrel has been held since 2024-05-09. The delayed post-polypectomy bleed was controlled with clips on 2024-05-20 with no bleeding since, so the antiplatelet agent should be restarted now (ASGE 2016 and ACG-CAG 2022: resume antiplatelet therapy for secondary prevention once hemostasis is achieved; prolonged interruption raises the stroke risk). Clopidogrel 75 mg daily, or aspirin 75-325 mg daily as an alternative single agent.

Iron deficiency anemia after acute blood loss: hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, MCV 82 fL, ferritin 8 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 6%; ferritin was 64 ng/mL in October 2023, before the bleed. tasks.subject: Pulsing sound in right ear: follow-up
tasks.request: She is here for follow-up of the pulsing sound in her right ear. An urgent care note from 5/10, her eye examination and her blood tests are in the chart, and her blood pressure is high again today. Please evaluate and place orders.
facts: Magnified pneumatic otoscopy: no retrotympanic mass
Blood pressure 156/96 today on amlodipine 5 mg

required.why: Unilateral, pulse-synchronous tinnitus for 4 months with a normal magnified pneumatic otoscopic examination (no retrotympanic mass), normal fundi (no papilledema), no anemia and normal thyroid function: a vascular cause (dural arteriovenous fistula, carotid or venous sinus abnormality, sigmoid sinus diverticulum) must be excluded. Imaging accepted per ACR appropriateness criteria for pulsatile tinnitus: CT angiography of the head and neck, MR angiography or venography, or CT of the temporal bone.

Unilateral pulsatile tinnitus needs a comprehensive audiogram with tympanometry (AAO-HNS tinnitus guideline 2014; ACR): it documents asymmetric or conductive hearing loss, which changes the imaging and the urgency.

Blood pressure 156/96 and 152/94 today, home 148-158/92-98 on amlodipine 5 mg: above the 130/80 goal (ACC/AHA 2017). Intensify with amlodipine 10 mg or add a second first-line class (ACE inhibitor, ARB or thiazide-type diuretic).
After an antihypertensive change, blood pressure is reassessed in about a month and monthly until controlled (ACC/AHA 2017). Window accepted: days 14-42; reference day 28.

forbidden.why: AAO-HNS tinnitus guideline 2014 recommends against antidepressants, anticonvulsants, anxiolytics and supplements for tinnitus; pulsatile tinnitus needs a cause, not symptomatic drugs.

extras.why: MRI of the brain with and without contrast with the vascular study is reasonable.
Carotid duplex as an adjunct.
Screening for primary aldosteronism is reasonable but not required.
High-output causes were checked recently; repeating them is harmless.

The primary care handheld otoscopy in March was not magnified. tasks.title: Sexual Dysfunction and Hormone Results Visit
tasks.subject: Repeat hormone test resulted
tasks.request: The repeat morning hormone test from 5/28 has resulted. He is booked for his results visit on 6/3 and wants to discuss treatment for the erection problem and early ejaculation; his blood pressure was high again at the last visit.
facts: Repeat drawn fasting in the morning, no illness
Prior PSA elevation explained by prostatitis
No plans to father more children

required.why: Erectile dysfunction for about a year with no nitrate use, good exercise tolerance (two flights of stairs without symptoms: low cardiac risk for sexual activity, Princeton consensus) and no interacting medicines: a PDE5 inhibitor is first-line (AUA 2018). With lifelong premature ejaculation and coexisting ED, the ED is treated first (AUA 2020; EAU). Any PDE5 inhibitor at a label dose.

Testosterone deficiency is confirmed: two early-morning fasting total testosterone values below 264 ng/dL (238 on 2024-05-14 and 226 on 2024-05-28, same assay) with symptoms (low libido, fewer morning erections, ED) and LH 3.6 (inappropriately normal: secondary). Prolactin, TSH and ferritin are normal and testosterone is above 150 ng/dL, so pituitary imaging is not needed (Endocrine Society 2018). He has no plans to father more children, hematocrit is 45.1% and the prior PSA elevation was due to prostatitis (1.8 ng/mL after treatment). Testosterone therapy is indicated (AUA 2018; Endocrine Society 2018); any formulation.
Before starting testosterone, PSA is measured in men over 40 to exclude prostate cancer (AUA 2018 clinical principle; Endocrine Society 2018 for ages 55-69). His last PSA was in November 2022.

ED is a marker of cardiovascular risk; men with ED should have cardiovascular risk factors assessed, including a lipid profile (AUA 2018). His last lipid panel was in March 2021 (LDL 146 mg/dL) and he now has hypertension: a lipid panel is due for the ASCVD risk estimate.

Hypertension above goal despite lifestyle measures since September 2023: 146/92 and 144/90 today, home average 145/91 (ACC/AHA 2017 stage 2). Start a first-line agent: ACE inhibitor, ARB, calcium channel blocker or thiazide-type diuretic. Beta-blockers are not first-line and can worsen erectile function.

Testosterone level and hematocrit are rechecked 3-6 months after starting therapy (Endocrine Society 2018; AUA 2018: hematocrit above 54% requires dose reduction or interruption). Window accepted: days 70-196; reference day 90.
After starting antihypertensive treatment, reassess blood pressure in about a month (ACC/AHA 2017). Window accepted: days 14-42; reference day 28.

forbidden.why: Nitrates are contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors (severe hypotension).

extras.why: Topical anesthetic or a daily or on-demand SSRI for lifelong premature ejaculation is reasonable (AUA 2020), although treating ED first is preferred.
Glycemic screening as part of the cardiovascular risk assessment.
Further hormone evaluation is reasonable.
A baseline ECG for new hypertension is reasonable.
Urology or sex therapy referral for premature ejaculation is reasonable.
The testosterone level is rechecked with the hematocrit (Endocrine Society 2018); as a separate order it is an acceptable extra.

tasks.title: Office-based Opioid Use Disorder Treatment Visit
tasks.subject: Request: office-based treatment for opioid use disorder
tasks.request: Patient with opioid use disorder who has been treated with monthly naltrexone injections asks to change to a daily office-based medication. Referred to your program; he is booked with you on 2024-06-03.
facts: Last HIV and hepatitis C tests in 2021

required.why: He missed the 2024-05-20 naltrexone injection, so his last dose was 2024-04-22 (42 days ago): no naltrexone blockade remains. He has used intravenous fentanyl since about 2024-05-21, last about 18 hours ago, and is in moderate withdrawal (COWS 14). Buprenorphine can be started today in the office (ASAM 2020; SAMHSA TIP 63): buprenorphine-naloxone 2/0.5-4/1 mg sublingual when COWS is 8-12 or more, repeated as needed up to 8-16 mg on day 1. Any transmucosal buprenorphine product and starting dose is accepted; extended-release injectable buprenorphine is not started before transmucosal doses are tolerated.

Everyone with opioid use disorder should have take-home naloxone (CDC 2022; SAMHSA; ASAM 2020). The risk is highest after a period of abstinence and around changes in treatment, and in anyone trying to overcome naltrexone. Nasal naloxone 4 mg or 8 mg, or intramuscular or injectable naloxone.
People who inject drugs need periodic hepatitis C testing (CDC 2020; USPSTF 2020); his last test was nonreactive in March 2021 and he has injected since. Antibody with reflex RNA.
People who inject drugs should be tested for HIV at least yearly (CDC); his last test was in March 2021.

After starting buprenorphine the patient is seen again within the first week to adjust the dose, check withdrawal and cravings and review the urine drug screen (ASAM 2020; SAMHSA TIP 63). Window accepted: days 1-7; reference day 3.

forbidden.why: He used fentanyl 18 hours ago: naltrexone now would precipitate severe withdrawal, and he has chosen to switch.
Extended-release injectable buprenorphine requires prior tolerance of transmucosal buprenorphine (Sublocade: at least 7 days).
Methadone for opioid use disorder can only be dispensed by an opioid treatment program, not prescribed from primary care.
Full agonist opioids are not treatment for opioid use disorder.
Benzodiazepines add respiratory depression risk with opioids.

extras.why: Repeat urine drug testing is routine in office-based treatment.
Hepatitis serologies at program entry are reasonable.
Sexually transmitted infection screening is reasonable.
HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis is indicated for people who inject drugs once HIV is excluded.
Symptom medicines for withdrawal are reasonable.
Baseline liver tests are reasonable.

tasks.subject: Abdominal ultrasound and addendum finalized
tasks.request: The abdominal ultrasound from 5/28 and its addendum are final. The report describes a liver finding and a gallbladder finding that need follow-up planning. The patient is booked for a results visit on 6/3.
facts: Mother died of liver cancer at 58
Gallbladder polyp 16 x 11 mm, sessile, confirmed

required.why: Chronic hepatitis B (HBsAg reactive and confirmed, anti-HBc reactive, on the scanned 2019 blood donation letter, never evaluated) places her in the population at risk for hepatocellular carcinoma even without cirrhosis, so the LI-RADS approach applies: a solid lesion of 1 cm or more on ultrasound is characterized with multiphase contrast-enhanced MRI or CT (AASLD 2023 HCC guidance; ACR LI-RADS). Contrast-enhanced ultrasound is also accepted.

Untreated chronic hepatitis B with ALT 64 U/L (about 2.5 times the AASLD upper limit of 25 U/L for women): quantitative HBV DNA (with HBeAg status) decides whether antiviral treatment is indicated (AASLD 2018 hepatitis B guidance). Treatment is not started before it is known.

Newly recognized chronic hepatitis B with raised ALT, a family history of hepatocellular carcinoma and an indeterminate liver lesion: refer to hepatology for treatment decisions and lesion management.

HBsAg-positive with a first-degree relative with liver cancer: hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance with ultrasound (with or without AFP) every 6 months is indicated regardless of age or fibrosis (AASLD 2018 hepatitis B; AASLD 2023 HCC). After the lesion is characterized, the next surveillance ultrasound is due in 6 months. Window accepted: days 150-210; reference day 182.

The addendum confirms a 16 x 11 mm sessile gallbladder polyp. Polyps of 15 mm or more warrant surgical consultation (SRU 2022 consensus) and polyps of 10 mm or more cholecystectomy in fit patients (ESGAR/EAES 2022) because of the risk of gallbladder cancer.

forbidden.why: In an at-risk liver, a lesion is characterized with multiphase imaging first (LI-RADS); biopsy is reserved for indeterminate imaging.
Antiviral treatment for hepatitis B is decided on HBV DNA, HBeAg and ALT (AASLD 2018); starting it before HBV DNA is known is premature.

extras.why: HBeAg/anti-HBe and hepatitis delta antibody in newly recognized HBsAg positivity are recommended.
Coinfection and hepatitis A immunity testing in hepatitis B.
AFP with surveillance imaging or lesion workup.
Fibrosis staging is part of the hepatitis B evaluation.
Hepatitis A vaccination if not immune.
Baseline liver function testing.

tasks.title: Dermatology E-consult: Generalized Blistering Eruption
tasks.subject: Generalized blistering rash in a 78-year-old man
tasks.request: Itching for about 3 months and tense blisters for about a month, not better with triamcinolone cream or cephalexin. Photos are in the chart. Please advise on the diagnosis, the testing needed and treatment; you may place orders directly. He can come to your clinic for any procedure.
facts: Wife applies creams including to his back

required.why: Generalized bullous pemphigoid (about 15% of the body surface) that did not respond to mid-potency triamcinolone 0.1%. First-line treatment is a superpotent topical corticosteroid, clobetasol propionate 0.05% applied to the whole body except the face (Joly 2002 and 2009; BAD 2022; EADV 2022), which is as effective as oral prednisone and safer in the elderly. His wife has been applying his creams twice daily, including to his back, so whole-body application is feasible. Other superpotent agents (halobetasol, augmented betamethasone dipropionate) are accepted.

Clinically bullous pemphigoid: an elderly man with months of pruritic urticarial plaques followed by tense blisters, Nikolsky negative, mucosa spared, eosinophilia. Diagnosis is confirmed by a lesional biopsy for histology plus perilesional direct immunofluorescence (linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane) (BAD 2022; EADV 2022).
Serum BP180 and BP230 ELISA (or indirect immunofluorescence on salt-split skin) supports the diagnosis and BP180 levels guide follow-up (BAD 2022; EADV 2022).

Disease control is reassessed after 1-3 weeks of initial treatment, when topical treatment is tapered or systemic treatment is adjusted (Joly regimen; BAD 2022), and the biopsy and serology results are reviewed. Window accepted: days 10-28; reference day 14.

forbidden.why: Sitagliptin started 7 months before the eruption: DPP-4 inhibitors are associated with bullous pemphigoid and should be stopped; no DPP-4 inhibitor should be re-ordered or substituted.
The erosions are not infected (no improvement with cephalexin, no fever); repeating antibiotics treats the wrong diagnosis.

extras.why: Emollients for skin care.
An antihistamine for itch is reasonable as an adjunct.
Baseline laboratory tests.
Local wound care for eroded blisters.
Nicotinamide is sometimes added as an adjunct.

required.why: Collagenous colitis. Budesonide is normally first-line, but on 2024-04-15 the HIV clinic changed her regimen to darunavir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (the medication list still shows bictegravir). Cobicistat is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor: with budesonide it causes Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression, and the combination is not recommended (Symtuza label; DHHS). Switching the antiretroviral regimen is not an option (integrase resistance). For patients who cannot take budesonide, AGA 2016 suggests bismuth subsalicylate (for example 3 x 262 mg three times daily) or mesalamine.

Hypokalemia from diarrheal losses: potassium 3.1 mmol/L (3.9 in April) with leg cramps and ongoing diarrhea 6 times a day; magnesium is normal. Oral potassium replacement (for example potassium chloride 20-40 mEq daily) until the diarrhea is controlled.
Recheck potassium (with creatinine and bicarbonate) about a week after starting replacement while diarrhea continues. Window accepted: days 3-14; reference day 7.

Celiac serology (tissue transglutaminase IgA with total IgA) is recommended in chronic watery diarrhea (AGA 2019) and celiac disease is associated with microscopic colitis; it was not sent with the stool studies and no duodenal biopsies were taken.

forbidden.why: Budesonide with cobicistat-boosted darunavir causes iatrogenic Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression (Symtuza and budesonide labels).
All infectious studies are negative and the biopsies show collagenous colitis; antibiotics are not indicated.
Lansoprazole is the drug most strongly associated with microscopic colitis and her dyspepsia has resolved; no proton pump inhibitor should be re-ordered.

extras.why: Loperamide for symptom control is reasonable as an adjunct.
Total IgA with tissue transglutaminase IgA.
Magnesium and thyroid testing in chronic diarrhea with hypokalemia.
An H2 blocker if dyspepsia recurs after the proton pump inhibitor is stopped.
HIV monitoring is coordinated with the HIV clinic.
Gastroenterology follow-up for collagenous colitis.
